# MP-365: full content

MP-365 (Modern Partners 365) is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that helps mid-size and enterprise companies get more out of Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365 and Copilot.

## Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 Consulting That Gets Used
URL: https://mp-365.com/

MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that delivers Dynamics 365 consulting for mid-size and enterprise teams. The work covers Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365 and Copilot, and the goal is faster decisions, cleaner data and less manual work.

### Dynamics 365 consulting services across eight areas
- Dynamics 365 CRM Consultation: Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service and Customer Insights, plus integrations that connect the CRM to ERP and other systems.
- SharePoint & Intranets: intranets, SharePoint Server upgrades, file share moves and portals for suppliers and partners.
- Microsoft Copilot & AI: Copilot readiness, rollout and custom Copilot agents built with Microsoft tools.
- Power Platform: Power Apps, Power Pages, Power Automate and Power BI built on the Microsoft data you already have.
- Microsoft 365 Migration: Exchange and OneDrive moves into Microsoft 365.
- M&A Tenant Migration: tenant to tenant migration for mergers, acquisitions and divestitures.
- Data Governance: permission models, Microsoft Purview and CRM data quality.
- Application Modernization & DevOps: moving legacy applications to Azure and automating releases for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

### Why teams choose MP-365 for Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365
- A small, senior team. You work with specialists who do the work, not layers of management and slow processes.
- Fast starts. MP-365 jumps into the problem first. Carlisle Construction had its Dynamics and SharePoint operations stabilized within a week, with no long discovery phase.
- Hands-on delivery. The team builds a working first version early, then refines it with your users instead of writing long planning documents.
- A Microsoft focus. MP-365 (Modern Partners 365) works on Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, Power Platform and Copilot. About MP-365 explains the company and its partner status.
- Your time comes first. The aim is that your people spend their time on the business, not on the system.

### Proof: Dynamics 365 client results
- OTIS Elevator: MP-365 provides platform and operations leadership for Dynamics. Deployments dropped from 13 hours to 4, and manual errors fell to near zero.
- Carlisle Construction: Dynamics and SharePoint operations were stabilized within a week.
- Hunter Panels: Dynamics CRM support aligned the platform with how the business works, cut manual work and improved performance.
- More detail: the client results and case studies page lists every client, including federal and state government work.

### How MP-365 runs a project in four steps
1. Understand the problem: MP-365 learns how your team works today and what is going wrong.
2. Build a quick first version: The team delivers a working minimum viable product early, so you see real progress.
3. Validate and refine: Your users test it, and MP-365 adjusts it until it fits how they work.
4. Deploy and hand off: MP-365 releases the solution, trains your people and hands it over with clear documentation.

### Industries MP-365 serves
MP-365 serves mid-size and enterprise organizations in construction, manufacturing, healthcare, elevator and facilities services, and federal and state government. The same Microsoft skills carry across all of them: a clean CRM, organized files, reliable automation and reports people trust.

### Next step: book a Dynamics 365 discovery call
A discovery call is a short conversation about one problem. Tell MP-365 what is slowing your team down, and you get a plain answer on whether and how it can help. Contact MP-365 to set one up.
If cost is your first question, see how Dynamics 365 implementation cost is worked out. To see the full range of work, browse the Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 services overview.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What does a Dynamics 365 consulting partner do?
A: A Dynamics 365 consulting partner designs, configures, integrates and supports Dynamics 365 so it fits how your teams work. MP-365 focuses on Sales and Customer Service, connects the CRM to ERP and other systems, and adds Power Platform automation and reporting around it.
Q: How do I choose a Dynamics 365 consulting company?
A: Choose a company that shows relevant client results, puts senior people on your work and explains what it will not do. Ask who does the work, what is excluded and how hand-off works. MP-365 publishes its client results so you can check them.
Q: How long does a Dynamics 365 project take?
A: The length depends on scope: the number of users, systems to connect, data to migrate and how much your team can help. MP-365 builds a working first version early, then refines it. The schedule is agreed during scoping, not guessed on a first call.
Q: Who does MP-365 work with?
A: MP-365 works with mid-size and enterprise organizations. Clients include construction, manufacturing, healthcare, elevator and facilities businesses, and federal and state government agencies. Typical contacts are sales, service and operations leaders, and IT leaders who must deliver a Microsoft project.
Q: What does MP-365 not do?
A: MP-365 does not implement ERP systems, resell Microsoft licenses, run help desks or managed IT services, or offer cybersecurity. It does not build custom software outside the Microsoft low-code tools. It does connect Dynamics 365 to ERP systems such as Business Central.
Q: Is MP-365 a Microsoft partner?
A: Yes. MP-365 (Modern Partners 365) is a Microsoft Solutions Partner. Its Microsoft partner directory profile and contact details appear on the About page, so you can confirm the listing directly with Microsoft.
Q: Can MP-365 help with Microsoft 365 and Copilot, not only Dynamics 365?
A: Yes. MP-365 also covers SharePoint, Microsoft 365 migration, data governance and Microsoft Copilot readiness and custom agents. Many projects combine them, for example cleaning up permissions before a Copilot rollout. The services overview groups every offering by area.
Q: Do I need a large budget to start working with MP-365?
A: No. MP-365 offers three engagement models: Ad hoc, Standard and Dedicated. Ad hoc has no minimum or retainer, so you pay only when you engage the team. The pricing page compares all three.
Q: What happens on a discovery call?
A: You describe the problem, the systems involved and what a good result looks like. MP-365 asks questions about users, data and deadlines, then tells you whether it is a fit and what the next step would be. You do not need to prepare documents.
Q: Can MP-365 take over an existing Dynamics 365 system?
A: Yes. MP-365 often supports and improves systems that already exist. For OTIS Elevator it provides platform and operations leadership for Dynamics, and for Hunter Panels it supports a CRM so the platform matches the business. Support work starts by understanding the setup, then fixing and confirming.

MP-365 gives mid-size and enterprise teams Dynamics 365 consulting from a small, senior group that starts fast and stays hands-on. Pick the area that matches your problem, or tell the team what is going wrong and let them point you to the right starting place. To start from a business problem or your sector, see Microsoft solutions or solutions by industry.

## Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 Consulting Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/

Microsoft 365 consulting from MP-365 covers eight service areas, from Dynamics 365 CRM and SharePoint to Copilot, Power Platform, migration and data governance. Find your situation below, and the table points you to the right page.

### Microsoft 365 consulting and Dynamics 365 services by area
MP-365 groups its 28 services under eight categories. Each category page explains the area and compares its services. Each service page covers one piece of work in detail: what it includes, how it starts and what it leaves out.
Microsoft 365 was formerly called Office 365. MP-365 uses the current name throughout.

Hundreds of thousands of files sit on network file shares | File Share to SharePoint Migration | Files land in organized libraries with metadata and version control.
Our intranet is out of date and hard to update | SharePoint Intranet Development | A new structure makes content faster to publish and easier to find.
We want Copilot but worry what it can see | Microsoft 365 Copilot Readiness | Data and permissions get fixed before the rollout.
Approvals and notifications still run on email | Power Automate Workflow Automation | Flows handle the repetitive steps for you.
Monthly reports take days to assemble | Power BI Consulting & Dashboards | Live dashboards replace manual compilation.
Customers or partners need to sign in and work with our data | Power Pages Portal Development | A portal gives outside users controlled access to business data.
Our mail is still on Exchange servers | Exchange to Microsoft 365 Migration | Mailboxes move to Exchange Online in a planned cutover.
A merger or divestiture means combining or splitting tenants | Cross-Tenant Mailbox, Teams & File Migration | Mail, Teams and files move to the right tenant.
Releases to Dynamics 365 keep breaking things | DevOps & Release Automation | Pipelines and testing make each release repeatable.

### How Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 work together
Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 share the same Microsoft identities, files and data connections. Dynamics 365 holds customer, sales and service records. Microsoft 365 holds mail, Teams chats, documents and SharePoint sites.
Many MP-365 projects touch both. A Dynamics 365 Sales rollout may link to SharePoint document libraries. A Copilot rollout depends on clean Microsoft 365 permissions. That is why the services above sit side by side.

### What MP-365 does not offer
- ERP implementation. MP-365 connects Dynamics 365 to ERP systems such as Business Central. It does not implement them.
- Licenses. MP-365 does not resell Microsoft licenses. Those fees are paid to Microsoft or your license provider. See pricing for how MP-365 fees work.
- Managed IT. MP-365 does not run help desks or outsourced IT support.
- Cybersecurity. The access audits cover Dynamics 365 roles and Microsoft 365 permissions, not security operations.
- Custom software. Power Apps and Power Pages are low-code tools. MP-365 does not run a general software or web design agency.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What Microsoft 365 consulting services do mid-size companies need?
A: Most mid-size companies start with one pain: scattered customer data, an outdated intranet, a mail migration or unclear permissions. MP-365 groups its services into eight areas so you can start where the pain is, then add others later.
Q: How do Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 work together?
A: Dynamics 365 manages customer, sales and service records, while Microsoft 365 handles mail, Teams, files and SharePoint. They share sign-in and data connections, so a sales record can link to a SharePoint folder or a Teams conversation. MP-365 configures both sides.
Q: Which Microsoft service should a company start with?
A: Start with the area that hurts most. Scattered sales data points to Dynamics 365 Sales, messy files to SharePoint, and a planned Copilot rollout to permissions work first. The situation table on this page maps common problems to a starting service.
Q: Does MP-365 offer Office 365 consulting?
A: Yes. Office 365 is now Microsoft 365, and MP-365 covers it through SharePoint, migration, Copilot and data governance work. If you are searching for an Office 365 consultant, the migration and SharePoint categories are the closest match.
Q: Can I hire MP-365 for a single small task?
A: Yes. The Ad hoc engagement model has no commitment, minimum or retainer, so you pay only when you engage the team. A single fix, an audit or a short build all fit. The pricing page compares the three models.
Q: Does MP-365 implement ERP systems?
A: No. MP-365 integrates Dynamics 365 with ERP systems such as Business Central so data flows without double entry. It does not implement, configure or consult on the ERP itself. The integration services page describes exactly what is covered.
Q: Does MP-365 resell Microsoft licenses?
A: No. MP-365 does not resell licenses or manage Microsoft subscriptions. You pay license fees to Microsoft or your license provider, and MP-365 fees are separate. MP-365 can tell you what a project needs, but you buy licenses elsewhere.
Q: Do I need Dynamics 365 to use MP-365 for SharePoint or migration?
A: No. SharePoint, Microsoft 365 migration, tenant migration and data governance work stand alone. Many clients use a single area. Others combine areas, for example a SharePoint upgrade followed by a CRM project.
Q: Can MP-365 take over a project another partner started?
A: Yes. MP-365 often steps into existing systems. The work starts by understanding what was built, then fixing and confirming what matters most. Its client results include platform stabilization and ongoing support for existing Dynamics environments.
Q: How do I start with a service?
A: Pick the closest page and read its At a glance block, then contact MP-365 with your problem. A discovery call confirms whether the service fits and what the first step is. If you are unsure which service you need, describe the situation and MP-365 will point you to one.

Microsoft 365 consulting from MP-365 spans eight areas, and each one has detailed pages for the work you may need. Use the situation table to pick a starting point, or describe your problem and let the team recommend one. To start from a business problem or your sector instead, see Microsoft solutions or solutions by industry.

## Dynamics 365 Implementation Cost and Pricing
URL: https://mp-365.com/pricing/

Dynamics 365 implementation cost depends on scope, not on a fixed price list. MP-365 prices work through three engagement models, Ad hoc, Standard and Dedicated, and agrees the figure for each project after scoping.

### MP-365 engagement models, as of November 2026
Model | Best for | How it is billed | Minimum commitment | Response time | What is included
Ad hoc | One-off needs: call MP-365 when something comes up | Pay only when engaged | None. No retainer. | Agreed during scoping | Specialist help on the problem in front of you, with no ongoing obligation.
Standard | Small projects and pre-defined pains. The recommended starting point. | A flat rate, whatever the volume of work | No forced minimum, and no penalty for quiet months | Agreed during scoping | MP-365 works as an extension of your team. You scale the work up or down as needs change.
Dedicated | Teams that need MP-365 consistently, like a Dynamics specialist embedded in the operation | Agreed during scoping | Agreed during scoping | Agreed during scoping | Priority access and availability, with a specialist who knows your environment.

### How MP-365 prices a Dynamics 365 project
MP-365 does not publish prices, because two Dynamics 365 projects with the same product can differ widely in effort. A ten-user sales pipeline and a multi-system rollout are different jobs. Cost follows the drivers in the next table, and the services overview shows what each area of work covers.
The tables on this page show how MP-365 engages and bills. They contain no price figures. The exact amount for your work is agreed in writing after scoping.

### What drives Dynamics 365 implementation cost, as of November 2026
Cost driver | Why it matters | The question MP-365 asks
Number of users | More users mean more roles, more training and more testing. | How many people will use the system, and in which roles?
Systems to integrate | Every connection to an ERP, marketing tool or database adds design and testing. | Which systems must exchange data with Dynamics 365, and in which direction?
Data to migrate | Volume and cleanliness decide how much mapping and cleanup is needed. | Where does the data live today, and how clean is it?
Customization | Standard setup is faster than custom forms, automation and reports. | Which processes are unique to your business, and which can follow standard behavior?
Number of environments | Test, staging and production environments each need setup and release steps. | Do you need separate environments for testing and training?
Timeline | A tight deadline can mean more people working in parallel. | Is there a fixed date, such as a contract end or a fiscal year start?
How much your team can help | Fast answers and available testers shorten the work. | Who on your side can make decisions, test and sign off?

### How MP-365 produces a Dynamics 365 cost estimate
1. Hold a discovery call: Contact MP-365 and describe the problem, the systems involved and the result you want.
2. Scope the work: MP-365 asks about users, data, integrations and environments, the drivers in the table above.
3. Receive a written estimate: You get the scope, the engagement model and the cost in writing.
4. Agree the terms: You confirm the scope, what is excluded and how changes are handled.
5. Kick off the project: MP-365 starts with a working first version and refines it with your users.

### How to compare Dynamics 365 consulting bids
- Who does the work. Ask who will build your solution, and whether senior people or subcontractors do the work.
- What is excluded. Compare scope line by line. A low bid often leaves out data migration, testing or training.
- How changes are handled. Ask how a change request is priced and approved before the project starts.
- What the hand-off includes. Look for documentation, training for your users and a defined support period.
- How success is measured. Agree on a result you can check, such as hours saved, errors removed or reports produced automatically.

### Microsoft licenses are priced separately
Microsoft sets Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 license prices, and you pay them to Microsoft or your license provider. MP-365 does not resell licenses, so license fees never appear in an MP-365 estimate. Check Microsoft's current price list for those figures.

### Estimate your project complexity
The short estimator below helps you size a Dynamics 365 or Microsoft 365 project. It asks about the service area, users, systems to connect, data and timeline. It then suggests an engagement model and a complexity tier, and lists the cost drivers that apply to your answers. Results are guidance, not a quote, and you do not need to enter an email address.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How much does Dynamics 365 implementation cost?
A: It depends on the number of users, the systems to connect, the data to migrate, customization and your timeline. MP-365 does not publish a price list. It scopes the work first, then provides a written estimate. The tables above show each cost driver.
Q: How is Dynamics 365 consulting priced?
A: MP-365 prices through three engagement models. Ad hoc means you pay only when engaged. Standard uses a flat rate whatever the volume. Dedicated gives you priority access to an embedded specialist. Specific rates are agreed during scoping.
Q: What affects the cost of a Dynamics 365 project?
A: Seven things move cost most: number of users, systems to integrate, data to migrate, customization, number of environments, timeline and how much your team can help. Each is explained in the cost drivers table, with the question MP-365 asks about it.
Q: Is there a minimum commitment?
A: No forced minimum applies to the Ad hoc and Standard models. Ad hoc has no retainer, and Standard has no penalty for quiet months. Dedicated terms, including any minimum, are agreed during scoping because the model reserves priority availability for you.
Q: Does the cost include Microsoft licenses?
A: No. Microsoft sets license prices, and you pay them to Microsoft or your license provider. MP-365 does not resell licenses, so its estimates cover consulting and implementation work only. Budget for both, and ask Microsoft for current license pricing.
Q: Which engagement model should I choose?
A: Choose Standard for a small project or a known pain, since it is the recommended option. Choose Ad hoc for occasional help with no commitment. Choose Dedicated if you need MP-365 consistently, like an embedded Dynamics specialist. The estimator suggests one based on your answers.
Q: What does the Dynamics 365 cost estimator do?
A: The estimator asks about your project and returns a suggested engagement model, a complexity tier of light, standard or complex, and the cost drivers that apply. It is guidance, not a quote. You can send the answers with your message to MP-365.
Q: How do I get an accurate quote?
A: Book a free consultation and describe the problem. MP-365 then scopes the work with you, covering users, integrations, data and environments, and sends a written estimate. A precise figure is only possible after that scoping step.
Q: Why is one bid much cheaper than another?
A: Differences usually come from scope. A cheaper bid may exclude data migration, testing, training or hand-off, or use less senior staff. Compare who does the work, what is excluded, how changes are handled and how success is measured before you judge on price.
Q: Can I start small and expand later?
A: Yes. Start with a single problem under the Ad hoc or Standard model, then scale the work up or down as needs change. Standard has no forced minimum and no penalty for quiet months. See the client results for how engagements have run.

Dynamics 365 implementation cost becomes clear once the scope is clear. Use the cost drivers and the estimator to prepare, then talk to MP-365 about your project so it can scope the work and send a written estimate.

### Problems MP-365 has solved, and the results
The stories below are anonymous examples. Each one follows the same pattern: the problem, what MP-365 built, and the result. Each links to the service page that describes the work in detail.

### SharePoint upgrade from old versions to Microsoft 365
Problem: the organization ran an older SharePoint version (2007, 2010, 2013 or 2016) and needed to reach Microsoft 365.
What MP-365 built and the result: a staged SharePoint Server upgrade and migration to Microsoft 365. The upgrade ran in stages.

### File shares with hundreds of thousands of files
Problem: network file shares held hundreds of thousands of files that needed structure.
What MP-365 built and the result: a file share to SharePoint migration into organized libraries with metadata, version control and workflows.

### A modern intranet for a manufacturer
Problem: the intranet needed a clearer structure, a simpler security model and faster content updates.
What MP-365 built and the result: a modern SharePoint intranet with a clear information architecture, a simpler security model and faster content updates.

### A financial advisory system moved from spreadsheets
Problem: a financial advisory team tracked its work in spreadsheets.
What MP-365 built and the result: a system in SharePoint Online with version control, metadata and automated calculations. See the SharePoint and intranet services for the full range.

### Sales tracking with live dashboards for leadership
Problem: sales reports took several business days each month to compile.
What MP-365 built and the result: one sales process in Dynamics 365 Sales with live dashboards for leadership.

### Lead tracking for marketing and sales leaders
Problem: marketing and sales leaders spent business days each month on lead reports.
What MP-365 built and the result: one lead process with dashboards for both teams, using lead management and attribution in Dynamics 365.

### Case tracking that replaced email-based support
Problem: support requests lived in email, so nobody could see who owned a request or how urgent it was.
What MP-365 built and the result: one case system in Dynamics 365 Customer Service that shows the owner, status and urgency of every case.

### Contract management with stages and reminders
Problem: legal and finance needed contracts to move through defined stages with clear owners.
What MP-365 built and the result: defined stages, owners, reminders and dashboards for legal and finance, with workflow automation handling the repetitive steps.

### CRM deployments that ship on a reliable schedule
Problem: CRM changes needed automatic deployment, a reliable quality assurance cycle and a record of what changed.
What MP-365 built and the result: automatic deployment, a reliable quality assurance cycle, release notes and a trackable backlog, delivered through DevOps and release automation.

### CRM access control with an approval process
Problem: CRM access needed an approval process and documented access levels.
What MP-365 built and the result: an approval process, documented access levels and automatic access reports, through a Dynamics 365 security roles and access audit.

### Reliable integrations with ERP and marketing systems
Problem: the CRM needed reliable connections to ERP and marketing systems.
What MP-365 built and the result: integrations with logging and alerts, service accounts instead of personal accounts and secure password storage, delivered as Dynamics 365 integration services.

## About MP-365 (Modern Partners 365)
URL: https://mp-365.com/about/

MP-365 (Modern Partners 365) is a Microsoft Solutions Partner for Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365 and Copilot. The MP-365 Microsoft partner team is small, senior and hands-on, and it works with mid-size and enterprise organizations.

### Who MP-365 is
MP-365 is a focused team of Microsoft specialists based in Vernon, Connecticut. It specializes in Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service, integrations that connect the CRM to ERP systems, Power Platform, SharePoint automation and Copilot.
The company is not a large consulting firm with layers of management and slow-moving processes. The team's goal is simple: your people spend their time on the business, not on the system.

### What an MP-365 Microsoft partner relationship looks like

## Dynamics 365 CRM Consulting for Mid-Size Teams
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/

Dynamics 365 CRM consulting from MP-365 (Modern Partners 365) covers six areas: Sales, Customer Service, Customer Insights, lead management, access audits and integrations. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that helps mid-size and enterprise teams in the United States set up, fix and run Dynamics 365.

### What Dynamics 365 CRM consulting includes
Service | Best for | What you get
Dynamics 365 Sales | Sales teams that track deals in spreadsheets or in a CRM nobody trusts | One pipeline, a sales process that matches how reps work, and forecasts leaders can rely on
Dynamics 365 Customer Service | Support teams that work from shared inboxes | Cases with an owner, a status and an urgency, plus queues, service level agreements and knowledge articles
Dynamics 365 Customer Insights | Marketing teams that send campaigns but cannot see what happens next | Segments, forms and journeys in Customer Insights - Journeys, connected to Sales
Lead Management and Attribution | Teams whose leads arrive from several sources and get lost | One lead process: capture, score, route and report by source
Security Roles and Access Audit | Organizations whose Dynamics 365 users have collected too much access over time | Reviewed roles, documented access levels and a repeatable access report
Dynamics 365 Integration Services | Teams that re-key data between the CRM and ERP, marketing or file systems | Integrations with logging, alerts and no double entry

### Which Dynamics 365 CRM service should you start with?
Start with the problem that costs you the most time today. If reps cannot say what will close this quarter, start with Sales. If customers chase answers by email, start with Customer Service. If two systems hold different numbers for the same customer, start with Integration Services.
Lead Management, Customer Insights and the access audit usually follow one of those. Most clients begin with a single area, prove it works, then add the next. That keeps the first release small and the risk low.

### When to hire a Dynamics 365 consulting partner
- Adoption has stalled: reps and agents keep their real notes in Excel, Outlook or a notebook, so the CRM data is out of date.
- Reports take days: someone builds the monthly sales or service report by hand because the system cannot produce it.
- The system has outgrown its builder: the person who configured Dynamics 365 left, and nobody knows why a workflow or plug-in exists.
- Releases break things: changes go straight to production, and users find the bugs.
- Data is re-keyed: staff copy orders, invoices or contacts between the CRM and another system.
- Access has sprawled: more users than expected hold the System Administrator role.

### How MP-365 approaches Dynamics 365 CRM projects
1. Understand the business problem: Talk to the people who use the system and the leaders who rely on its numbers. Write down the one problem to solve first.
2. Review what exists: Inspect the current Dynamics 365 environment: apps, security roles, workflows, plug-ins, integrations and data quality.
3. Agree a small first release: Define the minimum viable product (MVP) that proves the fix, and a roadmap for what follows.
4. Build in a test environment: Make changes in a sandbox, never in production, and keep a backlog that you can see.
5. Validate with real users: Let the people who do the work try it, collect their corrections and refine before go-live.
6. Deploy and hand off: Release with a go-live checklist, train the users and document what changed.
7. Support and improve: Stay on call for fixes and small changes, and review the results against the goals set in step one.

Factor | Support mode | Project mode
Use it when | Something is broken or slow and you need a specialist now | You are building something new or changing how a team works
How it runs | Understand the issue, jump in, fix and confirm, then brief you | Understand, build a quick MVP, validate and refine, then deploy and hand off
Your time | A short call to explain the problem and one to confirm the fix | Regular reviews with the users who will own the result

## Dynamics 365 Sales Consulting and Implementation
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/sales/

Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales is Microsoft's CRM app for tracking leads, opportunities and customers in one pipeline. MP-365 provides Dynamics 365 Sales consulting and implementation for mid-size and enterprise sales teams, built around the way your reps actually sell.

bestFor: Sales leaders at mid-size and enterprise companies who need one trusted pipeline, forecasts they can defend and less manual reporting.
includes: Sales process design, Dynamics 365 Sales configuration, forecasting, lead-to-opportunity flow, data import, Outlook and Teams setup, Power BI dashboards, user training and support.
notIncluded: ERP implementation, Microsoft license resale, custom software development and managed IT support.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your sales process, then a review of your current CRM and a plan for a small first release.

### What is Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales?
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales is a cloud CRM that runs on Microsoft Dataverse and is built as a Power Apps model-driven app. Sellers use it to manage accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities and quotes, and leaders use it to see the pipeline and forecast revenue.
Microsoft sells Dynamics 365 Sales in tiers. According to Microsoft Learn (2026), Sales Enterprise automates the process from lead to cash, Sales Premium adds AI features such as predictive scoring and relationship intelligence, and Sales Professional is a lighter app that includes a subset of the Enterprise tables. Which tier fits depends on your process, not your company size.

### Sales problems this work solves
- The pipeline lives in spreadsheets: each rep keeps a private version, so leadership cannot see the real number.
- Forecasts are guesses: stages mean different things to different reps, so the forecast moves every week.
- Reporting eats days: someone pulls data from several places each month to build the sales review.
- Reps enter data twice: once in the CRM and again in email, quotes or the ERP.
- Leads go cold: nobody owns a new lead for the first day, and follow-up depends on who noticed it.

### How MP-365 delivers a Dynamics 365 Sales implementation
1. Map the sales process: Sit with reps, managers and operations to write down how a deal moves from first contact to signed order, including where it stalls.
2. Audit what you have: Review the current CRM or spreadsheets, the data you want to keep and the systems that must connect.
3. Design the first release: Agree stages, required fields, ownership rules and the three reports leadership wants, and leave everything else for later.
4. Build a working MVP: Configure the app in a sandbox so reps can click through a real pipeline within the first sprints.
5. Import and clean the data: Load accounts, contacts and open deals, remove duplicates and standardize fields before users see them.
6. Validate with reps: Let a pilot group sell in the system, collect their corrections and refine the forms and views.
7. Deploy, train and hand off: Release with a go-live checklist, train each role and leave short guides your team can use.
8. Support and improve: Stay available for fixes and small changes, and review pipeline quality against the goals set at the start.

### Dynamics 365 Sales features MP-365 sets up
Feature | What it does | How MP-365 sets it up
Lead-to-opportunity process | Guides a seller through stages with a business process flow | Stages and required fields that match your real process, not the default template
Opportunity pipeline | Shows open deals by stage and owner | Views and a pipeline layout for each role, with stale-deal flags
Sales forecasting | Rolls up seller commitments and compares them with quota | A forecast hierarchy that mirrors your sales teams and the columns managers review
Sales accelerator and sequences | Gives sellers a work list and a set of next activities | Sequences for follow-up steps you already expect from reps
Predictive scoring | Scores leads and opportunities from past outcomes | Set up only when you have enough closed history to train a model
Outlook and Teams integration | Shows CRM records beside email and chat | Dynamics 365 App for Outlook and Teams for the roles that use them

### Microsoft products involved in a Dynamics 365 Sales project
A Dynamics 365 Sales project uses Dynamics 365 Sales, Microsoft Dataverse and Power Apps for the app and data. Power BI provides the dashboards, and Power Automate handles approvals, notifications and routine record updates. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint connect the CRM to daily work.
When your sellers use Copilot, MP-365 sets up Dynamics 365 Sales Agents on top of clean CRM data. Agents are only as good as the records they read, so the clean-up comes first.

### Proof: one sales process and live dashboards
A sales organization tracked deals in separate spreadsheets, and building the monthly sales report took several business days each month. MP-365 set up one sales process in Dynamics 365 with live dashboards for leadership.
Leaders now open a dashboard instead of waiting for a compiled report, and every rep works the same stages. See more delivery work on the clients page.

### How long does a Dynamics 365 Sales implementation take?
A Dynamics 365 Sales implementation takes as long as the scope you choose, and MP-365 keeps the first release small so reps use it early. Duration depends on the number of sales processes, the data to import, the integrations and how fast your team can review and approve.
The pricing page explains how MP-365 prices consulting. License fees are paid to Microsoft and are separate.

### When Dynamics 365 Sales is not the right fit
Dynamics 365 Sales is a poor fit if you have two or three sellers and a simple contact list, or if your main need is billing or order fulfillment. A spreadsheet or a lighter tool will cost less to run. If your problem is service rather than selling, look at Dynamics 365 Customer Service instead. If your pain is on the finance side, the fix is in your ERP, and MP-365 only connects the two.

## Dynamics 365 Customer Service Implementation
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/customer-service/

Dynamics 365 Customer Service gives support teams one place to track every customer issue as a case, with an owner, a status and a deadline. MP-365 handles the Dynamics 365 Customer Service implementation for mid-size and enterprise teams that run support from shared inboxes, spreadsheets or an outgrown help desk.

bestFor: Service and operations leaders whose customers wait on email replies, and whose agents cannot see who owns which issue.
includes: Case design, queues and routing, service level agreements, entitlements, knowledge articles, email and portal intake, dashboards, user training and support.
notIncluded: ERP implementation, outsourced help desk or managed IT support, Microsoft license resale and custom software development.
howItStarts: A discovery call about how requests reach you today, then a review of your inboxes, tools and current case data.

### What is Dynamics 365 Customer Service?
Dynamics 365 Customer Service is Microsoft's case management app for support teams. It turns each request into a case, records every interaction against it, and lets agents share answers from a knowledge base.
According to Microsoft Learn (2026), the app also covers unified routing, service level agreements (SLAs), entitlements, conversations across channels including voice, and collaboration in Microsoft Teams. Copilot Service workspace is the main app for service representatives. For new organizations with Enterprise licenses, it replaces the older Customer Service Hub.

### How case management works in Dynamics 365 Customer Service
1. A request arrives: A customer emails a monitored mailbox, calls, chats or submits a portal form.
2. The system creates a case: Rules create a case from the message and link it to the right customer account and contact.
3. The case is classified and routed: Routing rules set priority and send the case to a queue, or straight to an agent with the right skills.
4. An SLA timer starts: The SLA tracks the first response and the resolution deadline and warns the team before a deadline is missed.
5. An agent works the case: The agent sees the full history, searches knowledge articles and pulls in colleagues through Teams.
6. The case is resolved: The agent records the resolution and closes the case, and reports update the same day.

### Customer service problems this work solves
- Nobody owns the issue: three people reply to the same email, or none do.
- Status lives in someone's head: a manager asks for updates by chat because the system cannot show them.
- Urgent cases look like normal ones: a plant-down call sits behind a password reset.
- Answers get rewritten: each agent solves the same question from scratch because knowledge is not shared.
- Customers repeat themselves: a new agent has no history, so the customer explains the problem again.

### How MP-365 delivers a Dynamics 365 Customer Service implementation
1. Trace how requests arrive: List every channel customers use today, the mailboxes involved and who answers each one.
2. Define case types and priorities: Agree what counts as a case, the categories you report on and what makes a case urgent.
3. Design queues and routing: Decide which team gets which case and how work is assigned when someone is away.
4. Set up SLAs and entitlements: Translate your service promises into first-response and resolution timers, tied to customer terms where they apply.
5. Build the agent workspace: Configure Copilot Service workspace so agents see the case, history and knowledge in one view.
6. Load knowledge and past cases: Import the answers your team already uses and any case history worth keeping.
7. Pilot, refine and go live: Run one team in the system, fix what slows them down, then release to everyone with training.
8. Support and tune: Review SLA misses and reopened cases after launch and adjust routing and knowledge.

### Customer Service building blocks MP-365 configures
Building block | What it does | Decision MP-365 helps you make
Cases | Tracks one customer issue from request to resolution | Which fields agents must fill and which they can skip
Queues | Holds work for a team until someone picks it up | One queue per team, product or region
Unified routing | Classifies work and assigns it to the right queue or agent | Whether simple queues are enough, or skill-based assignment pays off
Service level agreements | Times first response and resolution against a target | Which targets you can honestly meet
Entitlements | Defines what support a customer is owed | Whether contract terms need to drive the SLA
Knowledge articles | Stores approved answers that agents and customers can search | Who writes, reviews and retires articles

### Microsoft products involved in a Customer Service project
Customer Service runs on Microsoft Dataverse and shares customer records with Dynamics 365 Sales, so account teams see open cases. Copilot Service workspace is the agent app, and Teams, Outlook and SharePoint support daily collaboration and documents.
Customers can log and follow their own cases through a portal built with Power Pages. Power Automate handles notifications and approvals, and Power BI reports on SLA performance. Microsoft also provides Copilot features in the workspace that help agents summarize cases and find information, and MP-365 turns them on once knowledge and case data are in good shape.

### Proof: replacing email-based support with one case system
A company handled customer issues through email threads. Nobody could see who owned a request, what state it was in or how urgent it was. MP-365 set up case tracking in Dynamics 365 so each issue shows its owner, status and urgency in one system.
Managers now filter by urgency instead of asking for updates. The clients page lists more MP-365 work.

### When Dynamics 365 Customer Service is not the right fit
Dynamics 365 Customer Service is not the right fit if one or two people answer a handful of emails a day, or if you want an outsourced help desk. MP-365 builds and supports the system, but it does not staff your support team or run an IT help desk. For internal IT tickets, a tool built for that purpose is usually simpler.

### Related Dynamics 365 CRM services
Service data gets more useful when it reaches other systems, so see Dynamics 365 Integration Services for connecting orders, assets or invoices to your cases. The full set of services sits under Dynamics 365 CRM consulting. For cost, read the pricing page.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Dynamics 365 Customer Service?
A: Dynamics 365 Customer Service is Microsoft's case management app for support teams. It tracks customer issues as cases, records every interaction, shares knowledge articles, routes work to the right team and times responses with service level agreements. It runs on Microsoft Dataverse and shares records with Dynamics 365 Sales.
Q: How does case management work in Dynamics 365 Customer Service?
A: A request becomes a case linked to the customer. Routing rules set priority and send it to a queue or an agent, an SLA timer tracks the deadline, and the agent resolves it using the case history and knowledge articles. Managers see status and urgency on dashboards without asking for updates.
Q: How long does a Customer Service implementation take?
A: It depends on the number of channels, case types, routing rules and SLAs, plus how quickly your team reviews decisions. MP-365 pilots with one team first, then expands. A discovery call that traces how requests arrive today lets MP-365 outline the stages for your situation.
Q: What is the difference between Customer Service and Sales?
A: Sales manages leads and deals before the purchase. Customer Service manages issues and questions after it. They share the same customer records, so an account manager sees open cases and an agent sees the account's deals. Many clients start with one and add the other later.
Q: What are SLAs and entitlements in Dynamics 365?
A: An SLA is a timer that tracks targets such as first response and resolution time. An entitlement defines what support a customer is owed, such as the channels or the number of cases. Entitlements can drive which SLA applies, so contract terms and deadlines stay in step.
Q: Do we need unified routing?
A: Not always. Simple queues are enough when a small team shares all work. Unified routing helps when cases need classification, skills or workload balancing across several teams. MP-365 starts with the simplest option that works and adds routing rules only when the volume justifies them.
Q: Can customers submit and track cases themselves?
A: Yes. A customer portal built with Power Pages lets signed-in customers log cases, add details and follow progress, using the same case data your agents see. This cuts status emails. MP-365 builds portals on existing Microsoft data.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 Customer Service create cases from email?
A: Yes. A monitored shared mailbox can create a case from each incoming message and link it to the matching customer. MP-365 sets rules for what becomes a case and what is ignored, such as auto-replies, so agents are not buried in noise.
Q: What is the Customer Service Hub, and should we still use it?
A: Customer Service Hub is the older single-session agent app. Microsoft Learn (2026) says it is not available for new organizations with Enterprise licenses, where Copilot Service workspace replaces it. MP-365 builds new implementations on Copilot Service workspace and helps existing users move over.
Q: Does Dynamics 365 Customer Service include Copilot?
A: Yes. Microsoft Learn (2026) lists Copilot features in Copilot Service workspace that help agents find information, summarize cases and conversations, and complete tasks. Availability depends on your licenses. MP-365 turns them on after knowledge articles and case data are tidy, since Copilot answers from that content.

A good Dynamics 365 Customer Service setup is simple: every issue has an owner, a status and a deadline. MP-365 builds that foundation first, then adds routing, knowledge and a portal as your team is ready.

## Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Marketing
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/customer-insights/

Microsoft Dynamics 365 Marketing is now called Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys, Microsoft's app for building customer segments and running email, text message and push journeys. MP-365 sets it up for mid-size and enterprise teams and connects it to Dynamics 365 Sales, so marketing and sales work from one customer record.

bestFor: Marketing and sales leaders who run campaigns but cannot see which contacts engaged, or which leads the campaign created.
includes: Customer Insights - Journeys setup, segments, forms, email and text templates, trigger-based journeys, lead handoff to Sales, reporting and user training.
notIncluded: Creative or copywriting for campaigns, ERP implementation, Microsoft license resale and managed marketing operations.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your current campaigns and tools, then a review of your contact data and what you already use in Dynamics 365.

### Is Microsoft Dynamics 365 Marketing the same as Customer Insights - Journeys?
Yes. Microsoft renamed Dynamics 365 Marketing as Customer Insights - Journeys in 2023, and people still search for the old name. The product now sits in the Dynamics 365 Customer Insights family, next to Customer Insights - Data, which unifies customer data from many sources.
One change matters if you used the older product. According to Microsoft Learn (2026), the outbound marketing module was removed in May 2026, and real-time journeys is the version that remains. Emails, forms, journeys and segments built in outbound marketing cannot be used in real-time journeys, so they need to be rebuilt.

### What Customer Insights - Journeys can do
- Segments: group contacts by attributes and behavior, and refresh the group as data changes.
- Trigger-based journeys: start a journey when a contact does something, such as submitting a form.
- Segment-based journeys: send a planned series of messages to a defined audience.
- Channels: email, text message and push notification, used alone or in the same journey.
- Forms and events: capture sign-ups on your website and manage event registrations.
- Customer Insights - Data link: use segments and profiles from Customer Insights - Data in journeys.

### Do you need Customer Insights if you already use Dynamics 365 Sales?
Question | Dynamics 365 Sales alone | Sales plus Customer Insights - Journeys
Who is it for? | Sellers and sales managers | Marketers who plan and send customer communication
How are campaigns run? | Campaigns and marketing lists inside the sales app | Segments and multi-step journeys across email, text and push
What triggers a message? | A person decides to send it | A contact action or a schedule
What do sales see? | Records sellers enter or import | Contact engagement shown on the same customer record
Best for | Occasional campaigns to small lists | Regular, targeted communication to larger audiences

### Customer Insights - Journeys and Sales share one customer record
The main value of Customer Insights - Journeys is not email. Both apps run on Microsoft Dataverse, so a contact who clicked a link or filled in a form is the same contact a seller sees in Dynamics 365 Sales.
That shared record removes the usual handoff problem, where marketing exports a list and sales never learns what happened to it. The rules for when a contact becomes a lead belong in your lead management process.

### Marketing problems this work solves
- Lists are exported by hand: someone downloads contacts to a spreadsheet and uploads them to another email tool.
- Marketing cannot see results in sales: campaigns get credit for clicks, not for pipeline.
- Messages ignore behavior: everyone on the list gets the same email regardless of what they did.
- Consent is scattered: opt-outs live in one tool, while another keeps sending.
- An older setup is going stale: journeys and emails built in outbound marketing no longer run.

### How MP-365 delivers a Customer Insights - Journeys setup
1. Review current campaigns and tools: List the email tools, forms, event tools and spreadsheets you use, and which ones you want to keep.
2. Audit the contact data: Check duplicates, missing emails, consent fields and how contacts and leads are related.
3. Set up the sending foundation: Configure the sending domain and its DNS records, consent and subscription settings, and the roles who can publish.
4. Build segments: Create the audiences you use most, such as new leads, current customers and event attendees.
5. Build one journey end to end: Create a form, a trigger, the messages and the handoff to a seller, and test it with real addresses.
6. Connect results to Sales: Show engagement on contact and lead records and report on pipeline, not only on opens.
7. Rebuild older assets: Recreate useful outbound marketing emails, forms and journeys in real-time journeys.
8. Train and hand off: Train marketers on segments and journeys, and leave short guides for the routine tasks.

### What you get from the setup

- One tested journey: a form-to-seller flow your team can copy.

- Reporting: a view of campaign results tied to leads and opportunities, with Power BI for deeper reports.
- Documentation and training: short guides for the people who run campaigns.

Customer Insights - Journeys is not the right fit if you send a monthly newsletter to a small list, or if nobody on your team will own segments and journeys after launch. Q: Is Dynamics 365 Marketing the same as Customer Insights - Journeys?

The outbound marketing module was removed in May 2026, according to Microsoft Learn, and real-time journeys is the version that remains.
Q: What can Customer Insights - Journeys do?
A: It builds customer segments and sends email, text message and push notification journeys, either on a schedule or when a contact acts. It also handles forms, events and consent. Because it shares Dataverse with Sales, engagement appears on the same contact record a seller opens.
Q: Do we need Customer Insights if we already use Dynamics 365 Sales?
A: Not necessarily. Sales can run basic campaigns and marketing lists. Add Customer Insights - Journeys when you need targeted segments, multi-step journeys and behavior-based triggers for larger audiences. If you only send occasional messages, the sales app may be enough.
Q: What is the difference between Customer Insights - Data and Journeys?
A: Customer Insights - Data unifies customer data from many sources into profiles and segments. Customer Insights - Journeys uses those segments, or ones built in the app, to send messages and run journeys. You can use Journeys alone. MP-365 only adds Data when your information sits in several systems.
Q: What happened to outbound marketing?

Q: Can we reuse our older marketing emails and journeys?

Q: How does a lead move from marketing to sales?

Q: Which channels does Customer Insights - Journeys support?
