Q: How does consent and opt-out management work?
A: Customer Insights - Journeys records consent and subscription choices on the contact, and journeys respect them. MP-365 sets up the fields, subscription settings and forms and checks that opt-outs stop messages. Your legal team still decides what consent your business needs. MP-365 does not give legal advice.
Q: Is Customer Insights - Journeys a good fit for a mid-size company?
A: Yes, when you have a marketing owner, a contact list large enough to segment and a sales team that follows up leads in Dynamics 365. It is less suitable if you send a few messages a year. MP-365 keeps the first setup small so the team can run it.

If you were running Microsoft Dynamics 365 Marketing before the rename, the job now sits in Customer Insights - Journeys, and some assets need rebuilding. MP-365 handles the setup, the rebuild and the connection to Sales.

## Dynamics 365 Lead Scoring and Lead Management
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/lead-management/

Dynamics 365 lead scoring ranks open leads so sellers call the likeliest buyers first, and it is one part of a four-step lead process: capture, score, route and attribute. MP-365 builds that process in Dynamics 365 for mid-size and enterprise teams that lose leads between marketing, sales and the spreadsheet in between.

bestFor: Sales and marketing leaders whose leads arrive from forms, events, partners and email, and whose reports cannot say which source produced revenue.
includes: Lead capture design, qualification flow, rule-based or predictive scoring, routing rules, duplicate handling, source and campaign tracking, dashboards and training.
notIncluded: Lead generation or advertising, campaign copywriting, ERP implementation and Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call to trace where leads come from and where they stall, then a review of your lead data in the CRM.

### What is CRM lead management?
CRM lead management is the process of capturing every inquiry, deciding which ones deserve attention, assigning each to an owner and tracking it until it becomes a deal or is closed. Good sales lead management makes sure nothing waits in an inbox and every lead has a recorded source.
In Dynamics 365, a lead is a record for a person or company you have not yet qualified. When a seller qualifies it, the system can create an account, a contact and an opportunity, and the opportunity keeps a link to the originating lead.

### Capture: get every lead into one place
Lead capture means every channel writes to the same lead table. Typical channels are website forms, event lists, partner referrals, LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms and email requests. Microsoft provides a Dynamics 365 connector that syncs leads from LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms.
Capture quality sets everything after it. Required fields, a clean source value and duplicate detection stop bad records at the door.

### Dynamics 365 lead scoring: rule-based and predictive
Lead scoring assigns each lead a number that estimates how likely it is to become a customer. In Dynamics 365 you can use predictive scoring, which learns from past outcomes, or a rule-based score you define yourself.
According to Microsoft Learn (2026), predictive lead scoring needs at least 40 qualified and 40 disqualified leads in the training period, and Sales Insights features must be enabled. New leads are scored within about five minutes. Updated leads are rescored every 24 hours.

### Route: give each lead an owner fast
Routing assigns a new lead to a person or a queue by rules such as region, product, company size or score. The aim is simple: no lead sits unowned. Rules should be few and explainable, because a rep who does not understand why a lead arrived will ignore it.
MP-365 also adds a visible follow-up deadline, so an untouched lead surfaces on a manager's view instead of going quiet.

### Attribute: how to track lead sources in a CRM
Lead attribution links each lead, and the revenue that follows, to where it came from. To track lead sources in a CRM, store the source and campaign on the lead at capture, carry both to the opportunity when the lead is qualified, and report on closed revenue by source.
Simple first-touch attribution credits the first source. Last-touch credits the final one. Richer models need extra fields and reports, and MP-365 builds them only if your team will act on the answer.

### Rule-based or predictive lead scoring
Factor | Rule-based score | Predictive score
How the score is set | Points you assign, such as job title, company size and form activity | A model trained on your past qualified and disqualified leads
Data needed | A clear idea of your ideal buyer | At least 40 qualified and 40 disqualified leads in the training period
Explainability | Easy to explain, because every point has a reason | Shows top influencing factors, but the model decides the weights
Licensing | Built with columns and automation you already have | Needs Sales Insights features; Sales Enterprise includes 1,500 scored records a month, and Sales Premium covers more
Best for | New programs, small history, or teams that want full control | Teams with enough closed leads and steady lead volume

### Where lead management usually breaks
- Sources are typed by hand: reps type different names for one source, so reports split it.
- Scores nobody trusts: a number appears on the form, but no one knows what it means.
- Duplicates: the same person enters as three leads, and sellers contact them three times.
- No handoff rule: marketing calls a lead ready, sales calls it junk, and neither measures the difference.
- Qualification stops reports: leads are closed without a reason, so you cannot see why deals fail.

### How MP-365 delivers Dynamics 365 lead management
1. Trace the lead journey: Follow real leads from first contact to closed, and note where each one waited or disappeared.
2. Define qualified: Write the criteria sales and marketing both accept, with a reason list for disqualified leads.
3. Standardize sources and campaigns: Replace hand-typed sources with controlled choices and map each capture channel to them.
4. Set up capture and duplicate rules: Connect forms and imports to the lead table and add rules that flag likely duplicates.
5. Build the scoring model: Start with a rule-based score, or train a predictive model if your history qualifies.
6. Configure routing and follow-up: Assign owners by clear rules and add follow-up deadlines that show up in manager views.
7. Build source and funnel dashboards: Report lead volume, conversion and revenue by source in Power BI or in-app dashboards.
8. Train and tune: Train the teams, then review score accuracy and rejection reasons after real use.

### What you get from lead management work
- One lead process: documented stages from capture to qualified or closed.
- A scoring model: rule-based or predictive, with a short note on how to read it.
- Routing rules: assignment logic your managers can explain.
- Clean source data: controlled values carried from lead to opportunity.
- Dashboards: funnel and source views built with Power BI.
- Training: short guides for sellers, marketers and administrators.

### Proof: one lead process and dashboards for marketing and sales
A company tracked leads in different places, and building lead reports took marketing and sales leaders several business days each month. MP-365 set up one lead process in Dynamics 365 with dashboards for marketing and sales leaders.
Both teams now work from the same lead data. The clients page shows more MP-365 work.

### When lead management work is not the right fit
Lead management work is not the right fit if you get a few leads a month, because a simple list will do. It also will not create demand. MP-365 does not run advertising or lead generation. It makes sure the leads you earn are captured, owned and measured.

### Related Dynamics 365 CRM services
Lead management sits between marketing and selling. See Customer Insights - Journeys for campaigns that create leads and Dynamics 365 Sales for the pipeline that follows. All services are listed under Dynamics 365 CRM consulting. For cost, read the pricing page.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How does lead scoring work in Dynamics 365?
A: Dynamics 365 lead scoring gives each open lead a number that estimates its chance of becoming an opportunity. Predictive scoring trains a model on past qualified and disqualified leads. A rule-based score uses points you define. Sellers see the score in views and on the lead form.
Q: How do you track lead sources in a CRM?
A: Record the source and campaign on each lead at capture, using controlled choices rather than typed text. Carry both values to the opportunity when the lead is qualified, then report closed revenue by source. This is what lets you compare channels by revenue instead of lead count.
Q: What is lead attribution?
A: Lead attribution links a lead, and the revenue it produces, to the source that brought it in. First-touch attribution credits the first source, last-touch the final one. MP-365 usually starts with a simple model, because a clean source field beats a complicated model with bad data.
Q: How many leads do you need for predictive lead scoring?
A: Microsoft Learn (2026) says you need at least 40 qualified and 40 disqualified leads created and closed within the training period you choose, and Sales Insights features must be enabled. If you have fewer, MP-365 sets up a rule-based score first and revisits predictive scoring later.
Q: Is lead scoring included in Dynamics 365 Sales Enterprise?
A: Partly. Microsoft Learn (2026) says Sales Enterprise can use predictive lead scoring with 1,500 scored records per month, and Sales Premium gives more capacity. Check your license before planning. Rule-based scoring uses standard columns and automation, so it does not depend on the premium features.
Q: How often are Dynamics 365 lead scores updated?
A: According to Microsoft Learn (2026), new leads are scored in near real time, with the score showing within about five minutes of saving. Updated leads are rescored every 24 hours. Models can retrain automatically so they learn from recent outcomes without manual work.
Q: What happens when a lead is qualified in Dynamics 365?
A: Qualifying a lead can create an account, a contact and an opportunity, automatically or by the seller's choice. Notes from the lead appear on the opportunity, and mapped fields carry over. If duplicate detection finds a match, the seller resolves it before qualification completes.
Q: How should leads be routed to sellers?
A: Route by a few clear rules, such as region, product line, company size or score, and send leftovers to a shared queue with a visible deadline. Avoid long rule chains. Sellers follow up on leads they understand, and managers can fix a simple rule quickly.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 stop duplicate leads?
A: Yes. Duplicate detection rules flag matching records, and Dynamics 365 Sales can also use fuzzy matching on lead and company names. When a duplicate exists, qualification pauses until the seller merges or resolves it. MP-365 tunes the rules so they catch real duplicates without blocking good leads.
Q: Can we import LinkedIn leads into Dynamics 365?
A: Yes. Microsoft provides the Dynamics 365 Connector for LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms, which syncs leads from LinkedIn forms into Dynamics 365 Sales. MP-365 maps the form fields and source value so those leads follow the same scoring and routing as every other channel.

Dynamics 365 lead scoring helps only when the lead process around it is clear: every lead captured once, scored, routed to an owner and tied to a source. MP-365 builds that process, then tunes it with your team's results.

## Dynamics 365 Security Roles and Access Audit
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/security-roles-audit/

Dynamics 365 security roles decide who can create, read, change and share each type of record, and they tend to drift as people change jobs. MP-365 reviews your roles and user access, removes unnecessary Admin rights, and documents who should have what.

bestFor: IT and operations leaders whose Dynamics 365 has run for a while and who cannot say who holds the System Administrator role, or why.
includes: User and role review, admin access check, role redesign by job function, business unit and team review, an approval process, documented access levels and recurring access reports.
notIncluded: Cybersecurity services, identity and access management, security monitoring, compliance certification, ERP implementation and Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call about how access is granted today, then a read-only review of users, roles and teams in your environment.

### What are Dynamics 365 security roles?
Dynamics 365 security roles are sets of privileges that control what a user can do with each type of data. They are part of Microsoft Dataverse, the data platform under Sales, Customer Service and Customer Insights. You assign a role to a user directly or to a team, and the user gets the privileges that role grants.
A role defines eight standard privileges for each table: Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign and Share. Each privilege carries an access level that says how wide it reaches.

### How Dynamics 365 security role permissions work
Layer | What it controls | Common mistake
Privileges | The actions a role allows on a table, such as Read or Delete | Granting Delete on tables where users only need Read
Access levels | How far a privilege reaches: user, business unit, parent and child business units, or the whole organization | Using organization-wide access when business unit access is enough
Business units | Security boundaries that group users and data | Leaving everyone in the root business unit
Teams | Groups that hold roles and can own records | Assigning roles to individuals, so nobody can see the pattern
Record sharing | One-off access to a specific record | Using sharing as the main model, which is slower and hard to troubleshoot
Column security profiles | Extra control over sensitive columns on a table | Skipping it for salary, margin or contract columns

### Why users end up with too much admin access
Users end up with too much admin access because permissions are added under pressure and rarely removed. Microsoft Learn (2026) states that Dataverse security privileges are cumulative: a user receives the broadest access from all of their roles and teams. Adding a restrictive role never takes access away.
That design makes sprawl easy. Someone cannot save a record, so an administrator grants System Administrator to unblock them. A new hire is set up by copying a colleague's access. A project ends, and nobody removes the temporary role. Over time the number of powerful users grows, and no one notices.

### What an access review looks for
- System Administrator holders: every user with the role, and a named reason for each.
- Unused access: accounts that have not signed in or that belong to people who left.
- Overlapping roles: users with several roles that add up to more than any job needs.
- Copied roles: custom roles cloned years ago that now grant far more than their name suggests.
- Shared and service accounts: accounts used by integrations with broader access than the integration needs.
- Sharing exceptions: records shared one by one that should follow a rule.

### How MP-365 runs a Dynamics 365 access audit
1. List users, roles and teams: Export every user in each environment with their direct roles, team roles and business unit.
2. Find the administrators: Identify everyone with System Administrator or equivalent rights and ask the business to justify each one.
3. Map access to job functions: Group users by what they do, such as seller, service agent, manager or finance reviewer.
4. Compare privileges with real need: Check each role against the tables and actions that function uses, and flag excess.
5. Design the target role set: Define a small number of roles per function, assigned through teams rather than to individuals.
6. Test in a sandbox: Apply the new roles to test users, run their daily tasks and confirm nothing breaks.
7. Apply changes with approval: Move users to the new roles in agreed batches, with a sign-off for each group.
8. Document and automate reporting: Record the access levels and schedule a recurring report of who holds which role.

### What you get from the audit
- Access inventory: a clear list of users, roles and teams per environment.
- Findings report: the excess access found, ranked by risk to your data.
- Role design: a smaller set of roles built around job functions.
- Approval process: a documented way to request, approve and remove access.
- Access report: a recurring view of who holds which role, built with Power BI or in-app views.
- Documentation: a plain description of each access level for your administrators.

### Microsoft products involved in a roles audit
The work happens in the Power Platform admin center and in Dataverse, where roles, business units and teams live. Microsoft Entra ID groups can feed Dataverse group teams, so a user's role follows their group membership. Power Automate can route access requests for approval, and Power BI shows the results.
Microsoft 365 permissions are a separate layer. Microsoft Purview and permission models covers the files and sites side, and the AI Data Governance Audit checks what Copilot can reach before rollout. Poor data quality also hides access problems, such as duplicate owners.

### Proof: CRM access control with approvals and automatic reports
A company's CRM access had grown without a process. MP-365 introduced an approval process for access requests, documented the access levels and set up automatic access reports.
Administrators can now see who holds which role without building a report by hand. The clients page lists more MP-365 work.

### When this audit is not the right fit
A Dynamics 365 access audit is not the right fit if you need security operations, threat monitoring, identity management or compliance certification. MP-365 does not provide those services. The audit covers Dynamics 365 roles and related Microsoft 365 permissions, and nothing beyond them. If you need broader security work, hire a specialist for that.

### Related Dynamics 365 CRM services
Access reviews often come with other clean-up work. See Dynamics 365 CRM consulting for the full list, and the pricing page for how MP-365 prices this kind of review.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What are security roles in Dynamics 365?
A: Security roles are groups of privileges in Microsoft Dataverse that define what users can do with each table. Each role sets Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign and Share privileges, with an access level for each. You assign roles to users or teams, and the access is added up.
Q: How do you audit user access in Dynamics 365?
A: List every user with their roles, teams and business unit, then identify who holds System Administrator. Compare each role with what the job needs, and remove what is extra. Test changes in a sandbox, apply them with approval, and keep a recurring report so drift is visible.
Q: Why do users end up with too much admin access?
A: Access is granted to unblock someone and rarely removed. Dataverse privileges are cumulative, so extra roles only add. Copying a colleague's access for a new hire, leftover project roles and staff who change jobs all push the count of powerful users up without anyone deciding it.
Q: Does adding a restrictive role take away access?
A: No. Microsoft Learn (2026) says Dataverse security is cumulative, and a user receives the broadest access granted by all their roles and team memberships. To reduce access you must remove or change the broader role. This is why audits find users with more access than any single role suggests.
Q: What are access levels in a Dynamics 365 security role?
A: Access levels say how far a privilege reaches. They range from only the records a user owns, to business unit records, to parent and child business units, up to the whole organization. Choosing the narrowest level that supports the job is the main way to limit exposure.
Q: What is the difference between a role, a team and a business unit?
A: A role lists privileges. A team is a group of users that can hold roles and own records. A business unit is a security boundary that groups users and data. Roles define what is allowed, business units define where, and teams make assigning roles manageable.
Q: Can we manage Dynamics 365 roles with Microsoft Entra groups?
A: Yes. Microsoft Learn (2026) describes mapping a Microsoft Entra security group to a Dataverse group team and assigning the role to that team. Users then gain or lose access as they join or leave the group. MP-365 designs the group structure with you during the audit.
Q: What is column-level security?
A: Column-level security restricts access to sensitive columns, such as pricing or personal data, even for users who can see the record. You enable it per column and grant access through a column security profile. Microsoft advises using it only where needed, since heavy use can slow performance.
Q: How often should Dynamics 365 access be reviewed?
A: Review administrator access often, and the full role set on a schedule that matches how quickly your team changes. Many organizations also review when staff leave or a major project ends. A recurring access report from MP-365 makes the review a quick check rather than a project.
Q: Is this a cybersecurity service?
A: No. The audit covers Dynamics 365 roles, teams, business units and related Microsoft 365 permissions. MP-365 does not provide security operations, threat monitoring, identity management or compliance certification. It is a practical review of who can do what in your CRM.

Dynamics 365 security roles stay manageable when each role matches a job, access flows through teams, and someone checks the list on a schedule. MP-365 sets that up and gives you the report to keep it that way.

## Dynamics 365 Integration Services and ERP Links
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/dynamics-365-crm/integration-services/

Dynamics 365 integration services connect your CRM to the other systems your business runs on, including ERP, marketing tools and SharePoint, so data moves automatically and nobody types it twice. MP-365 builds, tests and supports these integrations for mid-size and enterprise teams, and it connects ERP systems without implementing them.

bestFor: Operations, sales and IT leaders whose staff re-key orders, customers or invoices between Dynamics 365 and another system.
includes: Integration design, field mapping, Power Automate flows, API and Azure-based connections, SharePoint document integration, logging, alerts, service accounts, testing and support.
notIncluded: ERP implementation or configuration, Azure hosting management, Microsoft license resale and custom software development.
howItStarts: A discovery call to list the systems and the data that must move, then a review of current connections and any manual re-keying.

### What Dynamics 365 integration services cover
Dynamics 365 integration services cover the design, build and support of connections between Dynamics 365 and other systems. The most common are ERP systems such as Business Central, marketing and email tools, SharePoint document libraries and reporting platforms.
MP-365 works on the connection, not on the system at the other end. The aim is simple: when a customer, order or invoice changes in one place, the other system learns about it without a person copying it over.

### How do you integrate Dynamics 365 with an ERP?
Integrate Dynamics 365 with an ERP by deciding which system owns each type of data, then moving it with the lightest tool that is reliable enough. Customer and product records usually sync on a schedule or on change. Orders and invoices move when an event happens, such as an order being submitted.
The right tool depends on the ERP and the volume. Some connections are built in, some use Power Automate, and some need code against the Dataverse Web API. MP-365 picks per data flow instead of forcing one tool onto everything.

### Dynamics 365 integration options and when each fits
Approach | Best for | Watch out for
Built-in Business Central connection through Dataverse | Business Central customers who want products, price lists, opportunities, invoices and sales orders shared with Dynamics 365 Sales | Reconnecting resets default synchronization settings, so changes need to be documented
Dual-write | Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps that need near-real-time, two-way data with Dataverse | It is tightly coupled and adds concepts such as company and party to Dataverse, so the design needs planning
Power Automate cloud flows | Event-driven moves, approvals and notifications between the CRM and systems with a connector | Flows tied to a person's account stop when that person leaves
Dataverse Web API with Azure Logic Apps or Functions | High volume, unusual ERP structures or complex data transformation | Needs developer support and careful handling of Dataverse request limits
SharePoint document integration | Contracts, quotes and files stored against CRM records | Folder design and permissions must be planned before documents pile up

### Can Dynamics 365 connect to Business Central?
Yes. Microsoft Learn (2026) states that Business Central integrates with Dynamics 365 Sales through Dataverse. The standard mappings cover items and products, price lists, opportunities, posted sales invoices and sales orders. Sales orders can sync in one direction or both, and sellers can see Business Central information while working in Dynamics 365 Sales.
Microsoft Learn also describes dedicated Business Central integration security roles for the integration user account. MP-365 runs the connection under a dedicated account with only those privileges and reviews it against your security roles. The result is a connection that does not depend on one person's login.

### How Dynamics 365 SharePoint integration works
Dynamics 365 SharePoint integration stores documents in SharePoint but shows them on the CRM record. According to Microsoft Learn, server-based integration lets users sign in once, see SharePoint documents in lists and run SharePoint actions from the command bar. Users outside the CRM can open the same documents if they have SharePoint permissions.
The decisions that matter come first: which tables get document libraries, how folders are named, and who may open what. MP-365 settles those before turning it on for the sales or service teams.

### How to make sure no records are lost in an integration
- Log every transfer: record what moved, when and the result, so a missing record has a trail.
- Alert on failure: send a message to a named person when a run fails, instead of waiting for users to notice.
- Retry with care: Dataverse returns a 429 error with a Retry-After value when a user sends too many requests, and the integration must wait and try again.
- Match on stable keys: use an ID from the source system, not a name, so retries update a record instead of duplicating it.
- Use a service account: run the integration under a dedicated account, never under a person's login.
- Store secrets safely: keep passwords and keys in a secure store, not in a flow or a file.
- Reconcile counts: compare record totals on both sides on a schedule and report differences.

### How MP-365 delivers Dynamics 365 integration services
1. List the systems and data flows: Write down every system, what data moves, in which direction and how often it must happen.
2. Decide who owns each record type: Pick the system of record for customers, products, prices and orders, so conflicts have a rule.
3. Map the fields: Match each field between systems, including formats, required values and what happens when one is blank.
4. Choose the tool for each flow: Use a built-in connection, Power Automate or code against the API, based on volume and complexity.
5. Build in a sandbox: Create the connection in a test environment, with a dedicated integration account and logging from the start.
6. Test with real data: Run a sample of real records, including awkward ones, and compare totals on both sides.
7. Go live and monitor: Release in stages, watch the logs and alerts, and fix issues before users see them.
8. Document and hand off: Leave a map of every flow, its owner and its alert recipient, and stay available for support.

### What you get from integration work
- Integration map: a one-page view of systems, data flows and owners.
- Field mapping document: agreed matches and rules for each record type.
- Working connections: built, tested and running under dedicated accounts.
- Logging and alerts: a way to see what moved and to be told when something fails.
- Reconciliation report: record counts compared across systems on a schedule.
- Runbook: short instructions for restarting a failed flow.

Failures now produce an alert and a log entry rather than a silent gap in the data. See the clients page for more MP-365 work.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you integrate Dynamics 365 with an ERP?
A: Decide which system owns each type of data, map the fields, then pick the connection method for each flow: a built-in connection, Power Automate or code against the Dataverse API. Test with real records, then add logging and alerts. MP-365 builds the connection but not the ERP itself.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 connect to Business Central?
A: Yes. Business Central integrates with Dynamics 365 Sales through Dataverse, according to Microsoft Learn (2026). Standard mappings cover items and products, price lists, opportunities, invoices and sales orders. MP-365 sets up and supports the connection, and it does not do ERP implementation.
Q: How do you make sure no records are lost in an integration?
A: Log every transfer, alert a named person on failure, retry when Dataverse asks you to wait, and match records on stable IDs so retries update rather than duplicate. Run a scheduled count comparison between systems. These steps turn silent data loss into a visible, fixable error.
Q: What is the difference between Dynamics 365 integration and dual-write?
A: Dual-write is one specific method. Microsoft Learn describes it as tightly coupled, near-real-time, two-way integration between finance and operations apps and Dataverse. Integration is the broader job and includes Power Automate, APIs and built-in connections. MP-365 chooses the method per data flow.
Q: How much do Dynamics 365 integration services cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of systems, data flows, volume and the complexity of the mapping. A single scheduled sync is a small job, while two-way order flow with error handling is larger. The pricing page explains how MP-365 prices work. License fees go to Microsoft separately.
Q: How long does an integration project take?
A: It depends on how many data flows are involved, how clean the source data is and how quickly your team can answer mapping questions. MP-365 starts with the flow that removes the most re-keying, goes live with it, and adds the next. A discovery call produces a realistic sequence.
Q: Is a real-time integration always better than a scheduled one?
A: No. Real-time is worth the extra cost for orders, availability or anything a person waits on. Scheduled sync is simpler and more robust for master data such as products or price lists. Dataverse also limits request volume per user, so bulk loads often work better in batches.
Q: What are Dataverse service protection limits?
A: Microsoft Learn (2026) says Dataverse applies default limits per user and per web server, including 6,000 requests within a five-minute sliding window. When a client exceeds a limit, Dataverse returns a 429 error with a Retry-After value. A good integration waits and retries instead of failing.
Q: Why should integrations use a service account?
A: A dedicated account keeps the connection running when staff change jobs, and it limits what the integration can do. Microsoft's Business Central documentation provides dedicated integration roles for this purpose. MP-365 builds integrations under service accounts with only the privileges they need and stores their credentials securely.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 integrate with SharePoint?
A: Yes. Microsoft Learn describes server-based SharePoint integration that shows documents in the CRM record while storing them in SharePoint. Users sign in once and can run SharePoint actions from the command bar. MP-365 plans libraries, folders and permissions before turning the feature on.

Dynamics 365 integration services pay off when staff stop re-keying data and the numbers match across systems. MP-365 builds each connection with logging, alerts and a clear owner, so problems surface early. For the business view of this work, read about CRM and systems integration.

### When should a company move to SharePoint Online?
A company should move to SharePoint Online when its on-premises SharePoint can no longer be supported or patched, or when staff need to reach files without a VPN. Microsoft ended support for SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 on July 14, 2026, so those farms no longer receive security updates.
SharePoint Online also connects directly to Teams, Power Automate and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Those tools respect the permissions you set in SharePoint, so clean permissions matter more once Copilot is in use. The Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness service covers that side.
Staying on-premises is a valid choice for some organizations. Microsoft still ships updates for SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, and its documentation lists version 26H2 as of October 2026. MP-365 will tell you if that path fits better than the cloud.

### How MP-365 approaches SharePoint consulting
1. Listen to the business problem: Hold one focused session with the people who feel the pain. Capture what they cannot do today, not a list of features.
2. Inventory what exists: Scan current sites, libraries, workflows, permissions and customizations. Mark what to keep, fix, merge or retire.
3. Design structure before building: Decide site types, hub sites, content types, metadata and permission groups on paper first. Changing a diagram is cheaper than changing a live site.
4. Build a working version fast: Stand up a small, real slice, such as the home page and one department site, so your team reacts to something they can click.
5. Validate with your team: Let the people who will use it test it. Feedback changes the design before the larger build or migration begins.
6. Migrate or launch in stages: Move content and open sites in waves, with a rollback plan for each wave and a check with the site owner after it.
7. Hand off with documentation: Document the structure, train the owners and give your administrators what they need to run it without MP-365.

## SharePoint Intranet Services and Development
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/sharepoint/intranet-development/

SharePoint intranet services from MP-365 design and build a company intranet on SharePoint Online, with clear ownership, working search and no VPN needed. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that builds intranets for mid-size and enterprise teams replacing an old SharePoint Server site, a shared drive or a portal nobody opens.

bestFor: Mid-size and enterprise companies that need one trusted place for news, policies, department sites and tools, built on the Microsoft 365 licenses they already own.
includes: Site architecture, hub sites, home page, news, navigation, permission groups, search setup, page templates and owner training.
notIncluded: Custom software development, web design agency work, ERP implementation, cybersecurity services and Microsoft licenses.
howItStarts: A discovery call about who the intranet is for and what is broken today, followed by a working prototype of the home page and one department site.

### What SharePoint intranet services include
SharePoint intranet services turn a set of SharePoint sites into one company portal that staff actually use. A SharePoint intranet is not one site. It is a group of communication sites, team sites and hub sites that share navigation, search and a common look.
MP-365 handles the whole path: what the intranet should do, how the sites connect, who owns each page, how permissions work, and how staff will find things. It builds with SharePoint's own features and Power Automate, so your team can keep editing it after launch.

### Problems a SharePoint intranet fixes
- Nobody knows where the latest policy is: the same handbook sits in email, a shared drive and three old sites, and staff trust none of them.
- News never reaches the people who need it: announcements go out by email and get lost, especially for field and plant staff.
- Everything needs a VPN: staff outside the office cannot reach basic documents without connecting to the network first.
- Content has no owner: pages go stale because nobody is named as responsible, and updates wait for IT.
- Search returns noise: old versions, duplicates and files with no titles bury the page you need.

### How MP-365 delivers SharePoint intranet development
1. Define who the intranet serves: Interview a few people from each audience, such as office staff, field teams and managers. Write down the top tasks they need done.
2. Audit existing content and sites: List what lives on the old intranet, shared drives and Teams. Mark each item to keep, rewrite, move or delete.
3. Design the site structure: Plan communication sites, team sites and hub sites, and decide which function gets a hub. Use flat sites and hubs, not nested subsites.
4. Set the permission model: Create a small number of permission groups with named owners. Keep broad read access for the intranet itself and tighter access for sensitive sites.
5. Build the home page and one department site: Create the working slice first: navigation, news, quick links and one real department site. Your team reacts to something they can click.
6. Test with real users: Ask a mixed group to complete their top tasks. Change navigation, labels and layout based on what they struggle with.
7. Migrate content and open sites in waves: Move approved content, retire the old pages, and launch department by department so owners can learn in small groups.
8. Train owners and hand off: Teach page owners to publish and update. Document the structure, templates and governance rules for your administrators.

### How a SharePoint intranet is structured
A modern SharePoint intranet is built from three site types, and each has a different job. Microsoft's own intranet planning guidance names them as team sites for collaboration, communication sites for broadcasting, and hub sites for connecting related sites. MP-365 uses all three.

### Communication sites for company news and policies
Communication sites suit content that a few people publish and many people read. Examples are the home page, HR policies, safety procedures and leadership updates. They are private by default and do not need a Microsoft 365 group behind them.

### Team sites for departments and projects
Team sites suit groups that create and edit content together. Each team site sits behind a Microsoft 365 group, which gives the team a shared mailbox, calendar and Planner alongside the document library. They connect to Microsoft Teams when a team wants chat.

### Hub sites to connect related sites
A hub site links a family of sites under shared navigation, theme and search. An HR hub, for example, can bring together benefits, recruiting and the manager portal. A site can join only one hub, but its news can roll up to the hub. Hubs do not change the permissions on the sites inside them.

### What you get from MP-365
- Information architecture: a site map showing which sites exist, which hubs connect them and who owns each one.
- Home page and navigation: a configured home page, global and hub navigation, quick links and audience targeting where it helps.
- Page and news templates: reusable layouts so owners publish consistent pages without help.
- Permission model: documented groups and access levels, with owners named for every site.
- Search setup: titles, metadata and scoping so staff find policies and people quickly.
- Automations: approvals, review reminders and request forms built with Power Automate where they save time.
- Governance guide and training: a short document and a working session for site owners and administrators.

### Microsoft products used in a SharePoint intranet
Product | Role in the intranet
SharePoint Online | Hosts the communication sites, team sites and hub sites. Staff reach it from any device after signing in with their work account.
Microsoft 365 groups and Microsoft Teams | Give team sites their membership, shared mailbox and chat. Teams links back to the intranet.
Microsoft Entra ID | Provides the work sign-in that replaces the VPN requirement for reading intranet content.
Microsoft Search | Lets staff find pages, files and people from the SharePoint start page and the search box on each site.
Power Automate | Runs approvals, review reminders and request forms attached to intranet libraries and lists.
Power Apps | Adds small forms or lookups, such as an equipment request, when a list form is not enough.

### How much does a SharePoint intranet cost to build?
The cost of a SharePoint intranet depends on scope, not on a flat price. SharePoint is already included in most Microsoft 365 business and enterprise plans, so the main cost is design and build effort. MP-365 does not resell licenses, and Microsoft's license fees are separate.
The pricing page explains how MP-365 engagements work. A short discovery call is enough to produce a written estimate for your intranet.

### What drives intranet effort and timeline
- Number of audiences and sites: one company home page is simple. Ten departments with their own sites take more design and testing.
- Amount of content to migrate: pages, documents and forms from the old intranet each need a decision.
- Integration needs: links to HR, time tracking or CRM systems add build and test effort.
- Permission complexity: restricted sites, contractors and multiple regions change the access model.
- Your team's availability: content owners who answer quickly keep the project moving.

Q: What is a SharePoint intranet?

Q: Do employees need a VPN to use a SharePoint Online intranet?

Q: How are permissions handled on a SharePoint intranet?
A: MP-365 sets a small number of permission groups with named owners. Most intranet content is readable by everyone in the company, while sensitive sites such as HR or finance have tighter access. Hub sites do not change permissions, so each site keeps its own.

## SharePoint Migration Consulting and Upgrades
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/sharepoint/migration/

SharePoint migration consulting from MP-365 moves SharePoint Server 2010, 2013, 2016 and 2019 sites, content and workflows to SharePoint Online. Microsoft ended support for SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 on July 14, 2026, so those farms no longer receive security fixes. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that plans the move, handles the customizations and cuts over in stages.

bestFor: IT leaders running SharePoint Server 2010, 2013, 2016 or 2019 who need to move to SharePoint Online, or decide between the cloud and SharePoint Server Subscription Edition.
includes: Farm assessment, customization and workflow review, target site design, pilot, staged content migration, cutover, link cleanup and hand-off documentation.
notIncluded: Azure infrastructure or hosting management, cybersecurity services, custom software development, ERP implementation and Microsoft licenses.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your current farm, followed by a scan of sites, content and customizations and a written migration plan.

### What happens now that SharePoint 2016 and 2019 support has ended?
SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 keep running after July 14, 2026, but Microsoft no longer issues security updates or technical support for them. Every new vulnerability stays open, and compatibility with newer Microsoft 365 services slowly erodes.
Older versions are already further behind. SharePoint Server 2013 support ended on April 11, 2023, according to Microsoft's lifecycle documentation. If your farm is on any of these versions, the question is no longer whether to move, but where and in what order.

### Where each SharePoint Server version stands
Version | Support status (October 2026) | Move to SharePoint Online with Microsoft's tool
SharePoint Server 2010 | Out of support | Supported by the SharePoint Migration Tool
SharePoint Server 2013 | Support ended April 11, 2023 | Supported by the SharePoint Migration Tool
SharePoint Server 2016 | Support ended July 14, 2026 | Supported by the SharePoint Migration Tool
SharePoint Server 2019 | Support ended July 14, 2026 | Supported by the SharePoint Migration Tool
SharePoint Server Subscription Edition | In support, updated twice a year in Microsoft's documentation | Not a migration target for this move; it stays on-premises

### Migrate to SharePoint Online or move to Subscription Edition?
Migrate to SharePoint Online when you want Microsoft to run the platform and you want Teams, Power Automate and Copilot to work against the same content. Choose SharePoint Server Subscription Edition only when a business or regulatory reason keeps data on-premises. Subscription Edition still needs servers, patching and upgrades from your team.
MP-365 gives a plain recommendation after the assessment. Some companies split the move: most sites go to SharePoint Online, and a few stay on Subscription Edition behind a hybrid setup.

### How SharePoint migration consulting works, from scan to cutover
1. Scan the farm: Run Microsoft's SharePoint Migration Assessment Tool against SharePoint 2010, 2013 or 2016 farms to find blocking issues, then inventory sites, sizes, workflows and custom code by hand where the tool does not reach.
2. Decide what moves: Sort every site and library into move, merge, archive or delete. Most farms hold years of unused content that does not need to travel.
3. Design the target: Map old site collections and subsites to modern sites and hub sites. Decide permission groups and the Microsoft Entra ID accounts that users will sign in with.
4. Rebuild what will not move: Replace unsupported workflows, InfoPath forms and custom code with Power Automate, Power Apps or standard SharePoint features.
5. Run a pilot migration: Move one real site with its owners involved. Check permissions, metadata, versions and links before touching larger sites.
6. Migrate in waves: Move sites in groups. Repeat passes to catch changes made during the move, and record every exception in a log that owners can read.
7. Cut over and fix links: Switch users to the new sites, make old sites read-only, and update links in documents, emails and bookmarks that pointed to the old URLs.
8. Decommission and hand off: Archive or remove the old farm once owners sign off. Give your administrators the new structure, permission map and documentation.

### What does not migrate cleanly from SharePoint Server
Customizations are the main risk in any SharePoint Server migration. Content moves well. Code and legacy features need replacement.

### Workflows and InfoPath forms
Microsoft retired SharePoint 2013 workflows in SharePoint Online starting April 2, 2026, according to its Message Center notice MC542767, and recommends Power Automate instead. Workflows built in SharePoint Designer or InfoPath forms need to be rebuilt as Power Automate flows or Power Apps forms. MP-365 lists each one during the scan and rebuilds the ones that still matter.

### Farm solutions and custom code
Farm solutions that run full-trust code on your servers cannot run in SharePoint Online. MP-365 reviews what each one does and replaces it with a modern equivalent, such as a standard web part, a Power Automate flow or a retired feature nobody needs.

### Classic pages, permissions and subsites
Classic pages work, but they miss modern features, so MP-365 rebuilds key pages as modern pages. Permissions carry over cleanly only when on-premises accounts match accounts in Microsoft Entra ID, so identity mapping is checked before the first copy. Deep subsite trees are flattened into sites and hubs.

### What you get from MP-365
- Assessment report: sites, sizes, versions, workflows and custom code, each with a move, rebuild or retire decision.
- Migration plan: waves, owners, a communication note for each group and a rollback step for every wave.
- Target design: the new site and hub structure with the permission model.
- Rebuilt workflows and forms: Power Automate flows and Power Apps forms for the ones you keep.
- Migration logs: a record of what moved, what was skipped and why.
- Cutover support and link cleanup: redirected or updated links in key documents and navigation.
- Hand-off pack: structure, permissions and owner guidance for your administrators.

Tool | What MP-365 uses it for
SharePoint Migration Assessment Tool | Scans SharePoint 2010, 2013 and 2016 farms and reports issues to fix before the move.
SharePoint Migration Tool | Copies content from SharePoint Server 2010, 2013, 2016 and 2019 and from file shares to SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What happens now that SharePoint 2016 and 2019 support has ended?
A: Both versions keep running, but Microsoft ended support on July 14, 2026. They receive no security updates or technical help, so new vulnerabilities stay open. Staying put carries growing risk. Most organizations plan a move to SharePoint Online, or to SharePoint Server Subscription Edition if data must stay on-premises.
Q: How do you migrate SharePoint Server to SharePoint Online?
A: Scan the farm, decide what moves, design the target sites, rebuild unsupported workflows, pilot one site, then migrate in waves with Microsoft's SharePoint Migration Tool. Cut over, fix links and decommission the old farm after owners sign off. MP-365 manages each step with your team.
Q: How long does a SharePoint migration take?
A: Duration depends on content volume, number of sites, customizations and how fast owners approve each wave. A farm with few customizations moves faster than one with years of custom code. MP-365 gives a plan with waves and owners after the assessment, not before.
Q: Can we migrate SharePoint 2010 or 2013 straight to SharePoint Online?
A: Yes. Microsoft's SharePoint Migration Tool supports SharePoint Server 2010, 2013, 2016 and 2019 as sources. Older versions such as 2007 usually move in stages first. The harder part is replacing old workflows, forms and custom code, which MP-365 identifies in the assessment.
Q: What happens to our SharePoint workflows during migration?
A: Most old workflows need to be rebuilt. Microsoft retired SharePoint 2013 workflows in SharePoint Online starting April 2, 2026 and recommends Power Automate. MP-365 lists every workflow, retires the ones nobody uses, and rebuilds the rest as Power Automate flows.
Q: Do permissions carry over to SharePoint Online?
A: Permissions can carry over when on-premises accounts map to Microsoft Entra ID accounts. MP-365 checks identity mapping before the first copy and also uses the move to clean up broken inheritance and old groups, so the new site starts with a model people can explain.
Q: Should we move to SharePoint Online or SharePoint Server Subscription Edition?
A: Choose SharePoint Online for most organizations because Microsoft runs the platform and it works with Teams, Power Automate and Copilot. Choose Subscription Edition only when data must stay on-premises. It remains supported, but your team still patches and upgrades the servers. MP-365 recommends after the assessment.
Q: Will our URLs and links change?
A: Yes. Sites in SharePoint Online get new addresses, so links in documents, emails and bookmarks pointing to the old farm break unless they are updated. MP-365 identifies key links during planning, updates them where possible, and keeps old sites read-only until the new ones are approved.
Q: Can users keep working during the migration?
A: Yes. MP-365 migrates in waves, so each group keeps working on the old site until its wave. Repeated passes pick up changes made during the move, and a short freeze on edits applies only at cutover. Owners are told the date in advance.
Q: Does MP-365 host or manage our SharePoint servers?
A: No. MP-365 does not provide Azure infrastructure, hosting management or managed IT services. It plans and carries out the migration, hands off documentation, and can return in support mode when something needs fixing. SharePoint Online is run by Microsoft.

SharePoint migration consulting helps you leave an unsupported farm with a plan, not a rush. MP-365 assesses what you have, rebuilds what will not move, and cuts over in stages so your teams keep working.

## Migrate File Shares to SharePoint Online
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/sharepoint/file-share-migration/

Planning to migrate file share to SharePoint Online? The hard part is deciding what to keep, how to organize it and who may see it, not copying files. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that moves network drives and file servers into SharePoint libraries with clean structure, metadata, version history and permissions people can explain.

bestFor: Companies with Windows file servers or NAS drives holding years of folders, duplicate files and unclear access, and a goal of working in Microsoft 365.
includes: Content scan and cleanup plan, library and metadata design, permission model, pilot, staged migration with Microsoft's tools, cutover and owner training.
notIncluded: Hardware or Azure infrastructure management, cybersecurity services, custom software development, ERP implementation and Microsoft licenses.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your shares, followed by a scan of folder depth, file types, duplicates and access, and a written plan for what goes where.

### How to migrate file share to SharePoint Online without moving the mess
Migrating a file share to SharePoint Online works best as a redesign with a copy step in the middle, not a lift and shift. A copied folder tree keeps every old problem: deep paths, duplicate files, unclear owners and permissions nobody remembers granting.
MP-365 starts with a scan of the share, agrees with department heads what to archive or delete, designs libraries and metadata, and only then moves the files. People can then find things on day one instead of recreating the old maze online.

### Problems with file servers that this fixes
- Files are hard to find: folder names rely on one person's memory, and the same file exists in four places.
- Remote access is awkward: people use a VPN or copy files to laptops and USB drives.
- Version confusion: files named final, final2 and final-REAL circulate by email.
- Unclear access: old Windows groups and inherited folder permissions give the wrong people access to some folders and block others.
- Servers are aging: hardware, backups and storage all cost time to maintain.

### Should files go to SharePoint, OneDrive or Teams?
Destination | Use it for | Why
SharePoint document library | Department, project and company files that several people use | Shared ownership, permissions by site or library, version history and metadata
OneDrive | One person's working files and drafts | Tied to a person, so files can disappear from view when someone leaves unless it is planned
Microsoft Teams | Files discussed in a team's channels | A team's channel files are stored in the SharePoint site behind that team, so Teams is a view of SharePoint, not a separate place

### Most shared files belong in SharePoint, personal files in OneDrive
Shared business files belong in SharePoint, and personal working files belong in OneDrive. If a file will outlive one person's job, put it in a SharePoint library with named owners. MP-365 sorts each folder on the share into one of these homes during planning. The OneDrive migration service covers moving personal home drives.

### SharePoint limits that shape a file share plan
Limit | Value | What it means for the plan
Single file size | 250 GB per file | Very large files such as CAD or video archives still fit, but plan the upload time
Path length | 400 characters including the file name | Deeply nested folders must be shortened before migration
Library size | Up to 30 million files and folders | A single library can hold most shares, but search and views work better with a sound structure
Sync client | Syncing no more than 300,000 files per library is recommended | Large libraries are split by department or year so sync stays fast
Unique permissions | 50,000 supported, 5,000 recommended per library | Permissions are set at library or site level, not folder by folder

### What happens to folder permissions during migration?
Windows folder permissions do not map one to one to SharePoint, and copying them folder by folder creates trouble. Microsoft documents a supported limit of 50,000 unique permissions in a list or library and recommends staying near 5,000. In libraries with more than 100,000 items you also cannot break or restore permission inheritance on the library or folder.
MP-365 therefore designs permissions at the site and library level, using a few groups with named owners. Where a folder truly needs its own access, it becomes its own library or site. This is also the point where old access that nobody can explain is removed.

### How MP-365 moves a file server to SharePoint Online
1. Scan the shares: Report folder depth, path lengths, file types, last-modified dates, duplicates and access, so decisions use facts.
2. Agree what to keep: Ask department owners to mark folders to migrate, archive or delete. Old files without an owner follow a written default rule.
3. Design libraries and metadata: Decide which departments get which sites and libraries, and which fields such as document type, project or year replace deep folders.
4. Set the permission model: Create groups with named owners and apply access at the site and library level. Document who can see what.
5. Fix names and paths: Shorten paths over the limit, remove invalid characters and resolve name clashes before the copy starts.
6. Pilot with one department: Migrate one real share, let the team use it, and adjust libraries, views and metadata from their feedback.
7. Migrate in waves: Copy departments in groups with Microsoft Migration Manager, run extra passes to catch changes, and review the logs for failures.
8. Cut over and retire the share: Make the old share read-only, move users to the new libraries and sync, then archive or remove the share after owners sign off.

### Should we replace folders with metadata?
Replace folders with metadata where people search by attributes, and keep a light folder layer where people browse. Fields such as customer, project and document type let one file appear in several views without being copied. Too many required fields annoy users, so MP-365 usually starts with a few and adds more once people are working.
Design of fields, content types and search is covered in depth in SharePoint information architecture and search.

### What you get from MP-365
- Share scan report: folder, file, path and duplicate findings with recommended actions.
- Cleanup decisions: a signed-off list of what migrates, archives or is deleted.
- Library and metadata design: sites, libraries, content types, columns and views.
- Permission map: groups, owners and access levels, documented in plain language.
- Migration logs: what moved, what failed, and how each failure was resolved.
- Sync and user guidance: how to sync libraries with the OneDrive app and where each type of file belongs.
- Hand-off: owner training and a short governance note for future folders and libraries.

### Microsoft tools used to migrate a file server
Tool | What MP-365 uses it for
Migration Manager in the SharePoint admin center | Installs lightweight agents on servers or virtual machines, runs migration tasks from file shares to SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams, and reports progress. The source server must support SMB 2.0 or higher.
SharePoint Migration Tool | Handles smaller or scripted moves from file shares, including through PowerShell.
OneDrive sync app | Gives users offline access to libraries they need on their computers.
Power Automate | Adds approvals, review reminders or routing to libraries after the move.

See client results for more examples.

The cost depends on the amount of content, the quality of the folder structure, the number of departments and the complexity of permissions. Cleanup decisions take the most time, not the copy. MP-365 gives a written estimate after the scan. The pricing page explains engagement models, and Microsoft licenses are separate.

### When this is not the right fit
This service is not the right fit if you want to leave files exactly where they are, or if you only need a cloud backup of a server. SharePoint is a collaboration platform, not an archive tool. If your files sit in an old SharePoint environment rather than on a network drive, the SharePoint Server upgrade and migration service applies instead.
