### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you migrate a network file share to SharePoint?
A: Scan the share, agree what to keep, design libraries and metadata, set permissions, then copy in waves with Migration Manager in the SharePoint admin center. Agents installed on your servers do the transfer. After cutover the old share becomes read-only until owners confirm the new libraries work.
Q: Should files go to SharePoint or OneDrive?
A: Put shared business files in SharePoint and one person's working files in OneDrive. SharePoint keeps ownership with the team, so files stay when someone leaves. OneDrive is tied to an individual. MP-365 sorts each folder into one of these during planning.
Q: What happens to folder permissions during migration?
A: Windows folder permissions do not carry over cleanly. Microsoft recommends staying near 5,000 unique permissions per library, so MP-365 sets access at the site and library level with named groups. Folders needing their own access become separate libraries or sites, and old unexplained access is dropped.
Q: Can we migrate a file server to SharePoint Online without downtime?
A: Mostly yes. Staff keep using the old share while content is copied in waves. Extra passes catch files changed during the move. A short window where the old share is read-only happens at cutover for each department, and owners are told the date ahead of time.
Q: What is the maximum file size and path length in SharePoint?
A: Microsoft allows files up to 250 GB in SharePoint document libraries, and the full decoded path including the file name cannot exceed 400 characters. Long paths are the most common migration failure, so MP-365 reports and shortens them before the copy starts.
Q: How many files can one SharePoint library hold?
A: A library can hold up to 30 million files and folders. Microsoft recommends syncing no more than 300,000 files per library with the OneDrive app. MP-365 splits large shares by department or period so search, views and sync stay fast.
Q: Do we need to clean up files before migrating?
A: Yes, and it is worth the effort. Migrating duplicates and dead folders makes search worse and increases storage use. MP-365 scans for duplicates, old files and long paths, then asks owners to approve what to archive or delete before any copy starts.
Q: Will our users still see a folder structure?
A: Yes, but a lighter one. MP-365 keeps folders where people browse and adds metadata, such as project or document type, where people search or filter. Views let users group files in several ways without copying them. Training shows the new habits.
Q: Do users need the OneDrive app to work with SharePoint files?
A: No, but it helps. Users can work in the browser or in Office apps directly. The OneDrive sync app gives offline access and a File Explorer view for libraries they choose. MP-365 explains which libraries to sync and which to open online.
Q: Can version history replace our old backups?
A: No, not completely. Version history shows earlier edits of a file, and the recycle bin restores deleted files for a limited period. These help with mistakes but are not a full backup strategy. MP-365 does not provide backup services or managed IT.

To migrate file share to SharePoint Online well, clean up first, design for how people search, and set permissions at the library level. MP-365 handles the scan, the design and the staged copy, and trains your team to run the result.

## SharePoint Extranet and Vendor Portals
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/sharepoint/supplier-partner-portals/

A SharePoint extranet gives suppliers, subcontractors and partners one controlled place to exchange files and updates with you, instead of email attachments and personal file-sharing accounts. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that designs and builds vendor and partner portals on SharePoint Online, with a separate space for each outside company and permissions your team can explain.

bestFor: Companies that trade documents with vendors, subcontractors or partners and want one managed place, using the Microsoft 365 licenses they already have.
includes: Portal design, one site per partner or program, guest access setup, permission groups, document libraries and lists, onboarding and offboarding steps, and owner training.
notIncluded: Identity and access management services, cybersecurity services, custom software development, ERP implementation and Microsoft licenses.
howItStarts: A discovery call about who you share with and what moves back and forth, followed by a written portal design covering sites, access and ownership.

### What is a SharePoint extranet?
A SharePoint extranet is a set of SharePoint sites that people outside your company can open after signing in. Typical users are suppliers, contractors, distributors and customers' project teams. It is often called a vendor portal when the outside users are suppliers.
A good extranet is not one big shared folder. It is a group of small sites, each with a clear owner on your side, a short list of outside users and only the content that company needs.

### Problems a vendor portal solves
- Files travel by email: purchase documents, specifications and insurance certificates sit in inboxes, and nobody knows which version is current.
- Everyone shares through personal tools: staff use consumer file-sharing accounts, so IT cannot see who has what.
- Onboarding is slow: each new supplier needs a manual set of emails and folder invitations.
- Offboarding is forgotten: people from past contracts keep access because nobody removes them.
- Suppliers see too much: one shared folder lets one company see another company's files.

### How do you share files with vendors in SharePoint?
The safest pattern is one SharePoint site per outside company or program, shared with named guests. MP-365 builds this pattern and sets the rules that keep it clean.

### One site for each partner or program
Separate sites keep each company's content apart. Microsoft notes that when you share a folder with several guests, those guests can see each other's names in the Manage Access panel. Separate sites avoid that exposure and make offboarding simple.

### Sharing settings at organization and site level
SharePoint external sharing is set at both the organization level and the site level, and the more restrictive setting always applies. Microsoft recommends keeping confidential information in sites with external sharing turned off and creating separate sites for external sharing. MP-365 follows that rule when it lays out your tenant.

### How outside users sign in
SharePoint can share through Microsoft Entra B2B integration, which always creates a guest account, or through SharePoint external authentication. Which one fits depends on your policies. MP-365 explains the trade-offs, configures the chosen one with your administrators, and avoids anonymous Anyone links for portal content.

### SharePoint extranet or Power Pages portal?
Question | SharePoint extranet | Power Pages portal
Main purpose | Exchange and co-author files, share lists and updates | Let outside users sign in and work with business data, such as records, forms and statuses
Where data lives | In SharePoint libraries and lists | In Dataverse, often alongside Dynamics 365
Who it suits | Suppliers and partners who mostly send and receive documents | Customers, dealers or suppliers who submit requests, track cases or update records
Look and feel | SharePoint site pages with your branding | A portal with its own pages, forms and sign-in options
Effort to build | Lower; uses standard SharePoint features | Higher; needs data model design and form setup

### Should a vendor portal use SharePoint or Power Pages?
Use SharePoint when the main need is file sharing and simple lists, and use Power Pages when outside users must work with structured business data. If suppliers only need to download specifications and upload certificates, SharePoint is enough. If they must submit orders, track cases or edit records in Dynamics 365, Power Pages is the better base. MP-365 builds both and will tell you which fits.

### How MP-365 builds a SharePoint extranet
1. Map who shares what: List each type of outside user, what they send and receive, and who inside your company owns the relationship.
2. Design the site model: Choose one site per company or per program. Decide which libraries, lists and pages each site needs and how templates will be reused.
3. Choose the sharing settings: Set organization and site sharing levels, guest sign-in method and rules for link sharing, with your administrators.
4. Create permission groups: Define who on your side owns and edits, who on the partner side contributes, and who may only read.
5. Build a template and one live site: Create a reusable site template and one real partner site. Test with a friendly supplier before others join.
6. Add automation: Use Power Automate for onboarding requests, document approvals and notifications to your owners when partners upload files.
7. Onboard partners in groups: Send clear guest invitations with a short how-to. Add companies in batches so questions can be handled in time.
8. Hand off and set a review routine: Train your owners and document a regular check of who still has access. Offboarding is part of the design, not an afterthought.

### What you get from MP-365
- Portal design: a written site model showing which sites exist, who owns them and who is invited.
- Partner site template: a repeatable site with libraries, lists, a landing page and permissions already set.
- Sharing configuration: settings documented at organization and site level.
- Onboarding and offboarding flow: a request form and approval built with Power Automate, plus a removal checklist.
- Guest guide: a one-page how-to partners can follow to sign in and upload.
- Owner training: a working session for your people who manage partner sites.

### Microsoft products used in a SharePoint extranet
Product | Role
SharePoint Online | Hosts partner sites, document libraries and lists.
Microsoft Entra B2B | Provides guest accounts so outside users can sign in with their own work email.
Microsoft 365 groups | Group-connected team sites use group membership to control access.
Power Automate | Handles onboarding requests, approvals and upload notices.
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels | Label and protect sensitive documents; see Microsoft Purview and permission models.

### What guests can and cannot do
Guests who are not licensed in your organization are limited to basic collaboration, according to Microsoft's external sharing documentation. They can view and edit documents in the browser and work within the permission level you give them. If a guest needs more, such as OneDrive storage or creating a Power Automate flow, they need an appropriate license. MP-365 designs portals so that guests need nothing beyond basic access.

### What does a SharePoint extranet cost?
Cost depends on the number of partner types, the number of sites, the amount of automation and your approval rules. A template-based design keeps the cost of each added partner low. MP-365 gives a written estimate after discovery; the pricing page explains engagement models. Microsoft license fees are separate.

### When a SharePoint extranet is not the right fit
A SharePoint extranet is not the right fit for large public audiences, for sign-ups from unknown users, or for transaction-heavy portals; Power Pages fits those better. It is also not a substitute for security operations. MP-365 designs sharing and permission models but does not provide cybersecurity or identity and access management services.

### Related SharePoint services
Internal staff often need an intranet next to the portal, so that partner content and internal content stay on separate sites. See all services under SharePoint & Intranets.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you share files securely with vendors in SharePoint?
A: Create one SharePoint site per vendor or program, share it with named guests, and give them the lowest permission level they need. Avoid anonymous Anyone links for business files. MP-365 also sets a routine for removing access when contracts end.
Q: What is a SharePoint extranet?
A: A SharePoint extranet is a set of SharePoint sites that external users, such as suppliers, subcontractors and partners, can open after signing in. It gives you a managed place to exchange documents, lists and updates, with each outside company seeing only its own content.
Q: Should a vendor portal use SharePoint or Power Pages?
A: Use SharePoint when vendors mainly exchange files and simple lists. Use Power Pages when they must sign in and work with business data, such as submitting orders or updating records in Dynamics 365. MP-365 builds both and recommends one after a discovery call.
Q: Can suppliers see each other's files?
A: Not if the portal is designed correctly. Each company gets its own site, and nobody from another company is a member. Microsoft notes that guests invited to the same shared folder can see each other's names, so MP-365 avoids sharing one folder with many companies.
Q: Do external users need a Microsoft license?
A: Usually no. Microsoft states that unlicensed guests can do basic collaboration, such as viewing and editing documents in the browser. They need a license for things like OneDrive storage or creating a Power Automate flow. MP-365 designs partner sites to stay within basic access.
Q: How are vendors added and removed?
A: MP-365 builds an onboarding request and approval flow in Power Automate, so adding a vendor follows a set path with a named owner. Removal is part of the design: a checklist and a review routine make sure old contract partners lose access.
Q: Can we control what external users can download or edit?
A: Yes. Permission levels let you give read, contribute or edit access per site or library. Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview can add protection to specific documents. MP-365 recommends the simplest model that fits and documents it so your owners understand it.
Q: Does the vendor portal work with Dynamics 365?
A: It can. Documents related to accounts or orders can live in SharePoint and link to Dynamics 365 records, and approvals can run through Power Automate. If vendors need to update Dynamics 365 data directly, Power Pages is usually a better fit than SharePoint alone.
Q: Is a SharePoint vendor portal an alternative to Teams shared channels?
A: Sometimes. Teams shared channels suit active, chat-based projects with one or two partners. A SharePoint extranet suits many partners, formal document exchange and a stable structure. Both store files in SharePoint, so MP-365 can use them together.
Q: How much does a SharePoint extranet cost?
A: The cost depends on the number of partner types, sites, automations and approval rules. Using a site template lowers the cost of each added partner. MP-365 gives a written estimate after discovery. Microsoft licenses are billed separately by Microsoft or your license provider.

A SharePoint extranet works when every outside company has its own space, a named owner on your side and a way to be removed when the work ends. MP-365 designs and builds that structure on the Microsoft 365 licenses you already own.

## SharePoint Information Architecture and Search
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/sharepoint/information-architecture/

SharePoint information architecture is the way your sites, libraries, content types, metadata, navigation and permissions are organized so people can find the right file without asking a colleague. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that redesigns SharePoint structure and search for mid-size and enterprise teams whose staff say they cannot find anything.

bestFor: Organizations whose SharePoint or Microsoft 365 content is hard to find, duplicated or inconsistently labeled, and teams planning an intranet or migration who want the structure right first.
includes: Content and site review, site and hub model, content types and metadata, term sets, navigation design, search configuration, library templates, naming rules and owner guidance.
notIncluded: Custom software development, cybersecurity services, ERP implementation, content writing for every page and Microsoft licenses.
howItStarts: A discovery call about what people cannot find, followed by a review of your busiest sites and a few user searches to see where the structure fails.

### What is information architecture in SharePoint?
SharePoint information architecture is the plan for where content lives, how it is labeled and how people reach it. It covers site types, hub sites, libraries, content types, columns, term sets, navigation and permissions. It decides whether a person finds a contract in seconds or gives up and emails a colleague.
Information architecture is not the same as design. Design is how a page looks. Architecture is how the information is organized so that navigation, search and filters all point to the same files.

### Why SharePoint search is not working for your team
What people see | Likely cause | Fix
A new column does not appear as a filter, or its values are not found | Search has not re-crawled the library since the column was added | Request re-indexing of the library after all changes are made, and map the column to a managed property
A colleague sees more results than I do | Search results are trimmed to what each person is allowed to open | Review permissions rather than search settings, and fix overshared or locked-down areas
Numbers inside Excel files are not found | Microsoft does not index purely numeric data in Excel files, though text such as PO123456789 is indexed | Add the number to a metadata column or file name pattern that search can read
Product codes with dashes or symbols fail | Search breaks identifiers into pieces differently when indexing and querying | Map the code to its own managed property and adjust tokenization settings
Results show empty or odd titles | Several title sources compete and the highest-ranked mapped value wins | Set titles in a required column and use consistent file naming
The same file appears in many places | Content was copied between sites instead of linked or stored once | Pick one home per file and link to it from other sites

### Why can't employees find files in SharePoint?
Employees usually cannot find files in SharePoint because the structure grew without a plan, not because the search engine is broken. Typical causes are sites created for every request, folders nested many levels deep, files with no metadata, copies in several places, and permissions that hide content from the people who need it.
Microsoft's intranet planning guidance describes three situations people are in: they know a file exists and where it is, they know it exists but not where, or they do not know whether it exists. Navigation helps the first, search the second and discovery features the third. MP-365 designs for all three.

### How do metadata and search work together in SharePoint?
Metadata tells search what each file is, and search only returns what is in its index and what the user may open. When someone adds a site column to a library, SharePoint's search crawler creates a matching crawled property and an automatic managed property. MP-365 sets this up deliberately so the right fields can be searched, filtered and refined.

### Content types and site columns
A content type defines a kind of document, such as a contract or a safety report, with the columns it must carry. Site columns are reusable fields. Using the same columns across libraries lets one search or view find matching files across many sites.

### Crawled and managed properties
Search reads crawled properties, and only managed properties go into the index. In SharePoint in Microsoft 365, custom managed properties can only be text or yes/no. For other types, such as dates or numbers, MP-365 renames an unused built-in property with an alias and maps it to the column. Microsoft warns against changing the mappings of default properties, because other Microsoft 365 features depend on them.

### Re-indexing after changes
Search schema changes take effect only after content is re-crawled. For existing libraries, you request re-indexing in the library's advanced settings. Microsoft notes this can create heavy load on the search system, so MP-365 batches changes and re-indexes once.

### SharePoint site structure best practices
- One site per unit of work: give each team, function or project its own site, so permissions and lifecycle are managed separately.
- Hub sites instead of deep subsites: Microsoft recommends hubs for organizing intranet sites, because hubs link sites without locking them into a hierarchy that breaks when the company reorganizes.
- Libraries for topics, sites for owners: do not create a site for every topic. A library with good metadata often serves search better.
- Keep navigation short: Microsoft recommends no more than 100 links in navigation, even though the technical limit is 500 child links per level.
- Name things once: use one naming rule for sites, libraries and files, written down and enforced through templates.

### SharePoint navigation design that people can follow
Good SharePoint navigation shows where things are in the terms staff use, not how IT built them. Hub navigation can have up to three levels, but fewer is better. Use department names and common tasks as labels, and test them by asking people where they would look for a handful of real files.
Audience targeting can hide links that are irrelevant to a group. Private sites listed in shared navigation can show people an access request they cannot use, so MP-365 decides case by case whether to show them.

### A SharePoint metadata strategy people follow
- Few required fields: start with three or four, such as document type, owner and project. People skip long forms.
- Shared vocabularies: use term sets in the managed metadata service for values reused across sites, such as departments or regions.
- Defaults where possible: set default values by library or folder so users enter less.
- Content types for document kinds: a contract has different fields than a meeting note.
- Views over folders: build filtered and grouped views so one file shows up in the places people look.

### How MP-365 improves SharePoint structure and search
1. Find out what people cannot find: Gather ten to twenty real searches and tasks from different departments. Time how long each takes today.
2. Review sites, libraries and usage: Inventory sites, owners, sizes, activity and permissions. Flag duplicates, empty sites and content with no owner.
3. Design the target model: Draft the site and hub map, content types, columns, term sets and navigation on paper before changing anything live.
4. Set naming and metadata rules: Agree short rules owners can remember. Build library templates that apply them by default.
5. Configure search properties: Map columns to managed properties, set up refiners and result scopes, and tune key libraries.
6. Test with the same searches: Run the original tasks again with real users. Fix labels and navigation where people still hesitate.
7. Roll out by area: Apply the model to one department first, adjust, then extend to others. Re-index once per round of changes.
8. Train owners and hand off: Show site owners how to add content types, keep metadata clean and request changes. Document the rules.

### What you get from MP-365
- Findability baseline: before-and-after results for the real searches your staff run.
- Site and hub map: a diagram of sites, hubs, owners and permissions.
- Content type and metadata model: documented columns, content types and term sets.
- Navigation design: global, hub and site navigation with labels tested on users.
- Search configuration: managed property mappings, refiners and any query rules required.
- Library templates and naming guide: ready-to-use patterns for owners.
- Governance note: who may create sites, who approves new columns and how often to review.

Product | Role
SharePoint Online | Sites, libraries, content types, columns and the managed metadata service.
Microsoft Search | The search experience across SharePoint and Microsoft 365 content.
SharePoint admin center | Hub sites, search schema, site settings and sharing controls.

### Why good structure matters before Copilot

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is information architecture in SharePoint?
A: Information architecture in SharePoint is the plan for how sites, hubs, libraries, content types, metadata, navigation and permissions fit together. A good one lets people reach the right file through navigation, search or filters. A poor one produces duplicate files and unanswered requests for where things are.
Q: Why can't employees find files in SharePoint?
A: Usually the structure is the cause: many sites with no plan, deep folders, files without metadata, copies in several places and permissions that hide content. Search can only return what is indexed and what the person is allowed to open. Fixing structure and metadata solves most cases.
Q: How do metadata and search work together in SharePoint?
A: Search crawls files and their columns, maps them to managed properties and builds an index. Metadata columns become searchable, filterable and refinable when mapped correctly. Changes take effect after content is re-crawled, so MP-365 requests re-indexing once after a batch of changes.
Q: Why is SharePoint search not working?
A: Common causes are a library that has not been re-indexed after a new column, permission trimming that hides files from some users, numbers inside Excel files that are not indexed, and poor titles. MP-365 tests real searches to find which cause applies before changing anything.
Q: Should we use hub sites or subsites?
A: Use hub sites for most organizations. Microsoft recommends them for intranets because they connect sites through links, so a reorganization does not break the structure. Subsites remain supported, but they tie content to a hierarchy and share features across the whole site collection.
Q: How many levels of navigation should a SharePoint site have?
A: Keep it to two levels where you can. Hub navigation supports up to three, and Microsoft recommends no more than 100 links. Long menus slow people down. MP-365 tests labels with staff by asking where they would look for real files.
Q: What is a good SharePoint metadata strategy?
A: Use a small set of required columns, shared term sets for values reused across sites, content types for each document kind, and defaults to reduce typing. Add fields only when someone will filter or search by them. MP-365 starts with three or four and expands later.
Q: Can we fix search without moving content?
A: Often yes. Mapping columns, adding titles and metadata, adjusting navigation and removing duplicates can improve results on existing sites. If the content sits in the wrong places or has no structure, restructuring comes first. MP-365 reviews your busiest sites to decide.
Q: Does MP-365 redesign SharePoint sites after an intranet or migration?
A: Yes. Structure work can follow a migration or intranet launch, or be done before to prevent problems. MP-365 treats it as a separate, small project with measured searches before and after, so you can see whether findability improved.
Q: Does information architecture affect Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: Yes. Copilot only uses content a person can access, so oversharing becomes visible in answers. Clear structure, owners and labels also make good content easier to find. The AI data governance audit reviews access before rollout, and structure work supports it.

Good SharePoint information architecture makes the right file easy to find through navigation, search and filters that all agree. MP-365 reviews what people cannot find today, redesigns the structure and metadata, and tests the result with the same searches.

## Microsoft Copilot Consulting and Rollout
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/

Microsoft Copilot consulting from MP-365 covers four things: checking that your data is ready, rolling Copilot out to the right people, building agents that work with Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 data, and reviewing who can reach what. This page compares the five services in the area so you can pick a starting point.

### What Microsoft Copilot consulting includes
Microsoft Copilot consulting is the work between buying Copilot licenses and getting reliable value from them. MP-365 (Modern Partners 365), a Microsoft Solutions Partner, handles that work for mid-size and enterprise companies that run Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365.
The scope is deliberately narrow. MP-365 works with Microsoft Copilot and the Microsoft tools around it. It does not offer general AI strategy, and it does not build AI on non-Microsoft platforms. If you are looking for broader Microsoft 365 consulting, the Services hub shows the other areas.

### The five Copilot services compared
Service | Best for | Typical outcome | Starting point

### Which Copilot service to start with
Start with readiness or the data access review in almost every case. Copilot answers from content that each user can already open, so messy permissions become visible the day Copilot goes live.
Pick the sales agents first only when the work is limited to Dynamics 365 Sales and your lead data is clean. Pick custom agents first when one named process, such as answering order status questions, is the whole reason for the project.
Skip the early steps only if you have already cleaned up site permissions and sharing links. Most mid-size tenants have not.

### How MP-365 approaches a Copilot project
1. Pick one business outcome: Agree on the team, the task and the measure of success before any license or agent is touched.
2. Review data and access: Check which SharePoint sites, Teams and OneDrive content Copilot would reach, and who can open it today.
3. Fix the highest-risk permissions: Remove broad sharing, assign owners to orphaned sites and tighten access where the review found gaps.
4. Pilot with a small group: Turn Copilot on for a defined set of users with real tasks, and collect what works and what does not.
5. Add agents where the pilot shows a need: Configure the Dynamics 365 agents or build a Copilot Studio agent for the one process that earned it.
6. Train and hand off: Teach each role the prompts and habits that fit its work, then document what MP-365 set up.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What does Microsoft Copilot consulting include?
A: Microsoft Copilot consulting includes readiness checks, a data access and permissions review, a controlled rollout, Dynamics 365 sales agents, custom agents built in Copilot Studio, and Copilot Cowork rollout. MP-365 covers Microsoft tools only. It does not provide general AI strategy.
Q: What should a company do before rolling out Copilot?
A: Review who can access which files, then fix broad sharing first. Copilot returns content that each user is already allowed to open, so oversharing shows up quickly. Also choose a pilot group, define success measures and decide who owns training. The readiness assessment covers all three.
Q: What does a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout cost?
A: Cost has two parts: Microsoft's license fees and consulting fees. Microsoft sets license prices, and they are separate from MP-365's work. Consulting depends on scope, such as the number of sites reviewed and agents built. The pricing page explains how MP-365 engages.
Q: Does MP-365 sell Copilot licenses?
A: No. MP-365 does not resell Microsoft licenses or manage CSP subscriptions. You buy Microsoft 365 Copilot from Microsoft or your usual license provider. MP-365 advises on who should get seats first and how to configure the tenant for them.
Q: Can Copilot show people files they should not see?
A: Copilot does not bypass permissions. According to Microsoft's 2026 documentation, it can only summarize or reference content the user is authorized to access. The risk is that many users are authorized to open files nobody intended them to read. A data access review finds those cases.
Q: What is the difference between Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio?
A: Microsoft 365 Copilot is the assistant that works across your Microsoft 365 apps and data. Copilot Studio is the low-code tool for building your own agents that use your knowledge sources and connect to business systems. Companies often use both, with agents built in Studio.
Q: Which Copilot service should we start with?
A: Start with readiness or the AI Data Governance Audit unless you have already cleaned up sharing and permissions. If your team lives in Dynamics 365 Sales and the lead data is accurate, the Dynamics 365 sales agents can run in parallel with that cleanup.
Q: Does MP-365 build AI outside the Microsoft stack?
A: No. MP-365 works with Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio and the Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 data they use. It does not build models, set general AI strategy or integrate non-Microsoft AI platforms. If a request falls outside Microsoft tools, MP-365 will say so on the first call.
Q: How do Dynamics 365 agents relate to Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: They are separate products that work together. Dynamics 365 Sales includes agents such as the Sales Qualification Agent. Microsoft also offers a Sales agent inside Microsoft 365 Copilot that lets sellers query CRM data in plain language. Both depend on clean CRM data and sensible access.
Q: Who is Copilot consulting for, and who is it not for?
A: It suits mid-size and enterprise companies that already use Microsoft 365 or Dynamics 365 and want a structured rollout. It is a poor fit for companies without Microsoft 365, for those wanting a non-Microsoft AI build, or for a single user who only needs to switch Copilot on.

Microsoft Copilot consulting works best when the data comes first and the agents come second. Pick the service that matches your situation from the table above, or talk through your setup with MP-365 and we will recommend a starting point.

## Microsoft 365 Copilot Readiness Assessment
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/readiness/

A Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment checks your permissions, sharing, content and people before you switch Copilot on. MP-365 runs it for mid-size and enterprise companies, and the result is a ranked list of fixes plus a pilot plan.

bestFor: IT leaders and business sponsors who have bought, or are about to buy, Microsoft 365 Copilot and want a safe first launch.
includes: Permission and sharing review, content cleanup priorities, pilot group selection, role-based training plan and a written readiness report.
notIncluded: Microsoft license sales, cybersecurity services, managed IT support and non-Microsoft AI tools.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your tenant, your Copilot plans and the teams that will use it first.

### What a Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment is
A Copilot readiness assessment is a structured review of your Microsoft 365 tenant before Copilot users arrive. It is one part of MP-365's wider Microsoft Copilot consulting, and it answers three questions: what could Copilot reach, who is it ready for, and what must change first.
Microsoft states that Copilot grounds its answers in data users already have permission to access. That sentence is the reason for the assessment. Any file that is shared too widely becomes easy to find the moment someone asks Copilot a question.

### Problems a readiness assessment solves
- "Our SharePoint permissions are a mess." Years of sharing links, old project sites and broad groups mean nobody can say who sees what.
- "We bought licenses and nobody uses them." Seats sit idle because no pilot group, training or success measure was set.
- "HR and finance files worry me." Sensitive libraries sit in sites shared with the whole company.
- "Copilot answers are poor." Outdated, duplicate and unlabeled documents produce weak results.
- "Leadership wants a date, and IT wants a plan." Sponsors and administrators have no shared list of blockers.

### How MP-365 runs the readiness assessment
1. Confirm scope and goals: Agree which departments, workloads and use cases the first Copilot users will cover.
2. Pull the access reports: Run SharePoint and OneDrive permission, sharing link and sensitivity label reports for your tenant.
3. Rank the exposure: Sort sites by how many people can open them, whether external guests are present and how sensitive the content looks.
4. Review content quality: Spot inactive sites, duplicate libraries and files without owners that would dilute Copilot answers.
5. Choose the pilot group: Select users and tasks where Copilot is likely to save time, and set the measures you will track.
6. Write the remediation plan: List each fix, its owner and its priority, from quick wins to tasks that need site owner input.
7. Present and hand over: Walk IT and business sponsors through the findings and leave a plan your team can execute or MP-365 can carry out.

### What MP-365 checks before Copilot goes live
Area | Question we ask | Typical fix
Site permissions | Which sites are open to large groups or the whole organization? | Replace broad groups with named owners and members
Sharing links | Where have people created many new links recently? | Remove stale links and set tighter defaults
Sensitivity labels | Is sensitive content labeled where it lives? | Define labels and apply them to priority libraries
Site ownership | Does every active site have an accountable owner? | Assign owners and archive inactive sites
Content quality | Are the files Copilot would cite current and unique? | Retire duplicates and clean up library structure
Users and training | Who needs Copilot first, and what will they do with it? | Select a pilot group and write role-based guides

### How do you fix oversharing before deploying Copilot?
You fix oversharing by finding the widest-exposed sites first, then narrowing access with the owners' approval. Microsoft's SharePoint Advanced Management includes data access governance reports for this, and it can start site access reviews that ask site owners to confirm members and sharing.
For sites that cannot be fixed immediately, Microsoft offers Restricted Content Discovery, which stops chosen sites from surfacing in Copilot while the cleanup continues. MP-365 treats that as a temporary measure and not as the fix.

### Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption after the assessment
Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption depends on habits more than on settings. The assessment ends with an adoption plan with three parts.

### Start with a defined pilot group
A pilot of users with real, repeatable tasks gives you evidence. Meeting summaries, document drafting and email catch-up are common starting tasks.

### Train by role, not by feature
A salesperson, an accountant and a project manager need different prompts. MP-365 writes short guides for each role, built on your own documents and processes.

### Measure and review usage
Choose two or three measures before the pilot starts, such as active users and time saved on one named task. Review them with the sponsor, then decide who gets seats next.

### What you get from the assessment
- Readiness report: a plain-language summary of findings for business sponsors and IT.
- Exposure ranking: sites ordered by how widely they are shared and how sensitive they look.
- Remediation plan: each fix with an owner and a priority.
- Pilot plan: the user group, use cases and measures for the first rollout.
- Training outline: role-based guidance your team can reuse.
- Handover session: a walkthrough with your administrators.

### Microsoft tools involved in the assessment
The work uses the SharePoint admin center, the Microsoft 365 admin center and SharePoint Advanced Management. Microsoft says SharePoint Advanced Management is included with a Microsoft Copilot license. Where sensitivity labels are in play, the work touches Microsoft Purview. See Microsoft Purview and permission models for the follow-on work.

### Proof: moving messy files into governed libraries
MP-365 moved a client's file shares with hundreds of thousands of files into organized SharePoint libraries with metadata, version control and workflows. That work is the same cleanup readiness points to: clear structure, known owners and files that are easy to classify.
You can see named clients on the MP-365 clients page.

### When a readiness assessment is not the right fit
A full assessment is more than you need if you have a small tenant, a handful of sites and clear permissions already. In that case a short permissions and data access review may be enough. It is also the wrong tool if you want help choosing between AI vendors, because MP-365 works only with Microsoft Copilot.

### Related Copilot services
After the assessment, many clients move to Copilot Cowork for multistep tasks, custom Copilot agents for a single process, or the Dynamics 365 sales agents for lead work. Effort for any of these depends on tenant size; the pricing page explains how MP-365 engages.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is a Copilot readiness assessment?
A: A Copilot readiness assessment reviews permissions, sharing, content quality and user plans before Copilot goes live. It produces a ranked list of fixes, a pilot plan and a training outline. MP-365 treats permission cleanup as the first priority because Copilot works with whatever each user can already open.
Q: How do you fix oversharing before deploying Copilot?
A: Find the most widely exposed sites, confirm each owner, then remove broad groups and stale sharing links. Microsoft's data access governance reports and site access reviews support this. For urgent cases, Restricted Content Discovery can hide a site from Copilot while the real fix is made.
Q: How long does Copilot readiness take?
A: It depends on the number of sites, the volume of shared content and how many teams join the pilot. A small tenant moves quickly, while a tenant with years of sprawl takes longer. MP-365 sets the schedule after scoping, once the first reports show how much needs attention.
Q: Do we need a readiness assessment before buying Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: No, but it helps. Doing it before you buy lets you size the pilot and avoid paying for idle seats. Doing it after you buy still works. The only poor order is launching to everyone first and discovering overshared files from users' prompts.
Q: What does the assessment cost?
A: Cost depends on tenant size and scope, and MP-365 does not publish a fixed price. Microsoft's license fees are separate and are paid to Microsoft or your license provider. The pricing page explains how engagements are structured, and a discovery call gives you a scoped answer.
Q: Does the assessment change any of our settings?
A: No. The assessment reads reports and configuration, then writes findings. Changes happen only after you approve the remediation plan, and site owners confirm access decisions for their own sites. MP-365 can carry out approved fixes or hand the plan to your administrators.
Q: What licenses do we need for the assessment?
A: Microsoft states that SharePoint Advanced Management is included with a Microsoft Copilot license, and several data access governance reports depend on it. If your tenant has no Copilot license yet, MP-365 will check what reporting is available to you and tell you what is missing.
Q: What is Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption planning?
A: It is the plan for getting people to use Copilot well after launch. It covers who joins the pilot, which tasks they try, how they are trained and which measures show success. MP-365 builds this plan at the end of the assessment, using your own roles and documents.
Q: Is this a security assessment?
A: No. The assessment reviews data access and permissions in SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft 365, so Copilot answers from the right content. It is not a cybersecurity service or a compliance certification. For CRM roles, see the Dynamics 365 security roles audit.
Q: Who should be involved from our side?
A: Involve a business sponsor, a SharePoint or Microsoft 365 administrator and one leader from each pilot department. Site owners join briefly to confirm access on their sites. The total time asked of each person is small, but owner decisions are what keep the cleanup moving.

A Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment turns a vague worry about oversharing into a ranked list your team can act on. If you are planning a Copilot pilot, MP-365 can scope the assessment around your tenant and your first use cases.

## Dynamics 365 Sales Agents and AI for Sales
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/sales-agents/

Microsoft Dynamics 365 AI for sales means the agents built into Dynamics 365 Sales, such as the Sales Qualification Agent, plus the Sales agent that sellers use inside Microsoft 365 Copilot. MP-365 sets them up on top of your CRM data, tests them in a sandbox and trains your sellers to work with what they hand over.

bestFor: Sales leaders with steady inbound leads in Dynamics 365 Sales who want less manual research and faster follow-up.
includes: Agent selection, CRM data checks, Sales Qualification Agent setup, hand-off rules, sandbox testing, seller training and monitoring guidance.
notIncluded: ERP implementation, license resale, non-Microsoft AI tools and managed help desk support.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your lead sources, your current Dynamics 365 Sales setup and how sellers qualify leads today.

### What are Dynamics 365 sales agents?
Dynamics 365 sales agents are AI agents inside Dynamics 365 Sales that research leads and opportunities, draft or send outreach, and surface risks without a seller starting each task. Microsoft's documentation describes them as agents that autonomously research and engage with leads and opportunities.
They are part of MP-365's Microsoft Copilot consulting work, and they run on your own CRM records. Weak CRM data produces weak agent output, which is why setup starts with the data and not the agent.

### Microsoft Dynamics 365 AI for sales: the agents compared
Agent | What it does | Where it fits
Sales Qualification Agent | Researches leads, checks fit against your target customer profile, drafts outreach and hands promising leads to sellers | Teams with more inbound leads than sellers can research
Sales Opportunity Agent | Researches open opportunities, shows emerging risks and highlights promising deals | Managers who review pipeline by hand
Sales Close Agent | Engages customers near the end of the cycle, recommends products and handles objections | Transactional sales with repeatable offers
Sales Research Agent | Answers complex questions about sales data in natural language | Leaders and analysts who now request custom reports
Recommended Actions Agent | Gives sellers prioritized next actions on their opportunities | Sellers who lose track of follow-up
Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot | Lets sellers query CRM, email and meeting data in plain language | Sellers who work mostly in Outlook and Teams

### Which sales agent to start with
Start with the Sales Qualification Agent if lead volume is your bottleneck. Start with the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot if sellers waste time searching across CRM pages and inboxes.
Microsoft labels some of these agents as preview, and availability differs by region. MP-365 checks the current status for your tenant before recommending one, so you do not build a process around a feature that is not ready for production.

### What does the Sales Qualification Agent do?
The Sales Qualification Agent researches each assigned lead using CRM data and public sources, scores its fit against your target customer profile and prepares outreach. It does not replace the seller's judgment. Microsoft states the agent is designed to be a productivity tool.
It runs in one of two modes. Your organization deploys one mode at a time.

### Research-only mode
In research-only mode the agent researches leads, checks them against the target customer profile and generates an outreach email. Sellers read the insights and send the email themselves. Choose this mode first when your team is nervous about automated contact.

### Research and engage mode
In research and engage mode the agent also sends outreach, follows up, detects purchase interest and checks BANT criteria (budget, authority, need, timeline). Leads that meet your hand-off rules go to a seller, and the rest are disqualified. Microsoft allows an upgrade from research-only to engage later, but not the reverse.

### Copilot for Sales and Dynamics 365 sales agents
Copilot for Sales is the name many people still search for. Microsoft documents it today as the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, a conversational agent that works across Microsoft 365 apps and your connected CRM. It answers questions and drafts emails for the seller who asks.
The Dynamics 365 sales agents work differently: they run inside the CRM and act on leads in the background. Many teams use both. MP-365 sets them up so they draw on the same clean records and the same security roles.

### Problems AI sales agents can solve
- Idle leads: inbound leads from web forms, events and webinars sit in the CRM without a first touch.
- Manual research: sellers open several tabs to learn about a company before one email.
- Slow hand-off: marketing says a lead is ready, but sellers disagree and the lead goes cold.
- Unseen pipeline risk: managers find stalled deals at the quarterly review instead of during the quarter.
- Report requests: leaders wait for an analyst to answer a simple pipeline question.

### How MP-365 sets up Dynamics 365 sales agents
1. Review lead and account data: Check required fields, duplicates, lead sources and ownership so the agent works from accurate records.
2. Confirm prerequisites: Verify the Copilot Studio license, admin permissions, data policies and Exchange email synchronization the agent needs.
3. Define the target customer profile: Write down the criteria that make a lead worth a seller's time, and the hand-off rules for those who qualify.
4. Configure the agent: Set selection criteria, email instructions, assignment rules and knowledge sources, and check roles for custom security setups.
5. Test in a sandbox: Run the agent on a small set of leads in a test environment and review every email and hand-off decision.
6. Move to production: Export the agent as a solution and import it into production, then start with a narrow segment of leads.
7. Train sellers and supervisors: Show sellers how to work handed-over leads and show supervisors how to monitor the agent's activity.

### What you get
- Agent recommendation: which Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 agents fit your sales process.
- Data fixes: a short list of CRM data issues to correct before launch.
- Configured agent: target customer profile, selection criteria, hand-off and assignment rules.
- Tested outreach: email instructions reviewed against real leads.
- Seller guide: how to work handed-over leads and give feedback.
- Monitoring routine: what supervisors should check and how often.

### Microsoft products involved
The work uses Dynamics 365 Sales, Copilot Studio (the platform the Sales Qualification Agent runs on), Microsoft Dataverse, Exchange Online for email synchronization and Microsoft 365 Copilot for the Sales agent. Microsoft says the Sales Qualification Agent uses capacity assigned to your tenant, either prepaid or pay-as-you-go, and that capacity is billed by Microsoft.
The agent's output depends on your pipeline setup, so most clients pair this work with Dynamics 365 Sales consulting and a clear lead management and attribution process.

### Proof: one lead process with live dashboards
MP-365 built lead tracking for a client with one lead process and dashboards for marketing and sales leaders. The aim was to replace spreadsheet reporting with a single, trusted view of every lead.
That work is the foundation sales agents need: consistent lead sources, statuses and owners. See the client results page for named projects.

### When sales agents are not the right fit
Sales agents are a poor fit when lead volume is low, when your CRM data is unreliable or when your sellers do not use Dynamics 365 Sales. Fix the process first in those cases. They also do not suit teams that cannot allow automated email, though research-only mode may still help. A broader readiness assessment is the better first step if your main worry is data access.

### Related Copilot work
If your process needs behavior the standard agents do not offer, custom Copilot agents can fill the gap. MP-365 can discuss scope and cost on a call, and the pricing page explains how engagements work.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What are Dynamics 365 sales agents?
A: Dynamics 365 sales agents are AI agents inside Dynamics 365 Sales that research and engage with leads and opportunities. Microsoft's list includes the Sales Qualification, Sales Opportunity, Sales Close, Sales Research and Recommended Actions agents. They work from your CRM data and follow rules your administrators set.
Q: What does the Sales Qualification Agent do?
A: It researches each assigned lead from CRM and public sources, checks fit against your target customer profile and drafts outreach. In research and engage mode it also sends emails, follows up and hands qualified leads to sellers. Leads that do not qualify are disqualified, with supervisors notified.
Q: How is Copilot for Sales different from Dynamics 365 sales agents?
A: Copilot for Sales is now documented as the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot. It answers a seller's questions and drafts emails across Outlook, Teams and the CRM. Dynamics 365 sales agents work inside the CRM and act on leads in the background without a prompt.
Q: What do we need before turning on the Sales Qualification Agent?
A: Microsoft lists admin permissions in Dynamics 365 Sales, a Copilot Studio license, the modern Sales Hub interface, allowed data policy connectors and Exchange server-side synchronization. Without email synchronization, the agent does not generate outreach emails. MP-365 checks each item before configuration starts.
Q: Can the agent send emails without a seller approving them?
A: Only in research and engage mode. In research-only mode, the agent drafts the email and the seller sends it. Engage mode sends outreach autonomously, so MP-365 recommends a simulation run and a small first segment of leads, then a review of the emails before widening it.
Q: How much do AI sales agents cost?
A: Microsoft bills agent usage through tenant capacity, either prepaid or pay-as-you-go, and sets those prices. MP-365's consulting fee is separate and depends on scope. The pricing page explains the engagement models. MP-365 does not resell Microsoft licenses or capacity.
Q: Do the agents work with custom security roles?
A: Yes, with extra setup. Microsoft says out-of-the-box roles such as Salesperson and Sales Manager need no changes, while custom roles need specific table permissions to work agent-handed leads. MP-365 reviews those roles during configuration so sellers can open and reassign handed-over leads.
Q: Can we test the agent before sellers see it?
A: Yes. Microsoft recommends testing at a smaller scale first, and agents can be exported as a solution and imported into another environment. MP-365 configures and tests in a sandbox, reviews the agent's emails and hand-off decisions, and then moves the agent to production.
Q: Can we switch the Sales Qualification Agent from one mode to the other?
A: You can upgrade from research-only to research and engage, but not go back. Microsoft also notes that only one mode can be deployed in an organization, and that a configured agent cannot be deleted without contacting Microsoft support. Mode choice deserves care at the start.
Q: Does the agent replace our sales development team?
A: No. Microsoft states the agent does not replace human judgment. It handles research and first contact so sellers spend time on leads that show intent. Your team still owns relationships, pricing and closing, and still reviews the leads that the agent hands over.

Microsoft Dynamics 365 AI for sales pays off when the CRM data is clean and the hand-off rules are clear. MP-365 can review your lead process, recommend the right agents and set them up with your sellers in mind.

## Custom Copilot Agents Built in Copilot Studio
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/custom-agents/

Custom Copilot agents are AI assistants you build in Microsoft Copilot Studio for one defined job, using your own knowledge sources and business systems. MP-365 designs, builds and tests them against Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 data, then trains your team to maintain them.

bestFor: Operations, sales and service leaders with one repeatable task that depends on company data and currently eats staff time.
includes: Use case selection, agent design, knowledge source and connector setup, testing, publishing to Teams or Microsoft Copilot, and team handover.
notIncluded: Custom software development, non-Microsoft AI models, general AI strategy, license resale and managed help desk support.
howItStarts: A discovery call about the process you want to improve and where its data lives today.

### What are custom Copilot agents?
Custom Copilot agents are agents you configure to answer questions and complete tasks for a specific team or process. Microsoft describes an agent as an AI assistant that follows your instructions, draws on the knowledge sources you connect and uses tools to take action.
They are one part of MP-365's Microsoft Copilot consulting. They differ from the ready-made Dynamics 365 Sales agents, which Microsoft ships for sales work. A custom agent covers the process Microsoft did not build for, such as a project status assistant or an internal policy desk.

### What is Copilot Studio used for?
Copilot Studio is Microsoft's low-code studio for building and managing agents and workflows. It is where Copilot Studio agents are created, tested and published to channels such as Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Copilot and websites.
It also provides agent flows, which have an authoring experience similar to Power Automate. A flow can run as a standalone automation or serve as a tool the agent calls. Analytics, evaluations and administration features help you watch agents once they are live.

### What a custom Copilot agent can do for sales or service teams
Team | Example job | Data it uses | Action it can take
Sales | Prepare an account briefing before a call | Dynamics 365 accounts, opportunities and notes | Draft a summary for the seller to review
Customer service | Suggest an answer from approved articles | Knowledge articles and case history in Dynamics 365 | Draft a reply or update a case through a flow
Operations | Answer questions about an internal procedure | Policy documents in SharePoint | Point to the source document and the owner
Project teams | Report on status across active projects | Project lists and documents in Microsoft 365 | Compile a status update on request
Field and facilities | Log an issue from a chat message | Forms and Dataverse tables | Create a record and notify the owner

### How MP-365 builds a custom Copilot agent
1. Choose one job: Pick a single, repeatable task with a clear owner and a way to tell whether the agent got it right.
2. Map the data: List where the answers live, who may see them and how the agent will sign in to each source.
3. Write the instructions: Define what the agent should do, what it must refuse and how it should cite its sources.
4. Connect knowledge and tools: Add SharePoint and Dynamics 365 sources, connectors and agent flows for the actions the job requires.
5. Test with real questions: Run a test set drawn from your own tickets, emails and chats, and fix the gaps before anyone else sees the agent.
6. Publish to a pilot group: Release the agent in Teams or Microsoft Copilot to a small group and collect their feedback.
7. Hand over and monitor: Train your owners to update knowledge sources and read the analytics, and document how the agent is built.

### Agent, agent flow or Power Automate?
Use an agent when people ask questions in their own words and the next step depends on what they say. Use a flow when the steps are fixed and the trigger is clear. Many solutions need both.
A flow that approves an invoice does not need an agent. An agent that decides which flow to call does. MP-365 also builds standalone automations through Power Automate workflow automation when no conversation is needed.

### What you get
- Working agent: configured in Copilot Studio and published to the channel your users already open.
- Connected data: knowledge sources and connectors set up with the access model agreed in advance.
- Test set: the questions used to check quality, kept so you can repeat the test after changes.
- Design record: instructions, data sources, connections and known limits written in plain language.
- Owner training: how to update knowledge, review analytics and request changes.
- Next-step list: further agents or actions that the pilot suggests.

### Copilot Studio consulting and development considerations
Good Copilot Studio development starts with decisions about access. For each connection, decide whether the agent acts with the signed-in user's own access or with a shared service account. A shared account can reveal more than any individual user should see.
Microsoft also notes that Copilot agents can't read files that have user-defined sensitivity label permissions. Check your labels before you promise an agent will answer from those files. A data access review catches these issues early.

### What does a custom Copilot agent cost to build?
The cost depends on the number of data sources, the actions the agent takes and the testing needed. A read-only question-answering agent costs less to build than one that updates Dynamics 365 records. MP-365 gives a scoped answer after a discovery call, and the pricing page explains the engagement models.
Microsoft bills agent usage separately, and the model depends on the type of agent. Those charges go to Microsoft and are not part of MP-365's fee.

### Proof: integrations that run on service accounts
MP-365 built reliable integrations between Dynamics 365, ERP and marketing systems with logging and alerts, service accounts instead of personal accounts and secure password storage. Agents that call business systems need the same discipline, because a connection tied to one person's login breaks when that person leaves.
Named projects are on the clients page.

### When a custom agent is not the right fit
A custom agent is the wrong choice when the process changes weekly, when the data is scattered across unmanaged files or when a ready-made agent already covers the task. A readiness check on your data comes first in those cases, and the Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment is the usual route. It is also not for projects that need a custom-coded application, which MP-365 does not build.

MP-365 uses it to build agents on Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 data.

A: It can answer questions from approved knowledge, draft account briefings or case replies, look up Dynamics 365 records and trigger flows that create or update records. Sellers and service agents review the output. MP-365 scopes each agent to one job so results can be tested.
Q: What is the difference between a Copilot Studio agent and Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: Microsoft 365 Copilot is the general assistant across Microsoft 365 apps. A Copilot Studio agent is a purpose-built assistant for one task, with its own instructions, knowledge and tools. Agents can be published into Microsoft Copilot, so users reach them where they already work.
Q: Can an agent use our Dynamics 365 data?
A: Yes. Copilot Studio connects to Microsoft Dataverse, which holds Dynamics 365 data, and to other systems through prebuilt or custom connectors. MP-365 decides which tables the agent may read or write, and how it signs in, before any data is connected.
Q: Do custom agents respect user permissions?
A: It depends on how each connection is set up. An agent can use the signed-in user's access or a shared account. MP-365 chooses per connection and documents the decision, because a shared account can expose more data than any one user should see.
Q: How long does it take to build a custom Copilot agent?

Q: Does MP-365 build agents with non-Microsoft AI?
