Custom Copilot agents work best when they have one job, clean data and a named owner. If you have a process in mind, MP-365 can tell you whether Copilot Studio fits and what the build would involve.

## Copilot Cowork Consulting and Rollout
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/cowork/

Copilot Cowork consulting from MP-365 prepares your Microsoft 365 tenant for Microsoft's agentic assistant: who gets access, what it can reach, which actions need approval and how users learn to delegate. Microsoft made Copilot Cowork generally available on June 16, 2026, and MP-365 helps you roll it out without surprises.

bestFor: IT leaders and department heads who want Copilot to complete multistep work, such as inbox triage, meeting prep and document drafts, under clear controls.
includes: Access and spending policy design, data permission checks, approval and automation rules, model and plugin decisions, pilot, and role-based training.
notIncluded: License resale, custom software development, cybersecurity services, managed IT support and non-Microsoft AI tools.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing, your data permissions and the teams that should try Cowork first.

### What Copilot Cowork consulting covers
Copilot Cowork carries out tasks on a user's behalf across Microsoft 365. Microsoft's documentation says it can send emails, schedule meetings, create documents, post in Teams and handle multistep work. It is reached through the Microsoft Copilot app.
This page covers rollout, permissions and training. It is part of MP-365's wider Microsoft Copilot consulting.

### How do you roll out Copilot Cowork safely?
You roll out Copilot Cowork safely by deciding who may use it, cleaning up what they can reach and setting the rules for actions before the first pilot user logs in. Five decisions cover most of the risk.

### Control access with a spending policy
Microsoft states that Cowork access is granted through a spending policy that selects Cowork. The old agent setting under All Agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center no longer controls access. Anyone inside the scope of such a policy can use Cowork, so MP-365 builds the policy around security groups, not around a limit.

### Fix data permissions first
Cowork inherits the user's permissions, so it reaches only the files and emails that user can already open. That is reassuring only if those permissions are sound. A Copilot data access review comes before a wide rollout.

### Set rules for approvals and automations
Cowork asks for approval before sensitive actions, such as sending an email or posting in Teams. Users can approve once or skip the prompt for similar actions during a session. MP-365 sets guidance on when skipping is acceptable, and reviews event-driven tasks, which prepare actions for approval by default.

### Decide on models, plugins and browser use
Admins can turn off the Anthropic model family, control which plugins are deployed and switch the Cowork Browsing setting on or off. Microsoft notes that organizations inside the EU Data Boundary can use only GPT models. MP-365 documents each choice for your records.

### Teach people to delegate well
Good Cowork results come from clear task descriptions and careful review. MP-365 trains users to state the goal, name the source files and check the preview before approving.

### Copilot Cowork controls and the decision behind each
Control | Where it is set | Decision for your organization
Who can use Cowork | Spending policy in Copilot cost management | Which security groups join the pilot, and which do not
How much it can spend | Limits per tenant, group and user | Monthly budgets and who gets alerts
Which models are offered | Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center | Whether to allow the Anthropic models
Plugins and connectors | Plugin management in the admin center | Which plugins are deployed or hidden
Browser tasks | Cowork Browsing tenant setting | Whether web tasks in Microsoft Edge are allowed
Audit trail | Unified audit log and Microsoft Purview | Who reviews Cowork activity, and how often

### How MP-365 handles a Copilot Cowork implementation
1. Confirm licensing and billing: Check that pilot users hold Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and that usage-based billing is set up with your finance owner.
2. Review data access: Run the permission and sharing checks for the sites and mailboxes your pilot users depend on.
3. Create the access policy: Build the spending policy and security groups that decide who can use Cowork, with limits and alerts.
4. Configure admin settings: Set model, plugin and browser options, then record each decision and the reason for it.
5. Pick pilot tasks: Choose repeatable tasks such as daily briefings, meeting preparation and document drafting, with a named reviewer for each.
6. Train the pilot group: Run role-based sessions on writing tasks, reviewing previews and using approvals and pauses.
7. Review usage and widen access: Read the Cowork usage report with sponsors, adjust limits and add the next group.

### What you get from a Copilot Cowork setup
- Access design: the spending policy, groups and limits that control who uses Cowork.
- Permission findings: data access risks found before the pilot, with fixes ranked.
- Settings record: every admin decision on models, plugins and browser use.
- Pilot playbook: the tasks, reviewers and measures for the first users.
- Role-based training: short guides and live sessions for each pilot role.
- Review routine: how to read usage reports and decide on wider access.

### Microsoft products involved
A Copilot Cowork setup touches Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing, the Microsoft Copilot app, the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra ID security groups, SharePoint, OneDrive, Microsoft Purview and the unified audit log. Cowork saves the files it creates to your OneDrive and SharePoint workspace.
Microsoft documents Dynamics 365 Sales skills that work in Cowork, which ties this service to the Dynamics 365 sales agents.

### Proof: a simpler security model for a manufacturer
MP-365 built a modern intranet for a manufacturing client with a clear information architecture, a simpler security model and faster content updates. A simpler model matters for Cowork, because every action it takes depends on what the user can already reach.
The clients page lists named projects.

### When Copilot Cowork is not the right fit
Cowork is not the right first step if your tenant has no Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, if sharing and permissions are unreviewed or if nobody owns the spending budget. Start with a Copilot readiness assessment in those cases. Cowork also cannot delete files in OneDrive or SharePoint, or read encrypted files, so tasks that need either are out of scope.
Cost has two sides: Microsoft's usage-based charges, billed directly by Microsoft, and MP-365's consulting fee. The pricing page covers the second.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Copilot Cowork?
A: Copilot Cowork is Microsoft's agentic assistant in the Microsoft Copilot app. It carries out multistep tasks for a user, such as sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents and posting in Teams. Microsoft made it generally available on June 16, 2026. It acts only with that user's own access.
Q: How is Copilot Cowork different from Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: Per Microsoft's documentation, Copilot Chat helps with drafting and answers in one session, while Cowork completes multistep work across apps by taking action for you. Cowork needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and adds usage-based billing. Both respect the user's existing permissions.
Q: How do you roll out Copilot Cowork safely?
A: Review data permissions first, then grant access through a spending policy tied to a pilot security group. Set approval rules, decide on models and plugins, train the pilot users and watch the usage report. MP-365 runs these steps in that order.
Q: Who is allowed to use Copilot Cowork in our tenant?
A: Only users inside the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork. Microsoft says the older agent setting no longer controls access. To keep someone out, leave them out of every such policy, rather than lowering their limit. MP-365 designs these policies around security groups.
Q: What does Copilot Cowork cost?
A: Microsoft bills Cowork by usage on top of the Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and admins can set limits per tenant, group and user. Microsoft sets those prices. MP-365's fee for setup is separate, and the pricing page explains how engagements are structured.
Q: Can Copilot Cowork see all our company files?
A: No. Cowork inherits the signed-in user's permissions, so it reaches only files and emails that user can already open. The risk is overshared content, where many users can open files they should not. That is why MP-365 reviews permissions before a broad rollout.
Q: Will Copilot Cowork send emails without asking?
A: By default, no. Cowork shows an approval prompt before sensitive actions such as sending an email or posting in Teams, and users can see a preview. Users can skip prompts for similar actions in a session, so MP-365 sets guidance on when that is acceptable.
Q: Can we turn Copilot Cowork off for some people?
A: Yes. Access follows spending policy scope, so leaving a user out of every Cowork policy keeps them out. Admins can also turn off the Anthropic model family, manage plugins and switch off browser use in the admin center. MP-365 documents these settings during setup.
Q: Does Copilot Cowork use Anthropic models?
A: Yes, in part. Microsoft documents that Cowork can use Anthropic Claude models as a subprocessor, and admins can turn that model family off. Microsoft also says organizations inside the EU Data Boundary are limited to GPT models. Check your data residency needs with MP-365 before the pilot.
Q: Do we need a readiness assessment before Cowork?
A: It is strongly advised. Cowork amplifies whatever access users already have, so a permissions problem becomes a faster problem. A readiness assessment is a sensible first step for tenants that have never reviewed sharing and site ownership.

Copilot Cowork consulting is mostly about preparation: access, data permissions, approvals and training. MP-365 can scope a pilot for your tenant and leave you with settings, a playbook and users who know how to delegate.

## Copilot Data Protection and Permissions Audit
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/copilot/ai-data-governance-audit/

Copilot data protection starts with knowing who can open which files, because Microsoft 365 Copilot answers from whatever each user can already reach. MP-365's AI Data Governance Audit is a data access and permissions review for SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Dynamics 365, run before you enable Copilot.

bestFor: IT, compliance and business leaders who suspect their files are shared too widely and want that fixed before Copilot goes live.
includes: SharePoint and OneDrive permission and sharing review, label coverage check, Dynamics 365 role review, ranked cleanup list and owner review support.
notIncluded: Cybersecurity services, identity and access management services, compliance certification, managed IT support and license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your tenant, the Copilot plans you have and any areas where you already know files are overshared.

### What Copilot data protection means in this audit
Copilot data protection, as MP-365 uses the term, is about access: making sure Copilot can only draw on content the right people should see. The audit is a permissions review, not a security operations service.
People often search for Microsoft 365 Copilot security when they mean this question. Microsoft states that Copilot honors the same access controls that apply across Microsoft 365. The work is therefore to make those controls accurate. The audit is one service in MP-365's Microsoft Copilot consulting.

### What is Copilot oversharing?
Copilot oversharing is when Copilot surfaces content to a user who can technically open it but was never meant to read it. Copilot did not break a rule. The permission was too broad to begin with.
Typical causes are sites shared with "Everyone except external users", old sharing links that never expired, owner-less project sites and files stored in the wrong library. Before Copilot, those files were hard to find. With Copilot, a single question can pull them up.

### Signs your tenant has an oversharing problem
- Whole-company access: sites or files shared with every internal user through built-in groups.
- Link sprawl: hundreds of sharing links created over the years, some open to "Anyone" or to the whole organization.
- Orphaned sites: project and team sites with no active owner to approve access.
- Unlabeled sensitive files: HR, finance and legal documents with no sensitivity label.
- Guest leftovers: external users who still have access after a project ended.
- Admin-level CRM roles: Dynamics 365 users with broader security roles than their jobs need.

### What the data access review examines
Area | What MP-365 reviews | Typical finding
Site permissions | Snapshot of who can reach each SharePoint and OneDrive site | Sites open to thousands of users or to external guests
Everyone-style groups | Items shared with all internal users or with Everyone | Files exposed because of a built-in group
Sharing links | Sites with the most new links in the last 28 days | Links created for convenience and never removed
Sensitivity labels | Where labeled files live and where labels are missing | Sensitive libraries with no label
Site ownership | Owners, inactive sites and site attestations | Sites with no accountable owner
Dynamics 365 roles | Security roles assigned to CRM users | Users with unnecessary Admin access

### How do you audit data access before enabling Copilot?
1. Agree the scope: List the workloads, departments and Dynamics 365 environments that Copilot users will touch first.
2. Generate the access reports: Run the SharePoint data access governance reports and collect label and sharing link data for the scope.
3. Rank sites by exposure: Order sites by how many people can open them, whether guests are present and how sensitive the content appears.
4. Review Dynamics 365 roles: Check which CRM security roles each user holds and flag access beyond the job.
5. Ask site owners to confirm: Start site access reviews so the people who know each site confirm members and sharing.
6. Apply interim restrictions: Where cleanup will take time, limit access or keep chosen sites out of Copilot while the real fix proceeds.
7. Deliver the cleanup list: Hand over a ranked list with owners and recommended actions, and support the fixes if you ask us to.

### Which permissions should be cleaned up first?
Clean up the widest permissions on the most sensitive content first. That order gives the largest risk reduction for the least effort, and it matches Microsoft's own deployment blueprint, which starts with remediating oversharing.

### Priority order MP-365 uses
- First: items shared with Everyone or Everyone except external users, where the content is sensitive.
- Second: sites open to external guests that no longer need them.
- Third: sites with the broadest membership and no owner.
- Fourth: sharing links on finance, HR, legal and executive libraries.
- Fifth: inactive sites that still hold old, widely shared files.

### Interim measures versus real fixes
Microsoft's Restricted Content Discovery keeps selected sites and files from surfacing in Copilot, and Restricted Access Control limits a site to specific groups. Both buy time. Neither replaces correct permissions, because the files stay shared. MP-365 labels each as temporary in the report.

### Copilot data governance beyond the first cleanup
Copilot data governance is the ongoing routine that stops oversharing from returning. It combines site ownership policies, inactive site reviews, regular access reports and Microsoft Purview labels and policies. Microsoft recommends running site permission snapshots quarterly and activity reports monthly.
MP-365 sets up the first cycle and trains your administrators to repeat it. For the label and policy side, see Microsoft Purview and permission models.

### What you get from the audit
- Exposure report: every site in scope, ranked by exposure and sensitivity.
- Cleanup list: specific actions with owners and priority.
- Dynamics 365 role findings: users and roles that exceed job needs, as covered in the Dynamics 365 security roles audit.
- Interim controls plan: which sites to restrict now and when to lift each restriction.
- Governance routine: a schedule for repeating reports and owner reviews.
- Admin handover: a working session with your SharePoint and Microsoft 365 administrators.

### Microsoft tools used in the audit
The review uses SharePoint Advanced Management, the SharePoint admin center, Microsoft Purview, the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Dynamics 365 security role settings. Microsoft says SharePoint Advanced Management is included with a Microsoft Copilot license. Microsoft 365 E5 alone gives limited data access governance reporting, without the snapshot reports or remedial actions. MP-365 checks what your licenses allow before the audit starts.

### Proof: access control with approvals and reports
For one client, MP-365 set up CRM access control with an approval process, documented access levels and automatic access reports. The same habits drive this audit: someone approves access, the levels are written down and reports show drift.
The clients page lists named projects.

### When this audit is not the right fit
This audit is not a cybersecurity assessment, a threat review or a compliance certification. MP-365 does not provide those services, so look to a specialist security provider if you need them. A smaller tenant with tidy permissions may only need the broader Copilot readiness assessment, and teams about to launch an agentic assistant should also read about Copilot Cowork rollout.
Effort depends on the number of sites and users in scope. The pricing page explains how MP-365 engages.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Copilot oversharing?
A: Copilot oversharing happens when Copilot shows a user content they can open but were never meant to read. The files were already too widely shared. Copilot makes them easy to find. Typical causes are company-wide groups, old sharing links and sites with no owner.
Q: How do you audit data access before enabling Copilot?
A: Run permission, sharing link and label reports, rank sites by exposure, review Dynamics 365 roles and ask site owners to confirm access. Then apply temporary limits where needed and produce a cleanup list. MP-365 follows this sequence in the AI Data Governance Audit.
Q: Which permissions should be cleaned up first?
A: Start with sensitive content shared to Everyone or Everyone except external users. Then address external guests who no longer need access, sites with broad membership and no owner, and sharing links on finance, HR and legal libraries. Inactive sites come after, because their files matter less.
Q: Can Copilot access files a user is not allowed to open?
A: No. According to Microsoft's 2026 documentation, Copilot can only summarize or reference content the user is authorized to access. For encrypted content, the user also needs the EXTRACT and VIEW usage rights. The practical risk is content that users are allowed to open but should not.
Q: Is the AI Data Governance Audit a security service?
A: No. It is a data access and permissions review. It checks who can open which content in SharePoint, OneDrive and Dynamics 365 so Copilot draws on the right sources. MP-365 does not provide cybersecurity, identity management or compliance certification.
Q: What is Microsoft 365 Copilot security, and does this audit cover it?
A: Copilot security in Microsoft's model mostly means permissions, labels and policies that control what Copilot can use. This audit covers the permissions part for SharePoint, OneDrive and Dynamics 365 roles. Threat detection, incident response and compliance programs fall outside it.
Q: Do we need SharePoint Advanced Management for the audit?
A: It helps a great deal. Microsoft says SharePoint Advanced Management is included with a Microsoft Copilot license and provides the data access governance reports and site access reviews. MP-365 checks what your licenses include first and adapts the method if some reports are unavailable.
Q: Will the audit change our permissions?
A: Not on its own. The audit reads reports and produces a ranked list. Changes follow only after you approve them, and site owners confirm access for their own sites. MP-365 can carry out approved fixes or hand the list to your administrators.
Q: Can we hide risky sites from Copilot while we clean up?
A: Yes, temporarily. Microsoft offers Restricted Content Discovery to keep chosen sites and files from surfacing in Copilot, and Restricted Access Control to limit a site to certain groups. Both are stopgaps, so MP-365 records each one with a plan to remove it.
Q: How often should we repeat the review?
A: Microsoft recommends running site permission snapshot reports quarterly and sharing activity reports monthly. MP-365 sets that routine during handover. Repeat sooner after a merger, a reorganization or a large Copilot expansion, because each of those changes who can reach what.

Copilot data protection comes down to accurate permissions on the content Copilot can reach. MP-365's audit finds the gaps, ranks them and helps your owners close them, so Copilot launches on data you have reviewed.

## Power Platform Consulting for Business Teams
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/power-platform/

Power Platform consulting from MP-365 covers four Microsoft tools: Power Apps, Power Pages, Power Automate and Power BI. MP-365 builds them on the Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 data you already have, so apps, portals, approvals and reports all work from one source of truth.

### What Power Platform consulting includes
Power Platform consulting means designing, building and supporting Microsoft's low-code tools around your business data. MP-365 does this as part of its wider Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 services, so the work connects to the CRM and the files your teams already use.
The tools share one data layer. Microsoft's documentation says Power Pages sites use the same Microsoft Dataverse data that you use to build apps, workflows, reports and analytics. It also says Dynamics 365 apps store and secure their data in Dataverse, so you can build apps against your core business data without a separate integration.

### Which Power Platform service fits which problem
Service | Best for | Typical outcome | Built on
Power Apps Development | Teams that run a daily process in spreadsheets, email or paper | One app with clear owners, status and history for each request | Dataverse, SharePoint, Dynamics 365
Power Pages Portal Development | Customers, partners or applicants who need to sign in and update their own records | A secure external portal that reads and writes Dynamics 365 data | Dataverse, Dynamics 365
Power Automate Workflow Automation | Approvals, notifications and data moves that people repeat by hand | Flows that run on their own and leave an audit trail | Dataverse, SharePoint, Outlook, Teams
Power BI Consulting & Dashboards | Leaders who wait on spreadsheet reports | Live dashboards with one set of numbers for sales, service and operations | Dynamics 365, SharePoint, other business systems

### Which service to start with
Start with the service that removes your most expensive manual step. For most mid-size teams that is Power Automate, because one approval flow can save hours across many people.
Start with Power Apps when the pain is a missing system, such as inspections tracked on paper. Start with Power Pages when outsiders need access to your data. Start with Power BI when leaders do not trust the numbers.

### How to choose by the symptom you see
- People re-type the same data into several places: start with Power Automate to move the data once.
- A process lives in Excel and email threads: start with Power Apps to give it one record and one owner.
- Customers or partners email you for status updates: start with Power Pages so they can see their own cases and orders.
- Monthly reports take days to assemble: start with Power BI and connect it to the source systems.
- You are unsure where to begin: book a discovery call and MP-365 will rank the options by effort and payoff.

### How MP-365 approaches Power Platform work
1. Understand the process: Sit with the people who do the work and map how it runs today, including the workarounds.
2. Pick the data home: Decide whether the data belongs in Dataverse, SharePoint or your existing Dynamics 365 tables.
3. Build a small first version: Ship a working app, flow, portal page or dashboard for one team before widening scope.
4. Validate with real users: Watch people use it, fix what slows them down and confirm the numbers match the source.
5. Set the guardrails: Put environments, ownership and data policies in place so makers cannot expose data by accident.
6. Deploy and hand off: Move the solution into production, document it and train the people who will run it.
7. Support and improve: Fix issues quickly and add the next improvement from the backlog.

### Governance: who can build and share what
Power Platform governance decides which connectors, environments and makers are allowed. Microsoft's data policies in the Power Platform admin center let administrators control which connectors apps and flows can use, and Microsoft documents that these policies act as guardrails against accidental data exposure (Microsoft Learn, 2026).
MP-365 sets up this structure early. A department head can still build a quick app, but the app cannot send customer records to a personal mailbox or an unapproved service.

Power Platform is a poor fit for a product you plan to sell, or for a system that handles very high transaction volumes. ### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What does Power Platform consulting include?
A: Power Platform consulting includes scoping, building and supporting apps, portals, automated workflows and dashboards. MP-365 works with Power Apps, Power Pages, Power Automate and Power BI, and connects them to Dynamics 365, SharePoint and Microsoft 365. It also covers handover, training and ongoing fixes after go-live.
Q: What can you build with the Power Platform?
A: You can build internal apps for approvals and inspections, external portals where customers sign in, automated workflows that move data between systems, and Power BI dashboards. Each one can read and write the same Dataverse and Dynamics 365 data, so you do not maintain separate copies.
Q: How much does a Power Platform project cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of tools, the data sources and how many people use the result. Microsoft license fees are separate from consulting fees and are set by Microsoft. MP-365 scopes a first small piece of work so you can see value before committing more. See the pricing page for how MP-365 engages.
Q: Which Power Platform tool should we start with?
A: Start with the tool that removes your most costly manual step. Power Automate suits repeated approvals and data re-entry. Power Apps suits processes tracked in spreadsheets. Power Pages suits external users, and Power BI suits slow reporting. A discovery call usually settles the order quickly.
Q: Do we need Dynamics 365 to use the Power Platform?
A: No. Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI work with SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Excel and many other sources. Dynamics 365 helps because its apps already store data in Dataverse, which the other tools use directly. Teams without Dynamics 365 usually start from SharePoint lists or a new Dataverse environment.
Q: What is Dataverse and do we need it?
A: Microsoft Dataverse is the data platform behind Power Apps and Dynamics 365. You need it for model-driven apps, Power Pages portals and most Dynamics 365 integrations. For a simple internal app, a SharePoint list can be enough. MP-365 recommends the lighter option when it meets the need.
Q: How do you control who can build and share apps and flows?
A: MP-365 sets up separate environments, names an owner for each solution and configures Power Platform data policies. Those policies control which connectors apps and flows may use. Makers can still build, but they cannot connect business data to unapproved services without an administrator allowing it.
Q: Can business users build their own apps and flows?
A: Yes, and that is part of the appeal. Business users can build simple apps and flows safely when environments and data policies are in place. MP-365 builds the shared foundation, handles complex logic and reviews anything that touches customer or financial data before it goes live.
Q: What is the difference between Power Apps and Power Automate?
A: Power Apps gives people a screen to enter, view and approve data. Power Automate runs steps in the background, such as sending an approval request or copying a record. Most solutions use both: an app collects the request and a flow routes it, updates records and notifies people.
Q: Can Power Platform replace our custom software?
A: Sometimes. Internal tools for approvals, tracking and field work often run well on Power Apps and Power Automate at lower effort than custom code. Products you sell, or systems with very high transaction loads, usually need a software team. MP-365 works in low-code and will say when a project is not a fit.

Power Platform consulting works best when it starts with one real problem and a small first version. MP-365 can look at your processes, rank the four services by payoff and build the first piece on your existing Microsoft data.

## Power Apps Consulting and Development
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/power-platform/power-apps/

Power Apps consulting services from MP-365 turn spreadsheets, email chains and paper forms into apps your team uses every day. MP-365 designs and builds canvas and model-driven apps on Dataverse, SharePoint and Dynamics 365 data for approvals, inspections and daily operations.

bestFor: Operations, sales and service teams that run a daily process in Excel, email or paper and need one app with clear owners and status.
includes: App design, data model in Dataverse or SharePoint, canvas or model-driven build, connections to Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365, testing, deployment and handover.
notIncluded: Custom software development, web design agency work, ERP implementation, Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call about one process. MP-365 maps how the work runs today and proposes the smallest app that would help.

### Problems a custom Power App solves
- "Nobody knows who owns this request." An app gives every request one record, one owner and a visible status.
- "We keep the master list in Excel and it has five copies." An app on Dataverse or SharePoint keeps one shared copy with change history.
- "Inspectors fill in paper forms and someone re-types them." A mobile app captures the data, photos and signatures once, at the site.
- "Approvals get lost in email." An app with a Power Automate flow routes each approval and records the decision.
- "Our CRM screens do not fit how this team works." A focused app shows only the fields and actions that team needs, on top of Dynamics 365 data.

### What our Power Apps consulting services cover
MP-365 builds three kinds of apps most often. Each solves a different daily pain, and each is small enough to ship quickly and improve in use.

### Approval and request apps
A request app replaces the email-and-spreadsheet routine for purchases, access, time off or change requests. The app captures the request, a flow routes it to the right approver, and the decision is stored with the record. Managers approve from Teams or a phone.

### Inspection and site visit apps
A field app lets crews complete checklists on a phone or tablet, attach photos and capture a signature. Data lands in Dataverse the moment the form is saved, so the office sees it without waiting for paperwork. This suits safety walks, equipment checks and site visits.

### Companion apps for Dynamics 365
A companion app gives one team a simplified view of CRM data. A coordinator might see only open orders to confirm, with two buttons and a note field. Because Dynamics 365 stores its data in Dataverse, the app reads the live records directly. See Dynamics 365 Sales for the CRM side.

### Canvas apps and model-driven apps compared
App type | How it is built | Best for | Example
Canvas app | You design each screen freely in Power Apps Studio, much like a slide deck | Task-focused mobile or tablet apps with a custom layout | Site inspection checklist
Model-driven app | You choose tables, forms and views in the app designer, and the layout follows from the data model | Data-heavy apps with many related records and role-based access | Case or project tracker with several linked tables
Dynamics 365 app | Microsoft builds the app on Dataverse and MP-365 configures it | Standard sales or service processes | Sales pipeline and customer cases

### How to choose between canvas and model-driven
Choose a canvas app when the screen design matters most, such as a phone checklist. Choose a model-driven app when the relationships between records matter most. Microsoft's Power Apps documentation describes both types and says apps run in a browser and on phones and tablets.
Many MP-365 projects use both: a model-driven app for the back office and a canvas app for people in the field, sharing the same tables.

### How MP-365 delivers a Power Apps project
1. Watch the process: Spend time with the users and note each step, hand-off and workaround in the current routine.
2. Choose the data home: Pick Dataverse for relational data and security roles, or SharePoint lists for simple tracking.
3. Sketch the screens: Draw the screens with the users and agree what each role sees before building.
4. Build the first version: Build the smallest app that handles the core path from request to completion.
5. Add flows and connections: Connect Power Automate for routing and notifications, and link to Dynamics 365 or Outlook where needed.
6. Test with real users: Have the team run live cases, then fix what slows them down.
7. Deploy and train: Move the app to production through a managed solution, document it and train the owners.

### What you get from a Power Apps engagement
- A working app: deployed to your production environment and shared with the right users.
- A data model: tables and columns documented so others can extend them.
- Role-based access: security roles or SharePoint permissions that match who should see what.
- Connected flows: approvals and notifications built in Power Automate.
- Handover notes and training: a short guide for owners and a walkthrough for users.
- A backlog: a ranked list of next improvements so the app grows in order.

### Microsoft products involved in a Power Apps build
A typical build uses Power Apps for the interface, Microsoft Dataverse or SharePoint for the data, and Power Automate for routing. Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Excel often supply or receive data.
As of October 2026, Microsoft's documentation says you can describe an app to Microsoft Copilot in Power Apps and have it design a first draft. MP-365 treats that as a starting sketch. The data model, security and testing still need an experienced builder.

### Power Apps or custom software: how to decide
Use Power Apps when the app serves your own staff, relies on Microsoft data and needs to change often. Use custom software when you are building a product for sale, need a highly specialized interface or expect very large transaction volumes.
MP-365 builds low-code apps and does not offer custom software development. If your idea belongs in custom code, we will say so at the discovery call instead of forcing it into Power Apps.

### What affects the cost of a Power Apps build
The main cost drivers are the number of screens, the number of data sources and how complex the approval rules are. Microsoft license fees are set by Microsoft and are separate from consulting fees. The pricing page explains how MP-365 engages, and the first conversation usually produces a small first scope.

### Proof: replacing email-based tracking with one system
One MP-365 client ran support through email. MP-365 moved case tracking into one system that shows the owner, status and urgency of every case. That is the shape of work Power Apps suits: one record per item and a clear owner.
For named client results, see the clients page.

### When a Power App is not the right fit
A Power App is not the right fit if the process is already handled well in Dynamics 365 or SharePoint without extra screens. It is also wrong for public-facing sites, where Power Pages is the tool, and for pure reporting, where Power BI fits better.

### Related Power Platform services
Apps rarely work alone. Power Automate workflow automation handles the routing behind an app, and the wider Power Platform service page shows how all four tools fit together.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What can a custom Power App do for our business?
A: A custom Power App replaces a manual routine with a screen your team uses. Common examples are approval requests, site inspections, asset checks and simple trackers. It stores data once, shows who owns each item and works on desktop, phone and tablet. It can also read and update Dynamics 365 records.
Q: How long does it take to build a Power App?
A: It depends on the number of screens, data sources and approval rules. MP-365 builds a small first version for one team, puts it in front of real users and then expands. Simple trackers come together faster than apps with several connected systems. The discovery call gives a realistic scope.
Q: Should we use Power Apps or custom software?
A: Use Power Apps for internal tools that rely on Microsoft data and change often. Use custom software for a product you sell or a system with very high transaction volume. MP-365 works in low-code and does not do custom software development, so it tells you early when a project belongs elsewhere.
Q: What is the difference between a canvas app and a model-driven app?
A: A canvas app lets you design each screen freely, which suits phone and tablet tasks. A model-driven app builds its screens from your Dataverse tables, which suits data-heavy work with many related records. Many projects use both, with a model-driven app for the office and a canvas app for the field.
Q: Do Power Apps work offline?
A: Canvas apps can be built to work with limited connectivity, and Microsoft documents offline options for mobile use. Offline design adds effort because the app must store data locally and sync later. MP-365 confirms the need during discovery, since a site crew with poor signal needs this and an office team does not.
Q: Where is the data stored?
A: Data lives in Microsoft Dataverse, SharePoint lists or an existing system such as Dynamics 365 or SQL Server. MP-365 picks the home based on how many related records you have and who needs which access. Dataverse offers security roles and relationships, and SharePoint suits simple tracking.
Q: Can a Power App connect to Dynamics 365?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 apps such as Sales and Customer Service store data in Dataverse, which Power Apps reads directly, so there is no separate integration to build. A Power App can show a simplified view of CRM records or add a step that the standard screens lack, such as a field checklist.
Q: Who can use the app, and what licenses are needed?
A: Anyone you share the app with can use it, provided they hold a suitable Microsoft license. Requirements depend on the connectors and Dataverse features the app uses, and Microsoft sets the prices. MP-365 checks the license needs during design so there are no surprises at rollout.
Q: Can you fix or take over an app someone else built?
A: Yes. MP-365 reviews apps built by internal makers or other vendors, fixes slow screens and broken connections, and tidies the data model. Sometimes a rebuild of one screen is enough. The first step is a short review of the app, its owner and where it breaks.
Q: Who maintains the app after go-live?
A: You decide. A named owner in your team can handle small changes after training, and MP-365 can support the app on an ad hoc or ongoing basis for bigger fixes and new features. Either way, the app is documented and deployed through a managed solution so changes stay controlled.

Good Power Apps consulting services start with one painful process and a small first app that people want to use. MP-365 can map your process, choose the right data home and build the first version on your existing Microsoft data.

## Power Pages Consulting for Customer Portals
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/power-platform/power-pages/

Power Pages consulting from MP-365 gives you a secure portal where customers, partners or applicants sign in and work with your Dynamics 365 data. Power Pages was formerly called Power Apps portals, and MP-365 builds on the current product, including sign-in, permissions and forms.

bestFor: Organizations that need external users, such as customers, partners or applicants, to sign in and see or update their own records in Dynamics 365 or Dataverse.
includes: Portal design, sign-in setup, web roles and table permissions, forms and lists on Dataverse tables, case and request flows linked to Dynamics 365, testing and handover.
notIncluded: Web design agency work, custom software development, cybersecurity services, ERP implementation, Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call to list who signs in, what each group sees and which records they change.

### What Power Pages consulting delivers
Power Pages consulting delivers an external-facing website that reads and writes your business data. Microsoft describes Power Pages as a secure, low-code platform for creating, hosting and administering external business websites (Microsoft Learn, 2026).
The data sits in Microsoft Dataverse, the same data platform that Dynamics 365 uses. That means a customer can open a case on the portal and your service team sees it in Dynamics 365 at once, with no copy step in between.

### Problems a Dynamics 365 customer portal solves
- Status calls and emails: customers see their own cases, orders or applications without phoning your team.
- Paper and PDF forms: applicants submit structured data that lands directly in the CRM.
- Partner data in spreadsheets: partners register deals or update records themselves.
- No single sign-in: external users log in with an identity they already have instead of a shared password.
- Manual data entry: staff stop re-keying what outside users send them by email.

### Power Pages compared with a SharePoint portal
Question | Power Pages portal | SharePoint supplier or partner portal
Main job | Let external users work with business records | Share documents, files and pages with partners
Where the data lives | Dataverse tables, including Dynamics 365 data | SharePoint libraries and lists
What users do | Submit forms, track cases, update their own records | Download, upload and read content
Access control | Web roles and table permissions at record level | SharePoint permissions on sites, libraries and files
Choose it when | Outsiders need to act on CRM or case data | Outsiders mainly need files and shared content

### Which portal approach fits your use case
Choose Power Pages when external users sign in to submit, track or change records. Choose a SharePoint portal when the goal is document sharing with suppliers or partners. MP-365 builds both and explains the SharePoint side on its SharePoint supplier and partner portals page.
Some clients need both: a Power Pages site for case and order data and a SharePoint area for contracts and drawings.

### How access works in a Power Pages portal
Access in Power Pages has three layers: who can sign in, which web role they hold, and which table records that role may touch. MP-365 designs all three together, because a portal that exposes the wrong record is worse than no portal.

### Sign-in options
Power Pages ties each signed-in user to a Dataverse contact record. Microsoft lists supported identity providers including Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Entra External ID, Azure AD B2C, and OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0 providers. Microsoft's documentation does not recommend local username-and-password accounts, so MP-365 uses an external identity provider.

### Web roles
A web role groups users who get the same permissions on the site, such as Customer, Partner or Applicant. Users without a web role get only what anonymous visitors get. MP-365 keeps the list of roles short and documents what each one allows.

### Table permissions
Table permissions decide which Dataverse records a role may read, create, update or delete. Microsoft documents access types such as global, contact, account and self, so a customer can see only the cases linked to their own contact or company. A permission only takes effect once a web role is attached to it.

### How MP-365 builds a Power Pages portal
1. Define the external users: List each group that signs in, what they need to do and which records belong to them.
2. Model the data: Confirm which Dataverse or Dynamics 365 tables the portal reads and writes, and fix gaps in the relationships.
3. Set up sign-in: Connect the identity provider and decide how new users register or receive invitations.
4. Create web roles and permissions: Build the web roles and table permissions, then test each role with a real account.
5. Build pages, forms and lists: Design the site in the Power Pages design studio with forms and lists tied to the tables.
6. Connect the back-office process: Link portal submissions to Dynamics 365 queues, owners and Power Automate flows.
7. Test, launch and hand off: Run user testing, deploy to production and train your team to manage content and users.

### What you get from a portal project
- A live portal: pages, forms and lists connected to your Dataverse or Dynamics 365 data.
- Access design: documented web roles and table permissions, tested per role.
- Sign-in setup: your chosen identity provider, with registration or invitation rules.
- Back-office routing: submissions routed to the right owner in Dynamics 365.
- Admin guide: instructions for managing users, content and permission changes.
- Improvement backlog: ranked next steps such as new forms or dashboards.

### Microsoft products behind a Dynamics 365 portal
A Dynamics 365 portal usually combines Power Pages, Dataverse and one or more Dynamics 365 apps. For support portals, the partner app is often Dynamics 365 Customer Service, where agents work the cases customers open online.
Power Automate adds approvals and notifications, and Microsoft Entra handles sign-in. Power BI can report on portal activity using the same Dataverse data.

### Proof: access control experience that carries into portals
A portal exposes CRM data to outsiders, so how access is governed matters. MP-365 supports Dynamics 365 CRM for the US Department of Transportation, and has built CRM access control for another client with an approval process, documented access levels and automatic access reports.
That discipline is the same one a Power Pages portal needs: know who can see what, and prove it. See the clients page for named work.

### What MP-365 does and does not take on
MP-365 designs permission models and checks that each role sees only what it should. It does not provide cybersecurity services, and it does not certify a portal against compliance frameworks. If your sector has formal requirements, your compliance team signs off alongside the build.

### When Power Pages is not the right fit
Power Pages is not the right fit for a marketing website with no sign-in, or a brochure site where a standard content system is simpler. It is also overkill when partners only need documents, where a SharePoint portal is cheaper to run. Cost depends on scope and Microsoft licensing, which Microsoft sets separately; see the pricing page.

### Related Power Platform services
Portals work best alongside the rest of the Power Platform. Internal staff often use Power Apps on the same tables that the portal exposes to outsiders.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Power Pages?
A: Power Pages is Microsoft's low-code platform for building secure websites that external users can sign in to. The site reads and writes data in Microsoft Dataverse, the same data layer used by Dynamics 365 and Power Apps. Typical uses are customer, partner and applicant portals.
Q: Is Power Pages the same as Power Apps portals?
A: Yes, Power Pages is the current name for Power Apps portals. Microsoft announced the change at its Build conference in May 2022. Searches for Dynamics portals or a Dynamics 365 portal usually mean this same product, so MP-365 builds on Power Pages and its design studio today.
Q: What is the difference between Power Pages and a SharePoint portal?
A: Power Pages lets signed-in external users submit and update business records stored in Dataverse. A SharePoint portal mainly shares files and content with partners or suppliers. Choose Power Pages for cases, orders and applications, and SharePoint for documents. Many clients use both side by side.
Q: Can customers see their own cases in a Dynamics 365 customer portal?
A: Yes. A portal can list and open only the cases tied to the signed-in customer, using contact or account access in table permissions. Agents work those cases in Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and customer replies appear on the case record without any manual copying.
Q: How do customers and partners sign in?
A: Users sign in with an identity provider such as Microsoft Entra External ID, Azure AD B2C, or an OpenID Connect or SAML provider. They can also use social providers. Microsoft's documentation does not recommend local username-and-password accounts. MP-365 sets up registration or invitations to match how you onboard users.
Q: How does Power Pages keep one customer from seeing another's data?
A: Table permissions and web roles control access. Power Pages blocks access to Dataverse records unless a permission grants it, and a contact or account access type limits users to records linked to them. MP-365 tests every role with real accounts before launch to confirm the limits hold.
Q: Do we need Dynamics 365 to use Power Pages?
A: No. Power Pages works with any Dataverse environment, so you can run a portal on custom tables without Dynamics 365. Having Dynamics 365 adds ready-made data such as accounts, contacts and cases. MP-365 recommends the Dynamics 365 route when the portal serves sales or service processes.
Q: How much does a Power Pages project cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of user groups, forms, integrations and the sign-in setup. Microsoft's license fees are set separately from consulting fees. MP-365 usually proposes a first portal for one user group, then expands. See the pricing page for how engagements work.
Q: Can you redesign or fix an existing portal?
A: Yes. MP-365 reviews existing portals, whether built as Power Apps portals or Power Pages, and fixes broken forms, slow pages and loose permissions. A common first step is an audit of web roles and table permissions, to confirm each group sees only its own records.
Q: Does MP-365 certify a portal for compliance?
A: No. MP-365 builds permission models and checks that roles see only what they should, but it does not certify portals or provide cybersecurity services. If you must meet a framework such as HIPAA or FedRAMP, your compliance team should review the design with MP-365.

Power Pages consulting pays off when outside users need to act on your data, not just read files. MP-365 can list who needs access, design the permissions and build the first portal on your Dynamics 365 or Dataverse tables.

## Power Automate Consulting and Workflows
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/power-platform/power-automate/

Power Automate consulting from MP-365 removes the repeated manual steps that slow your team: approvals by email, copy-and-paste between systems and status updates typed by hand. MP-365 designs, builds and fixes cloud flows across Dynamics 365, SharePoint, Outlook, Teams and other business systems.

bestFor: Teams that route approvals by email, re-type data between systems or run classic Dynamics 365 workflows that are hard to maintain.
includes: Process mapping, cloud flow design and build, approvals, notifications, Dynamics 365 and SharePoint connections, error handling, testing, deployment and handover.
notIncluded: ERP implementation, custom software development, managed services or help desk support, Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call about one repeated process. MP-365 walks through it step by step and marks what can run on its own.

### What Power Automate consulting covers
Power Automate consulting covers finding, designing and building the automations that save your team the most time. A Microsoft Power Automate consultant at MP-365 works from your real process, not a template. MP-365's Power Automate developers build flows that handle errors, owners and audit needs.
Microsoft describes cloud flows as automated workflows that connect apps and services and can be triggered by events or by a schedule. MP-365 uses them to move data, route approvals and keep systems in step.

### Problems Power Automate solves in daily work
- Approvals stuck in inboxes: a manager is away and a purchase request sits for days with no one tracking it.
- Double entry: a sales rep updates the CRM, then types the same facts into a spreadsheet or another tool.
- Missed follow-ups: nobody is reminded when a contract, quote or case is about to go stale.
- Fragile classic workflows: old Dynamics 365 workflows and plug-ins that nobody dares to change.
- File chaos: documents saved by hand into folders, with no naming or permissions rule.

### Types of cloud flow and when to use each
Flow type | Starts when | Example at work
Automated cloud flow | An event happens, such as a new email or a changed record | When a Dynamics 365 opportunity is won, create a project folder in SharePoint and notify the delivery team
Instant cloud flow | Someone selects a button | A manager selects a button in Teams to request approval for a purchase
Scheduled cloud flow | A set time arrives | Every night, upload that day's transactions to SharePoint or a database

### What Power Automate can automate
Power Automate can automate anything with a trigger and a series of actions across the many apps it connects to. Beyond cloud flows, desktop flows can automate tasks in Windows applications that have no modern interface. MP-365 uses desktop flows only when no connector exists.
Good first candidates share three traits: people repeat the task often, the rules are clear, and the data already lives in a Microsoft system.

### How an approval workflow works in Power Automate
1. Start from a trigger: A new request record, a form submission or a button in Teams starts the flow.
2. Look up the approver: The flow reads the manager or owner from Dataverse, Dynamics 365 or Microsoft Entra, so no one hard-codes names.
3. Send the approval: The approver receives a request in Teams, Outlook or the Approvals app with the key details.
4. Wait for the decision: The flow pauses until a response arrives, with a reminder or escalation if nothing happens.
5. Branch on the answer: An approved request moves on to the next step. A rejected one returns to the requester with comments.
6. Record the outcome: The flow writes the decision, time and approver back to the record for audit.

### Replacing classic workflows and plug-ins with cloud flows
MP-365 replaces fragile classic Dynamics 365 workflows and plug-ins with cloud flows where it lowers the cost of change. A flow is visible in a designer, so an administrator can read what it does. Plug-in code often needs a developer for every tweak.
Not every plug-in should move. Logic that must run inside a database transaction may stay as code. MP-365 reviews each one and tells you which to move, which to keep and why.

### How MP-365 delivers a Power Automate project
1. Map the current process: Walk through each step with the people who do it and note exceptions.
2. Pick the first flows: Rank candidates by hours saved and risk, and choose one or two to build first.
3. Design the flow: Define the trigger, conditions, approvers, data fields and failure handling before building.
4. Build in a solution: Create flows inside a Power Platform solution, using connection references so they move cleanly between environments.
5. Add error alerts: Log failures and notify a named owner instead of failing silently.
6. Test with real data: Run live cases in a test environment and confirm each branch behaves.
7. Deploy and hand off: Release to production, document each flow and show the owner how to monitor it.

### What you get from Power Automate consulting services
- Working flows: deployed to production in a managed solution.
- Approval routing: approvers, reminders and escalation rules that match your policy.
- Connected systems: flows linking Dynamics 365, SharePoint, Outlook and Teams.
- Error handling: alerts that tell a named owner when a run fails.
- Documentation: a plain-language description of each flow, its trigger and its owner.
- Next-step list: ranked automations to build next.

### Microsoft products and controls involved
MP-365 builds with Power Automate cloud flows, Microsoft Dataverse, SharePoint, Outlook, Teams and Dynamics 365. Microsoft says you can also describe what you want to Copilot in the new designer and have it suggest the actions, as of Microsoft's July 2026 documentation. MP-365 uses that for drafts, then reviews each step.
Administrators control which connectors flows may use through Power Platform data policies. MP-365 checks your policies before building so a flow does not fail at deployment.

### Proof: automation that cut deployment time
MP-365 leads platform and operations for Dynamics at OTIS Elevator. Deployments went from 13 hours to 4, and manual errors fell to near zero. The principle is the one behind every flow MP-365 builds: replace a repeated manual step with a repeatable one.
Read more on the clients page.

### When Power Automate is not the right fit
Power Automate is not the right fit for simple field logic, such as making a field required, which a Dynamics 365 business rule handles better. It is also not ideal for moving very large data volumes between systems on a strict schedule. For that, MP-365 uses Dynamics 365 integration services with logging and alerts.

### Cost and related services
Cost depends on the number of flows, the systems involved and the approval rules. Microsoft's license fees are separate from consulting; see the pricing page for how MP-365 engages.
Flows pair naturally with Power Apps for the screen people use, and with custom Copilot agents that call a flow to take action. The wider Power Platform page shows how the four tools connect.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What can Power Automate automate?
A: Power Automate can automate approvals, notifications, document handling and data moves between apps such as Dynamics 365, SharePoint, Outlook and Teams. Cloud flows run on triggers or schedules, and desktop flows handle Windows applications. The best candidates are repeated tasks with clear rules.
Q: How do approval workflows work in Power Automate?
A: A trigger starts the flow, the flow sends an approval request to Teams or Outlook, waits for a response, then branches on approve or reject. It writes the outcome back to the record. Reminders and escalation rules handle approvers who are away or slow to answer.
Q: How long does a workflow automation project take?
A: It depends on the number of flows, systems and approval rules. A single approval flow is a small job, while a chain of flows across several systems takes longer. MP-365 builds the highest-value flow first so you see results early, then adds more from a ranked list.
Q: What is the difference between a cloud flow and a desktop flow?
A: A cloud flow connects online services through connectors and runs without a person at a computer. A desktop flow automates actions in Windows applications, usually where no connector exists. MP-365 prefers cloud flows because they are easier to monitor and maintain.
Q: Can Power Automate replace our classic Dynamics 365 workflows?
A: Often, yes. Cloud flows can take over most classic workflow and plug-in logic, and they are easier for administrators to read and change. MP-365 reviews each existing workflow and plug-in, then recommends which to move and which to leave alone.
Q: Do we need a developer to maintain flows?
A: Not usually. Cloud flows are built in a visual designer, so a trained administrator can handle small changes. MP-365 documents each flow, names an owner and sets up failure alerts. For larger changes you can call MP-365 on an ad hoc or ongoing basis.
Q: What happens when a flow fails?
A: A well-built flow records the failure and alerts a named owner. MP-365 adds error handling to each flow, such as retries for temporary problems and clear notifications for data issues. Without it, a failed run can go unnoticed for days.
Q: Can Power Automate connect to our ERP system?
A: Yes, when the ERP offers a connector or an API. MP-365 does not implement ERP, but it connects Dynamics 365 and Power Automate to ERP systems such as Business Central so data flows without double entry. Larger or higher-volume links use the integration services approach.
Q: How much does Power Automate consulting cost?
A: Cost depends on how many flows you need, the systems they touch and the approval rules. Microsoft sets license fees separately from consulting. MP-365 scopes a small first flow so you see the value before committing more. The pricing page explains how engagements work.
Q: Is Power Automate secure for business data?
A: Flows run under controls your administrators set. Power Platform data policies limit which connectors flows may use, and flows use connections with defined permissions. MP-365 reviews connectors and ownership before building, but it does not provide cybersecurity services.

Power Automate consulting pays back fastest when it starts with one process people already complain about. MP-365 can map that process, build the first flow on your Microsoft systems and show you what to automate next. For one common use, read about contract management automation.

## Power BI Consulting and Dashboards
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/power-platform/power-bi/

Power BI consulting from MP-365 replaces spreadsheet reports with live dashboards built on your Dynamics 365, SharePoint and business system data. MP-365 designs the data model, builds the reports and sets who can see which numbers.

bestFor: Sales, service and operations leaders whose reports are assembled by hand and whose numbers differ between teams.
includes: Report requirements, connections to Dynamics 365 and other sources, data model, dashboards, row-level security, refresh setup, testing and handover.
notIncluded: Data warehouse builds for unrelated systems, ERP implementation, custom software development, Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call about the decisions your leaders need to make. MP-365 lists the questions each dashboard must answer and where the data lives.

### What Power BI consulting includes
Power BI consulting includes working out which questions your leaders ask, finding the data that answers them, and building dashboards they trust. It also covers refresh schedules, security and training, so the reports keep working after launch.
MP-365 starts from the decision, not the chart. A pipeline dashboard exists to show a sales director which deals need attention this week, not to display every field in the CRM.

### Reporting problems MP-365 fixes first
- Reports built by hand: someone exports data, pastes it into Excel and fixes formulas before every meeting.
- Two sets of numbers: sales and finance quote different totals because each uses its own file.
- Stale data: leaders see last month's picture when they need this week's.
- Everyone sees everything: a regional manager can open data that belongs to another region.
- Dashboards nobody opens: the visuals answer questions that nobody asked.

### How Power BI connects to Dynamics 365 data
Connection option | How it works | Use it when | Watch for
Dataverse connector, import mode | Data is cached in Power BI and refreshed on a schedule | Most reports; Microsoft recommends import wherever possible | Data is as fresh as the last refresh
Dataverse connector, DirectQuery | Power BI queries Dataverse each time a report opens | A report needs near real-time data or stricter use of Dataverse security | Slower visuals on large tables
Dataverse (Legacy) connector | Reads data through the older Dataverse service interface | Query results larger than 80 MB, or image columns | Older connector; keep it for these cases only
SharePoint, Excel and other sources | Power BI connectors read lists, files and other databases | You need to combine CRM data with files or another business system | Messy source data needs cleaning first

### What it takes to connect Power BI to Dynamics 365
Connecting Power BI to Dynamics 365 is quick when the setup is right and confusing when it is not. Per Microsoft Learn (2026), the Dataverse connector needs the TDS endpoint setting enabled in your environment, and the connector needs TCP port 1433 or 5558 open. Many proxy servers do not handle this protocol.
Microsoft also documents a result-size limit of 80 MB per query on the Dataverse connector. MP-365 handles this by filtering rows, dropping unused columns and shaping the model before the report grows. Choice and lookup columns arrive as two columns each, so the model needs tidying before users see it.

### Power BI dashboards by audience
A good Power BI implementation gives each audience its own view of the same data. MP-365 designs these views with the people who use them, then tests each against the source system.

### Sales leadership dashboards
Sales dashboards show pipeline by stage, forecast against target, deals at risk and rep activity. They read directly from Dynamics 365 Sales, so the numbers match what reps see in the CRM. Managers can drill from region to rep to deal.

### Lead and marketing dashboards
Lead dashboards show where leads come from, how fast they are followed up and which sources turn into revenue. They depend on a clean lead process, which is why they pair with lead management and attribution. Teams using Dynamics 365 Customer Insights can add journey results.

### Service and operations dashboards
Operations dashboards show open work, ageing, ownership and backlog. For service teams they track cases by owner and urgency. For project teams they track milestones and late items, drawing on SharePoint lists and other sources where needed.

### Row-level security: who sees which rows
Row-level security limits each user to the rows they are allowed to see. In Power BI you define roles with DAX filter expressions in Power BI Desktop, publish the model, then add members to roles in the Power BI service (Microsoft Learn, 2026).
Two details matter in practice. Row-level security applies to workspace viewers, not to admins, members or contributors. And a dynamic role that uses the signed-in user's name lets one rule serve every manager, so a regional lead sees only their region.

### How MP-365 delivers Power BI implementation services
1. List the decisions: Interview leaders and write down the decisions each dashboard must support.
2. Locate the data: Identify where each number lives and who owns it, and note gaps and duplicates.
3. Build the data model: Shape tables and relationships, choose import or DirectQuery, and define measures once.
4. Draft the first dashboard: Build one dashboard for one audience and review it with its users.
5. Reconcile the numbers: Compare each figure to the source system until finance and sales agree.
6. Apply security and refresh: Set row-level security roles, workspace access and a refresh schedule.
7. Publish and train: Release to the Power BI service, train viewers and hand over the model to its owner.

### What you get from Power BI consulting services
- Dashboards: published reports for each audience, built on one shared model.
- A documented data model: tables, relationships and measures with plain-language definitions.
- Security setup: row-level security roles and workspace access matched to your org chart.
- Refresh and monitoring: a refresh schedule and an owner who is alerted when it fails.
- Reconciliation notes: proof that the dashboard totals match the source systems.
- Training and backlog: a session for viewers and a ranked list of next reports.

### Microsoft products involved in a Power BI project
A Power BI project uses Power BI Desktop to build the model and reports, and the Power BI service to publish, share and refresh them. Data usually comes from Microsoft Dataverse and Dynamics 365, with SharePoint, Excel and other business systems alongside. Microsoft's documentation calls the published data models semantic models.
Licensing for Power BI is set by Microsoft and is separate from consulting fees. The pricing page explains how MP-365 engages, and the license needs depend on who builds and who views.

### Proof: live dashboards that replaced hand-built sales reports
One MP-365 client lacked a single sales process, and reports were compiled by hand each month. MP-365 set up one tracking process and live dashboards for leadership, so the numbers came straight from the system. A second client got one lead process and dashboards for marketing and sales leaders.
For named client results, see the clients page.

### How to choose among Power BI consulting companies
Choose a Power BI partner that asks about decisions before charts and that can explain your source data. Ask who will build the model, how they check totals against source systems and what you own at handover. Ask also how they handle security, since many dashboards fail on access rather than design.
MP-365 is a small senior team that works in Dynamics 365, SharePoint and the Power Platform, so CRM data does not need translation.

### When Power BI is not the right fit
Power BI is not the right fit if your real problem is bad data entry. A dashboard on messy CRM records only shows the mess faster, and cleanup comes first. It also does not suit transaction screens where staff create records; that is a job for Power Apps. MP-365 does not build enterprise data warehouses for unrelated systems.

### Related Power Platform services
Dashboards are one part of the wider Power Platform service. Teams often pair them with Power Apps, which captures clean data at the source.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What does Power BI consulting include?
A: Power BI consulting includes defining the decisions your reports must support, finding and connecting the data, building a shared data model, designing dashboards, setting row-level security and refresh, and training users. MP-365 also reconciles dashboard totals against the source system so leaders trust them.
Q: How do you connect Power BI to Dynamics 365?
A: MP-365 uses the Dataverse connector in Power BI Desktop, which needs the TDS endpoint setting enabled in your environment. You then choose import mode for scheduled refresh or DirectQuery for near real-time data. Microsoft recommends import wherever possible, so MP-365 chooses DirectQuery only when a report needs it.
Q: How long does a Power BI dashboard project take?
A: It depends on the number of data sources, the state of the data and how many audiences need dashboards. A single dashboard on clean Dynamics 365 data moves fast. Combining several systems or fixing messy records takes longer. MP-365 delivers one audience first, then expands.
Q: What does Power BI implementation cost?
A: Cost depends on data sources, dashboard count and security needs. Microsoft sets Power BI license prices separately, based on who builds and who views reports. MP-365 scopes a first dashboard so you see value before committing more. See the pricing page for how engagements work.
Q: Do we need a data warehouse for Power BI?
A: Not usually. For Dynamics 365 and SharePoint reporting, Power BI can read the source data directly and model it in the report. A warehouse becomes useful when many unrelated systems must be combined at scale. MP-365 recommends the simplest design that meets your reporting needs.
Q: Can Power BI show real-time data from Dynamics 365?
A: Yes, with DirectQuery on the Dataverse connector, which queries the data when a report opens. Import mode refreshes on a schedule instead. Microsoft recommends import where possible, so MP-365 uses DirectQuery for reports where fresh data matters more than speed, such as a live service queue.
Q: How do you control who sees which data?
A: MP-365 uses row-level security. Roles are defined with DAX filters in Power BI Desktop, and members are assigned in the Power BI service. Microsoft notes that row-level security applies to workspace viewers, not admins, members or contributors, so MP-365 also designs workspace access carefully.
Q: Why do our reports show different numbers than the CRM?
A: The usual causes are different filters, stale refreshes, duplicate records or measures defined in several places. MP-365 defines each measure once in a shared model and reconciles totals against Dynamics 365 until the numbers agree. That also reveals data quality issues worth fixing at the source.
Q: Can you fix or redesign our existing Power BI reports?
A: Yes. MP-365 reviews existing reports for slow visuals, duplicated measures, broken refresh and loose access. Often the fix is to move to a shared data model rather than patch each report. The first step is a short review of the reports your leaders use most.
Q: Is Power BI the same as Excel?
A: No. Excel works well for ad hoc analysis by one person, while Power BI is built for shared, refreshed reports with a governed data model and role-based access. Many teams keep using Excel for analysis and use Power BI for the numbers leaders review each week.

Power BI consulting works when it starts with the decisions your leaders make and ends with numbers they trust. MP-365 can build the first dashboard on your Dynamics 365 data, reconcile it to the source and set up the security around it. For what leaders should see first, read about executive dashboards.

## Microsoft 365 Migration Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/microsoft-365-migration/

Microsoft 365 migration services move your email, files and, in a deal, your whole tenant into Microsoft 365 without stopping the business. MP-365 (Modern Partners 365), a Microsoft Solutions Partner, plans each move around how your users work, not around the tool.

### What Microsoft 365 migration services include
A Microsoft 365 migration moves data and habits. The data is mailboxes, personal files, team sites and sometimes an entire tenant. The habits are how people open Outlook, find a file and share a document on Monday morning.
Microsoft 365 was formerly called Office 365, and many teams still search for office 365 migration. The work is the same under either name. MP-365 groups it into three areas: email moves to Exchange Online, files moves to OneDrive and SharePoint, and tenant moves between companies.
Each area has its own Microsoft tools, limits and cutover risks. A plan that treats them as one copy job misses things users notice first, such as a broken Outlook profile or a shared link that no longer opens.

### Microsoft 365 migration services compared
Service | Best for | Typical outcome | Typical sources
Exchange to Microsoft 365 Migration | Organizations whose mailboxes still sit on Exchange Server or another mail system | Mailboxes, calendars and contacts in Exchange Online, with mail routing to the right place | Exchange Server (cutover, hybrid or staged) and IMAP mail systems
OneDrive Migration | Moving personal files and home drives into OneDrive | Files in OneDrive with folder structure kept and users shown where everything went | File shares, Windows known folders, another Microsoft 365 tenant
SharePoint Server upgrade and migration | Teams still running SharePoint Server 2010 to 2019 | Sites, libraries and permissions rebuilt in SharePoint Online | SharePoint Server and SharePoint Foundation
Tenant to tenant migration for mergers | Mergers, acquisitions and divestitures | Mail, files and users moved from one Microsoft 365 tenant to another | A Microsoft 365 tenant

### How to choose where to start
- Email is still on-premises. Start with Exchange. Mail is the workload users notice most, and it sets the identity and domain decisions for everything else.
- Files sit on file servers or local PCs. Start with OneDrive for personal files, and move shared departmental folders into SharePoint libraries.
- You run SharePoint Server. Plan the site migration first, because Microsoft ended support for SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 on July 14, 2026.
- A deal is closing. Start with the tenant plan. The surviving tenant and the domain decision shape every other step.
- You are unsure. Book a free consultation and bring a list of your systems. MP-365 will map them to a sequence.

### How MP-365 approaches a Microsoft 365 migration
1. Inventory the source: List mailboxes, shared mailboxes, file shares, sites, sizes and owners, so nothing is found for the first time on cutover day.
2. Confirm licensing and identity: Check that every user has the right Microsoft 365 license and that directory sync or user accounts exist where the method needs them.
3. Pick the method per workload: Choose cutover, hybrid, SharePoint Migration Tool, Migration Manager or a cross-tenant tool for each workload, and write down why.
4. Pilot with a small group: Move a few mailboxes and folders first, then check the user experience before scaling up.
5. Migrate in batches: Copy data in the background while people keep working, and report on every item that fails.
6. Cut over in a planned window: Switch mail routing, update DNS, and tell users exactly what changes on their device.
7. Verify and hand over: Confirm results with data owners, then retire the old system only after they sign off.

### Which Microsoft tool fits which source
Source | Microsoft tool | What it moves | What to know
Exchange 2010, 2013 or 2016 with fewer than 150 mailboxes | Cutover or express (minimal hybrid) migration | Mail, calendar items, tasks and contacts | Microsoft recommends this size range for a fast move; express migration needs a one-time directory sync
Exchange with more than 150 mailboxes | Exchange hybrid migration | Mail, calendar items, tasks and contacts | Moves a limited number of users at a time
Other IMAP mail systems | IMAP migration | Email only | Calendars and contacts do not move
On-premises file shares | SharePoint Migration Tool or Migration Manager | Files and folders to SharePoint, OneDrive or Teams | Migration Manager supports files up to 250 GB
Windows user folders | OneDrive Known Folder Move | Desktop, Documents and Pictures | Controlled by policy, rolled out in stages
