SharePoint Server 2010 to 2019 | SharePoint Migration Tool | Sites, lists, permissions, versions and some workflows | Run a scan first to find issues

### What drives the cost of Microsoft 365 migration services
Cost follows the number of users, the volume of data, the number of source systems and how much cleanup the data needs. The size of the mailbox or file share matters less than the number of exceptions inside it, such as shared mailboxes, long file paths and legal holds.
Microsoft license fees are separate and are paid to Microsoft or your license provider. MP-365 does not resell licenses. See MP-365 pricing for how engagements are scoped and billed.

### Common migration problems MP-365 plans for
- Outlook profiles. Users can need a new profile when the primary address or tenant changes.
- Shared mailboxes and delegates. Permissions are easy to miss and users notice immediately.
- Long paths and blocked names. Files with paths over 400 characters or reserved names fail on upload.
- Local PST files. Old archives sit on laptops and need a decision, not a surprise.
- Mail routing during coexistence. Mail between migrated and unmigrated users must keep arriving.
- Mobile devices. Phones that sync mail can need to be re-added after the switch.

### Why many Microsoft 365 migrations have a deadline
Microsoft ended support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 on October 14, 2025, and for SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 on July 14, 2026. Servers keep running after those dates, but they no longer receive fixes. That is the reason most mid-size organizations call MP-365 for a SharePoint Server migration or a mailbox move.

### Proof: staged upgrades to Microsoft 365
MP-365 has moved SharePoint environments from versions 2007, 2010, 2013 and 2016 to Microsoft 365 in stages for financial services and manufacturing organizations. Staging let each business unit move when its content was ready. See other work on the MP-365 clients page.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is included in a Microsoft 365 migration?
A: A Microsoft 365 migration includes planning, moving the data, cutting over mail routing or access, and supporting users afterward. The data can be mailboxes, OneDrive files, SharePoint sites or a whole tenant. MP-365 scopes each workload separately, because each uses a different Microsoft method.
Q: How long does a Microsoft 365 migration take?
A: It depends on mailbox sizes, file volume, network capacity and how many exceptions your data has. Microsoft also throttles mailbox moves to protect the service, so speed varies. MP-365 sizes your environment first, then gives a plan with dates tied to your own data rather than a generic estimate.
Q: How much do Microsoft 365 migration services cost?
A: Cost depends on user count, data volume, number of source systems and data cleanup. Microsoft license fees are separate and set by Microsoft. MP-365 does not resell licenses. The pricing page explains engagement models and the factors that move a quote up or down.
Q: Is an Office 365 migration different from a Microsoft 365 migration?
A: No. Microsoft renamed Office 365 to Microsoft 365, so the terms describe the same service. The tools are the same, including Exchange Online, OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Some older documents still say Office 365, which is why both phrases appear in searches.
Q: Will users lose email or files during the migration?
A: No, not when the migration is planned correctly. Data copies in the background while users keep working, and the final switch is short. What users do notice is a changed Outlook profile, a new file location or an updated sign-in, so MP-365 sends clear instructions before cutover.
Q: Do we need an Office 365 migration consultant, or can our IT team do it?
A: Your IT team can do a small move with Microsoft's tools. Outside help pays off when you have many mailboxes, a hybrid Exchange environment, long file paths, a tight cutover window or a tenant move. MP-365 can lead the project or support your team on the hard parts.
Q: Can Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint be migrated in one project?
A: Yes. MP-365 sequences them in one plan, usually mail first because it affects identity and domains, then files. Each workload still uses its own method and has its own limits, so the plan lists them separately. Moves between companies follow the tenant migration path.
Q: What should we do before a migration starts?
A: Name an owner, list your systems and gather admin access. Clean up what you do not want to move, such as unused mailboxes and old shares. Check that licenses are available. A short discovery call with MP-365 turns this into a checklist for your environment.
Q: What happens to our old servers after the migration?
A: Keep them read-only until data owners confirm the results, then retire them. In a hybrid Exchange setup, decommissioning needs planning because mail flow and directory sync may still depend on the old servers. MP-365 documents what the old servers did before anyone turns them off.
Q: Does MP-365 migrate between two Microsoft 365 tenants?
A: Yes. MP-365 handles tenant moves for mergers, acquisitions and divestitures, including mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint content and domain cutover. Microsoft's own tools have limits, especially for Teams. The cross-tenant migration page explains what moves and what does not.

Good Microsoft 365 migration services keep your users working, report every failure and leave your team in control of the new environment. MP-365 starts with an inventory of what you have, then sequences email, files and tenant moves around your business calendar.

## Exchange Online Migration Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/microsoft-365-migration/exchange-online-migration/

Exchange Online migration services move your mailboxes from Exchange Server or another mail system into Microsoft 365, using a cutover, express or hybrid plan chosen for your size and risk. MP-365 runs the project for IT leaders who need email to keep working while it happens.

bestFor: Organizations moving mailboxes from Exchange Server, or another mail system, to Exchange Online in Microsoft 365.
includes: Method selection, readiness checks, domain verification, directory sync and licensing, pilot and batch mailbox moves, mail flow and DNS cutover, Outlook and phone guidance, and decommissioning guidance.
notIncluded: Help desk or managed IT, Microsoft license resale, cybersecurity services and ERP implementation.
howItStarts: A discovery call about your Exchange version, mailbox count and domains, followed by a written scope.

### Exchange Online migration: which method fits
Method | Source | Fits when | Watch for
Cutover | Exchange Server | You have fewer than 150 mailboxes and want to move them in one short window | Microsoft supports up to 2,000 mailboxes but calls 150 or fewer more reasonable; by default 20 mailboxes migrate at once
Express (minimal hybrid) | Exchange 2010, 2013 or 2016 | You have a small number of mailboxes and no plan to keep directory sync running | Directory sync runs once and then stops, so you manage users in the cloud afterward
Full hybrid | Exchange 2010 or later | You have more than 150 mailboxes, or users must live on both sides for a while | Needs directory sync and the Hybrid Configuration Wizard, so setup takes more care
Staged | Exchange 2003 or 2007 | You have an older Exchange organization with more than 150 mailboxes | Needs directory sync, and users move in groups you define
IMAP | Other email systems, or Exchange 2000 and earlier | The source supports IMAP and you only need mail | Moves email only, not calendars, tasks or contacts

### Problems an Exchange Online migration solves
- Unsupported servers. Microsoft ended support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 on October 14, 2025, so the server no longer gets fixes.
- Server upkeep. Patching, certificates and storage on an on-premises mail server cost your team time every month.
- Mailbox limits. Users hit quotas and keep PST files on laptops that nobody backs up.
- Mobile and remote access. Staff outside the office depend on VPN or published servers to reach mail.
- A deal or reorganization. A new company structure needs mail in a tenant you can manage.

### How MP-365 runs an Exchange Online migration
1. Inventory the mail environment: Record the Exchange version, mailbox count and sizes, shared and resource mailboxes, public folders, journaling and any third-party archive.
2. Verify your domains: Add each email domain to Microsoft 365 and prove ownership with a DNS TXT record before any mailbox moves.
3. Choose the method: Match cutover, express hybrid, full hybrid, staged or IMAP to your size, Exchange version and timeline, and document the reason.
4. Prepare identity and licenses: Set up Microsoft Entra Connect where the method needs it and assign Exchange Online licenses to every user who will move.
5. Configure coexistence: Run the Hybrid Configuration Wizard or create the migration endpoint so mail flows between old and new mailboxes.
6. Pilot with test users: Move a few mailboxes first and check Outlook, mobile and shared mailbox access with the people who use them.
7. Migrate in batches: Copy mailbox data in the background, watch failures and skipped items, and complete batches in the window you agreed.
8. Cut over mail routing: Point the MX record and other mail DNS records to Microsoft 365 and confirm inbound and outbound mail.
9. Support users and decommission: Handle profile and device issues, then retire Exchange servers only after you confirm nothing still depends on them.

### Hybrid Exchange migration explained
A hybrid Exchange migration connects your on-premises Exchange organization to Exchange Online so mailboxes can move a few at a time while both sides keep working. Microsoft calls the setup tool the Hybrid Configuration Wizard.

### When minimal hybrid is enough
Minimal hybrid, also called express migration, suits organizations running Exchange 2010, 2013 or 2016 that plan to move everyone in a short period. It runs directory sync once, then turns it off, so you manage users in Microsoft 365 afterward.

### When full hybrid is worth the setup
Full hybrid fits larger organizations that move users in groups, or that need on-premises and cloud mailboxes to coexist for a long time. It keeps directory sync running, which adds setup work but gives you control over who moves and when.

### How to migrate Exchange to Office 365 without disruption
Disruption comes from three places: mail routing, Outlook profiles and mobile devices. MP-365 plans each one before the first mailbox moves. Mail routing stays correct during coexistence, Outlook is tested on a pilot group, and phones get written instructions.
Microsoft also throttles mailbox moves to protect the service, so copy speed varies. MP-365 starts copying early and keeps the final switch for a planned window, so a slow day for Microsoft's service does not move your cutover.

### Will users lose email during the migration?
No, not with a planned migration. Mail keeps arriving at either the old or the new mailbox while data copies in the background, and the final switch for each user is short.
What users notice is smaller: Outlook may prompt a restart or need a profile refresh, and phones may need to be re-added. MP-365 sends users clear instructions before cutover and watches for support requests on the first day.

### What you get from the migration
- A written migration plan. Method, order of batches, coexistence design and rollback points.
- Migrated mailboxes. User, shared and resource mailboxes in Exchange Online, with a report of any skipped items.
- Working mail flow. Inbound and outbound mail verified after the DNS change.
- User guidance. Short instructions for Outlook and phones, ready to send.
- A decommissioning checklist. What to confirm before shutting down old Exchange servers.

### Microsoft products and tools involved
- Exchange Online in Microsoft 365, the destination for the mailboxes.
- Exchange Server 2010 and later or another mail system as the source.
- Hybrid Configuration Wizard to connect on-premises Exchange to Exchange Online.
- Microsoft Entra Connect to sync users from on-premises Active Directory.
- Exchange admin center and Exchange Online PowerShell to create and monitor migration batches.
- Microsoft Purview Import service for PST files that need to come into mailboxes.

### What affects the effort and cost of an Exchange Online migration
Effort depends on the mailbox count, the Exchange version, whether you need coexistence, and how many shared mailboxes, public folders and PST files you have. Public folders move separately from user mailboxes, so MP-365 scopes them as their own task.
Microsoft license fees are separate and MP-365 does not resell licenses. For how engagements are priced, see MP-365 pricing.

### When Exchange Online migration is not the right fit
This service is for moving into your own Microsoft 365 tenant. If you are moving mailboxes between two Microsoft 365 tenants after a deal, you need tenant to tenant migration, which uses different Microsoft tools. If your main problem is files rather than mail, start with OneDrive migration.
For a very small team with a handful of mailboxes, an admin can often use Microsoft's guided tools without outside help. See the wider Microsoft 365 migration services page to compare options.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you migrate Exchange to Exchange Online?
A: You verify your domain, choose a method, license users, then move mailboxes with cutover, hybrid, staged or IMAP migration. Mail data copies in the background. Finally you change the MX record to Microsoft 365 and retire the old servers. MP-365 picks the method from your Exchange version and mailbox count.
Q: What is a hybrid Exchange migration?
A: A hybrid Exchange migration connects on-premises Exchange to Exchange Online so mailboxes can move in groups while both sides keep working. You set it up with the Hybrid Configuration Wizard. It suits larger organizations or any move that needs coexistence between old and new mailboxes.
Q: Will users lose email during the migration?
A: No. Mail continues to arrive at the old or new mailbox while data copies in the background. The final switch for each mailbox is short. Users may need to restart Outlook or refresh their profile, and phones may need to be re-added. MP-365 sends instructions before cutover.
Q: Which Exchange Online migration method should we choose?
A: Choose by mailbox count and Exchange version. Microsoft suggests cutover or express migration for fewer than 150 mailboxes on Exchange 2010 to 2016, and hybrid for more. Staged migration applies to Exchange 2003 and 2007, and IMAP covers other systems. MP-365 documents the reason in your plan.
Q: How many mailboxes can a cutover migration handle?
A: Microsoft states that cutover migration supports up to 2,000 mailboxes, but calls 150 or fewer a more reasonable number because of how long creating and moving 2,000 users takes. Larger organizations are better served by a hybrid migration that moves limited groups of users at a time.
Q: Why does mailbox migration speed vary?
A: Microsoft throttles discretionary workloads such as mailbox moves to protect the service for all customers. Speed also depends on mailbox size, network capacity and the migration method. By default, simple Exchange migrations move 20 mailboxes at once across all batches, so MP-365 plans around that limit.
Q: Is Exchange Server 2016 or 2019 still supported?
A: No. Microsoft ended support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 on October 14, 2025, according to Microsoft Learn. The servers still run, but they receive no fixes. Microsoft's guidance points to Microsoft 365 or Exchange Server Subscription Edition, and MP-365 can help with the Microsoft 365 route.
Q: What happens to Outlook and phones after migration?
A: Outlook usually finds the migrated mailbox after the DNS and profile settings are correct, though some users need a restart or a new profile. Phones that sync mail often need to be re-added. MP-365 tests these on a pilot group first and prepares short instructions for everyone.
Q: Can an IMAP migration move calendars and contacts?
A: No. IMAP migration copies email only. Microsoft states that cutover, staged and hybrid migrations copy mail, contacts, calendar items and tasks, while IMAP does not. If you must keep calendars, MP-365 looks for another route or plans a manual calendar export.
Q: What happens to public folders and shared mailboxes?
A: Shared and resource mailboxes are part of the inventory and move with the users who rely on them. Public folders move separately from user mailboxes, so MP-365 scopes them as their own task. Both need a check after migration, because permissions are easy to miss.

A good Exchange Online migration keeps mail flowing, tells users exactly what changes and leaves your team with a clean Microsoft 365 setup. MP-365 chooses the method from your real mailbox count and Exchange version, then runs the pilot, batches and cutover with you.

## OneDrive Migration Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/microsoft-365-migration/onedrive-migration/

OneDrive migration moves users' files from file shares, laptops or another Microsoft 365 tenant into each person's OneDrive, with folder structure, permissions and sharing in mind. MP-365 picks the Microsoft tool that fits your source, cleans up what would fail, and tells users where everything went.

bestFor: Organizations moving personal files from file shares, home drives, local PCs or another Microsoft 365 tenant into OneDrive.
includes: Content scan, tool selection, path and file name cleanup, pilot, bulk upload, Known Folder Move policy, sharing and permission guidance, and user communication.
notIncluded: Help desk or managed IT, Microsoft license resale, cybersecurity services and ERP implementation. Shared department folders are scoped as SharePoint work.
howItStarts: A discovery call about where the files live today and how many users are involved, then a scan of the source.

### Common OneDrive migration scenarios
- Home drives on a file server. Each user's personal folder becomes that user's OneDrive.
- Files on local PCs. Desktop, Documents and Pictures move into OneDrive and keep syncing.
- Files in an older SharePoint Server library. Personal content moves to OneDrive, team content to SharePoint Online.
- Users leaving another tenant. After a merger or divestiture, OneDrive accounts move between Microsoft 365 tenants.

### OneDrive migration tool options compared
Tool | What it moves | Best for | Limits to know
SharePoint Migration Tool | Files from file shares and SharePoint Server 2010 to 2019 into SharePoint, OneDrive or Teams | An admin running tasks from one machine, with saved tasks that re-run for new or changed files | Run its scan first; it does not support Windows authentication when several providers are set up
Migration Manager | File share content into SharePoint, OneDrive or Teams | Many users at once, using agents on several servers and a CSV file for multiple user migrations | Files up to 250 GB; the source must support SMB 2.0 or higher
Known Folder Move | Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Screenshots and Camera Roll from Windows PCs | Files that already sit on user devices | Policy-driven; roll it out in stages to protect the network
OneDrive sync app or browser upload | Small sets of files added by the user or admin | A handful of users with little data | The website copies up to 2,500 files at once; use the desktop app for large transfers
Cross-tenant OneDrive migration | OneDrive accounts between two Microsoft 365 tenants | Mergers, acquisitions and divestitures | One-time move with no incremental passes; not supported for GCC, GCC High or DoD

### OneDrive migration limits to check before you start
- File size. Microsoft supports files up to 250 GB for OneDrive and SharePoint upload, download and sync.
- Path length. The full path, including the OneDrive URL, cannot exceed 400 characters, so deep folder trees fail.
- Invalid characters. File and folder names cannot use characters such as quotation marks, colons, asterisks or question marks.
- Reserved names. Names such as CON, PRN, AUX, NUL and desktop.ini are blocked.
- Sync size. Microsoft recommends syncing no more than 300,000 items in total, so very large libraries need a plan for what stays online-only.
- Account size in cross-tenant moves. A migrated OneDrive account can hold at most 5 TB or 1 million items, and holds block the move.

### How MP-365 runs a OneDrive migration
1. Scan the source: Find file counts, sizes, deep paths, blocked names and files over 250 GB before anything moves.
2. Decide what goes where: Send personal files to OneDrive and shared team folders to SharePoint, and agree the mapping with data owners.
3. Clean up what would fail: Shorten paths, rename blocked files and remove duplicates and abandoned folders with the owners' approval.
4. Choose the tool: Select SharePoint Migration Tool, Migration Manager, Known Folder Move or a cross-tenant move for each source.
5. Pilot with a small group: Migrate a few users, check their files and sync, and fix issues before the main run.
6. Run the migration in waves: Upload in batches that suit your network, re-run saved tasks for late changes, and review reports for failed items.
7. Switch users over: Retire the old drive mapping, turn on OneDrive sync and send each user a short guide to their new location.

### OneDrive migration questions MP-365 hears most
Three questions come up on almost every project: how files get to OneDrive, whether anything limits size, and what happens to links people already use. The answers depend on the source system.

### How do you migrate user files to OneDrive?
You scan the source, then copy files with a Microsoft migration tool into each user's OneDrive. Admins use the SharePoint Migration Tool or Migration Manager for file shares, and Known Folder Move for files already on Windows PCs.

### Is there a size limit when migrating files to OneDrive?
Yes. Microsoft supports individual files up to 250 GB, and a full path of no more than 400 characters. The tool reports files that break these rules, and MP-365 fixes or excludes them with the owner's agreement.

### What happens to sharing links after migration?
Links that point to the old file share stop working, because OneDrive is a new location with its own links. Users re-share what they need from OneDrive. In a cross-tenant move, Microsoft leaves a redirect at the old OneDrive so old links keep opening for people who still have access to the new one.

### OneDrive or SharePoint: where should files go?
Personal working files belong in OneDrive, and files that a team owns belong in SharePoint. A file that sits in one person's OneDrive depends on that person staying with the company and sharing it correctly.
For shared department folders, use file share to SharePoint migration, which maps folders to libraries with metadata and permissions. MP-365 splits a file server between the two so each file lands in the right home.

### What you get from the migration
- A source scan report. File counts, sizes and every item that would fail.
- A mapping document. Which folders go to OneDrive, which go to SharePoint, and who approved it.
- Migrated files. Folder structure kept, with a report of anything excluded.
- A Known Folder Move policy. Configured and staged where it applies to your Windows devices.
- User guidance. A short guide to the new location, sync and sharing.

### What affects the effort and cost of OneDrive migration
Effort follows the number of users, the volume of files, how clean the source is and how many exceptions need a decision. A tidy file share with short paths moves with little rework. An old share with deep folders, duplicates and blocked names needs cleanup first.
Microsoft license fees are separate, and MP-365 does not resell licenses. MP-365 pricing explains how engagements are scoped.

### When OneDrive migration is not the right fit
OneDrive is not the right home for files that many people edit together, such as project folders or department records. Those belong in SharePoint or Teams. If the real need is email, see Exchange to Microsoft 365 migration.
If you are moving OneDrive accounts between companies, the work follows tenant to tenant migration, with Microsoft's cross-tenant tools. The wider Microsoft 365 migration services page shows how these pieces fit together.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you migrate user files to OneDrive?
A: Scan the source, clean up what would fail, then copy files into each user's OneDrive. Use the SharePoint Migration Tool or Migration Manager for file shares, and Known Folder Move for files on Windows PCs. MP-365 picks the tool per source, pilots it, then runs the migration in waves.
Q: Is there a size limit when migrating files to OneDrive?
A: Yes. Microsoft supports individual files up to 250 GB, and Migration Manager supports the same size for file share migrations. Full paths are limited to 400 characters. Cross-tenant OneDrive accounts can hold at most 5 TB or 1 million items. Your scan shows what exceeds these limits.
Q: What happens to sharing links after migration?
A: Links to the old file share stop working, so users re-share files from OneDrive. In a cross-tenant OneDrive move, Microsoft leaves a redirect at the old location, and shared links keep opening for people who still have access to the new one. Redirects stay until the source tenant is deprovisioned.
Q: Which OneDrive migration tool should we use?
A: Use the tool that matches the source. SharePoint Migration Tool suits an admin moving file shares or SharePoint Server content. Migration Manager suits many users through agents. Known Folder Move suits files already on PCs. Cross-tenant tools handle moves between Microsoft 365 tenants. MP-365 chooses after scanning.
Q: Can Known Folder Move replace a file migration?
A: Only for files on user devices. Known Folder Move redirects Desktop, Documents and Pictures to OneDrive on Windows PCs. It does not pull files from a file server. If folders are redirected to a network share, Microsoft advises using Migration Manager first, then turning on Known Folder Move.
Q: Do file permissions carry over from a file share?
A: It depends on the tool settings. Migration Manager and the SharePoint Migration Tool have options to preserve file share permissions. Most personal OneDrive content needs only the owner, so MP-365 usually keeps permissions for shared folders going to SharePoint and applies owner-only access to home drives.
Q: Does version history move with the files?
A: From SharePoint Server, the SharePoint Migration Tool lets you decide how much file history to keep. File shares hold no version history to carry over, so files arrive as current versions. MP-365 sets this per source and records the choice in your migration plan.
Q: What happens to Outlook PST files in user folders?
A: Microsoft supports PST files in OneDrive, but they sync less often, and Known Folder Move migrates them when Group Policy is set up for it. MP-365 usually recommends importing PST content into mailboxes with the Microsoft Purview Import service instead of leaving archives in OneDrive.
Q: What happens to files with long paths or blocked names?
A: They fail the upload. Microsoft limits full paths to 400 characters and blocks names such as CON, PRN, AUX, NUL and desktop.ini. The scan lists every affected item. MP-365 shortens paths and renames files with the owner's approval, or excludes them and documents why.
Q: Can OneDrive accounts move between Microsoft 365 tenants?
A: Yes. Microsoft's cross-tenant OneDrive migration moves accounts during mergers and divestitures. It is a one-time move without incremental passes, needs a per-user license, and is not supported for GCC, GCC High or DoD. See cross-tenant migration for the full picture.

A OneDrive migration succeeds when files arrive where users expect them, in a structure that does not break. MP-365 scans the source, fixes what would fail and chooses the right Microsoft tool for each group of users.

## Tenant to Tenant Migration for Mergers
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/tenant-to-tenant-migration/

Tenant to tenant migration moves email, files and users from one Microsoft 365 tenant to another when companies merge, one buys another or a division is sold. MP-365 plans the move around what Microsoft's tools can and cannot carry, so IT leaders see the gaps before they commit to a deal timeline.

### What is a tenant to tenant migration?
A tenant to tenant migration moves user data from one organization's Microsoft 365 tenant into another's. A tenant is the Microsoft 365 environment your company owns, with its own users, domains, mailboxes and SharePoint sites. People also search for an Office 365 tenant migration, and Microsoft 365 is the current name for the same service.
Microsoft describes the work as moving content, not identities. You create and configure the users in the target tenant, and the tools move the data to match them. That is why a good plan starts with the user list, not the mailbox copy.
The work sits inside a wider M&A IT effort, and it has one fixed rule: each tenant owns its own domains, so email addresses and sign-ins change at some point in the move.

### What Microsoft's cross-tenant tools do and do not support
Tool | What it moves | What it does not move | What to know
Cross-tenant mailbox migration | Email, contacts, calendar, tasks and notes, plus Recoverable Items and voicemail | Teams chat folder content, Teams meeting links, signatures, Microsoft 365 Groups, mailboxes on hold | The source mailbox is deleted after a successful move
Cross-tenant OneDrive migration | User OneDrive accounts, with a redirect left at the old location | Accounts on hold, or above 5 TB or 1 million items | One-time move with no incremental passes; not supported for GCC, GCC High or DoD
Cross-tenant SharePoint migration | Group-connected, modern, classic and communication sites, including the files of Teams-connected sites | Teams content and channels, 2010 and 2013 workflows, apps, Power Apps and automations | Licensed per 100 GB, and Microsoft's page says Enterprise Agreement customers only
Migration Orchestrator | Mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams chats and Teams meetings in one batch | Identities, Teams and channels, SharePoint sites | Batches are limited to 100 users; migrations are not subject to SLAs
FastTrack cross-tenant service | Exchange Online, SharePoint and OneDrive | Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and Planner | Invitation only, with a minimum of 150 licenses; US Government and Education not supported
Microsoft Entra cross-tenant synchronization | Nothing; it creates guest-style users for access | All data | Microsoft says it is not a migration tool, because the source tenant is still needed to sign in

### What the Microsoft tool limits mean for a deal
As of November 2026, Microsoft's own cross-tenant tools cover mailboxes, OneDrive accounts and SharePoint site content. They do not move Teams channels, and the mailbox tool does not move Microsoft 365 Groups. A deal that depends on Teams history, group structures or Planner boards needs a separate plan.
MP-365 lists those gaps during scoping and tells you which items to rebuild, which to archive and which to leave behind. Where a Microsoft tool does not cover a workload, MP-365 says so before you commit rather than during cutover.

### Merger, acquisition or divestiture: how the plan differs
The deal type decides which tenant survives and which way data flows. Microsoft describes three migration models: a single-event cutover, a phased move in batches, and a tenant move or split for divestitures.

### Acquisition: move into the buyer's tenant
In an acquisition, the acquired company's users, mail and files usually move into the buyer's tenant. The buyer's IT sets the naming, license and policy standards. Plan for the acquired company's domains, which must leave their old tenant before the buyer's tenant can use them.

### Merger: choose the surviving tenant
In a merger of equals, pick the surviving tenant on facts: user count, licenses, data volume, policies and compliance posture. The other tenant moves in. Until the cutover, the two sides run side by side, which is covered by tenant coexistence and domain cutover.

### Divestiture: split users out into a new tenant
In a divestiture, a subset of users leaves for a new tenant while everyone else stays. The hard part is deciding which shared mailboxes, sites and groups belong to which side. MP-365 builds that ownership list first, then moves the divested users' data.

### How MP-365 approaches tenant to tenant migration
1. Inventory both tenants: List users, domains, mailboxes, shared mailboxes, Teams, SharePoint sites, groups, licenses and any data on hold.
2. Pick the target and the model: Decide which tenant survives, then choose single-event, phased or split migration for the deal.
3. Map what moves and what does not: Match each workload to a Microsoft tool and list items that must be rebuilt, such as Teams channels and Microsoft 365 Groups.
4. Confirm licensing: Check that every migrating user has the Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on before any move starts.
5. Prepare the target users: Create the user objects and mail users in the target tenant with the attributes Microsoft's tools require.
6. Set up trust and coexistence: Configure cross-tenant trust, directory visibility and calendar sharing so both companies keep working.
7. Pilot, then migrate in batches: Move a pilot group, review results with their managers, then migrate mailboxes, OneDrive and sites in batches.
8. Cut over the domain: Move the email domain to the surviving tenant, update DNS, and walk users through their new sign-in.
9. Close out the source: Confirm data owners are satisfied, then retire or reduce the source tenant on an agreed schedule.

### Tenant migration services at MP-365
Service | Best for | Typical outcome
Cross-Tenant Mailbox, Teams & File Migration | Moving mailboxes, Teams data and files between Microsoft 365 tenants | Mail, OneDrive and SharePoint content in the target tenant, with a clear list of what was rebuilt
Tenant Coexistence & Domain Cutover | Keeping two tenants working together until the domain moves | Shared directory view, calendar sharing and a planned domain cutover

### What cannot move between tenants and what to do instead
- Teams channels and posts. Microsoft's tools do not move them. Rebuild the team structure and decide what history to archive.
- Microsoft 365 Groups. The mailbox tool does not move them, so recreate groups in the target tenant.
- Sensitivity labels. Microsoft says labels are not exported, so recreate them in the target tenant.
- Outlook signatures. They are not migrated and must be recreated.
- Teams meeting links. Existing meeting URLs are invalid in the target tenant, so meetings must be recreated.
- Workflows, apps and Power Apps on SharePoint sites. Rebuild and reconnect them after the site moves.
- Mailboxes and OneDrive accounts on hold. Microsoft blocks the move, so a hold plan is part of scoping.

### Licensing and cost for tenant to tenant migration
Microsoft requires a Cross-Tenant User Data Migration license for each migrating user. It is a one-time fee per user, can be assigned to either the source or target user, and covers mailbox and OneDrive migration. Microsoft says it makes no exceptions to this requirement, and migrations fail without it.
MP-365 does not resell Microsoft licenses, so you buy the add-on from Microsoft or your license provider. MP-365's own fees depend on user count, data, number of domains and how many items need rebuilding. See pricing for how engagements are scoped.

### How long does a tenant to tenant migration take?
The time depends on the number of users, the amount of content, the workloads selected and overall Microsoft service traffic. Microsoft states that cross-tenant migrations are not subject to SLAs, so no one can promise a fixed finish.
MP-365 plans around dependencies you control: user preparation, licensing, trust setup, the pilot and the domain cutover. It then builds the schedule backward from your deal milestones, such as the day one legal entity change.

### Related Microsoft 365 migration work
Not every deal needs a tenant move. If you are consolidating mail into your own tenant, see Exchange to Microsoft 365 migration. The wider Microsoft 365 migration services page covers files, mail and SharePoint outside of deals, and the MP-365 services overview lists everything else.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is a tenant-to-tenant migration?
A: A tenant-to-tenant migration moves user data from one Microsoft 365 tenant to another, usually because of a merger, acquisition or divestiture. It covers mailboxes, OneDrive files and SharePoint content, plus a plan for domains and users. Microsoft's tools move content, so you must prepare the user accounts in the target tenant.
Q: How long does a tenant-to-tenant migration take?
A: It depends on user count, data volume, the workloads you choose and Microsoft service traffic. Microsoft states that these migrations are not subject to SLAs. MP-365 builds your schedule from the preparation steps you control and the deal milestones you must meet, rather than from a generic estimate.
Q: What happens to Teams and SharePoint in a merger?
A: SharePoint site content can move with Microsoft's cross-tenant SharePoint migration, but Teams channels and their posts do not move with Microsoft's tools. A Teams-connected site moves as a SharePoint site only. MP-365 rebuilds the team structure in the target tenant and helps you decide what history to archive.
Q: Does Microsoft have a built-in tool for tenant migration?
A: Yes. Microsoft offers cross-tenant mailbox migration, cross-tenant OneDrive migration, cross-tenant SharePoint migration and Migration Orchestrator. They need a per-user license and prepared target users. They do not cover everything, especially Teams channels and Microsoft 365 Groups, so most projects still involve rebuilding some items.
Q: Can Teams chats move between tenants?
A: Partly. Microsoft's Migration Orchestrator lists Teams chats and meetings as workloads, and it copies them rather than moving them, so duplicate threads can exist in both tenants. Teams channels are not moved. The older mailbox tool does not migrate the Teams chat folder. Check current availability with Microsoft before planning around it.
Q: What licenses do we need for a tenant migration?
A: Each migrating user needs the Microsoft Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on, a one-time per-user fee that can be assigned to the source or target user. Users also need normal Microsoft 365 licenses in the target tenant. MP-365 does not resell licenses, so you buy through Microsoft or your provider.
Q: Can two tenants use the same domain name?
A: No. Microsoft states that source and target tenant domain names must be unique for mailbox migration, and a domain can be verified in only one tenant. So users get target-tenant addresses during the move, and the domain cutover happens later. See coexistence and domain cutover.
Q: Is Microsoft Entra cross-tenant synchronization a migration tool?
A: No. Microsoft states that cross-tenant synchronization is not a migration tool, because the source tenant is still required for users to sign in, and data such as OneDrive and SharePoint would still need to move. It is useful for access between tenants during coexistence, not for the move itself.
Q: Can we migrate between tenants in GCC, GCC High or DoD?
A: Support is limited. Microsoft says cross-tenant OneDrive migration is not supported for GCC, GCC High or DoD, cross-cloud moves are not supported, and its FastTrack service excludes US Government customers. MP-365 does not provide compliance certification, so confirm requirements with Microsoft and your compliance team early.
Q: What is the difference between coexistence and migration?
A: Migration moves the data. Coexistence keeps the two companies working together before, during and after the move, with shared directory visibility, calendar sharing and mail routing. Most deals need both. MP-365 covers coexistence in its tenant coexistence and domain cutover service.

Tenant to tenant migration works when you know early what Microsoft's tools carry and what they leave behind. MP-365 scopes the gaps first, then runs mail, files and the domain cutover to fit your deal calendar. For the wider deal, read about M&A IT integration and separation.

## Cross-Tenant Mailbox, Teams and File Migration
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/tenant-to-tenant-migration/mailbox-teams-files/

Cross-tenant mailbox migration moves users' Exchange Online mailboxes from one Microsoft 365 tenant to another during a merger, acquisition or divestiture, and MP-365 pairs it with OneDrive, SharePoint and a rebuild plan for Teams. You get a clear list of what Microsoft's tools move, what they skip, and what your users will see on day one.

bestFor: IT teams in a merger, acquisition or divestiture who must move users between two Microsoft 365 tenants.
includes: Scoping of mailbox, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams moves, target user preparation, trust and endpoint setup, pilot and batch migration, day-one user guidance, and a rebuild list for items Microsoft's tools do not move.
notIncluded: Cybersecurity services, managed IT or help desk, Microsoft license resale and ERP implementation. The Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on is bought from Microsoft.
howItStarts: A discovery call about both tenants, followed by a written scope that lists what moves and what is rebuilt.

### Cross-tenant mailbox migration: what moves and what does not
Item | Moves? | What to know
Email, contacts, calendar, tasks and notes | Yes | Microsoft moves user-visible content plus Recoverable Items (deletions, versions and purges)
Archive mailboxes | Yes | The archive GUID must exist on the target user; users with up to 12 auxiliary archives are supported
Shared mailboxes | Yes | Only store permissions are kept, so check access after the move
Voicemail | Yes | Voicemail attachments arrive in the target mailbox; they do not show in the Teams client in the target
Teams meetings in the calendar | Moved, but links break | The meeting URL is not updated, so recreate the meetings
Teams chat folder content | No | The source admin can still search and export it with a content search
Outlook Outbox items | No | The Outbox is stored locally in the Outlook client
Signatures | No | Users must recreate them
Microsoft 365 Groups | No | Recreate the groups in the target tenant
Mailboxes on any hold | Blocked | Remove or plan the hold before the move

### How do you migrate mailboxes between Microsoft 365 tenants?
You prepare both tenants, create matching mail users in the target tenant, then run the move from the target tenant as migration batches. Exchange's mailbox replication service copies the mailbox, and at completion the source mailbox becomes a mail user that points to the target.
Microsoft supports cross-tenant mailbox moves for cloud-only tenants, hybrid tenants or a mix of the two. Admins use Exchange Online PowerShell or the new Exchange admin center to submit batches.

### What must be in place before a cross-tenant mailbox move
- Licenses. Each migrating user needs the Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on, or the migration fails.
- A scoping group. The source tenant needs a mail-enabled security group that limits which mailboxes may leave.
- Trust. The target tenant needs a migration application and endpoint. Both tenants need an organization relationship that allows mailbox moves.
- Target mail users. Each user must exist in the target with the source ExchangeGUID, ArchiveGUID where used, and x500 addresses copied over.
- Unique domains. The source and target tenants cannot use the same domain name during the move.
- Role holders. An Organization Administrator sets the move capability, and the Move Mailboxes role runs the batches.

### How MP-365 runs a cross-tenant migration
1. Scope users and workloads: Agree which mailboxes, OneDrive accounts and SharePoint sites move, and which Teams items are rebuilt.
2. Confirm licenses and holds: Check the Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on for each user and list every mailbox or OneDrive account on hold.
3. Set up trust between tenants: Create the migration application, endpoint and organization relationships, and scope the source with a mail-enabled security group.
4. Create the target mail users: Build mail users in the target tenant with the matching GUIDs, x500 addresses and target-tenant addresses.
5. Validate before any move: Test the endpoint and run Microsoft's validation script to catch attribute mismatches on all objects at once.
6. Pilot, then submit batches: Move a pilot group, then submit larger batches early so content syncs before the agreed completion date.
7. Complete and fix day-one issues: Update on-premises mail users if you run hybrid, rebuild Outlook profiles and confirm shared mailbox access.
8. Move files and rebuild Teams: Run OneDrive and SharePoint moves, then recreate teams, channels and groups in the target tenant.

### Teams migration tenant to tenant: what Microsoft supports
Microsoft supports moving Teams chats and meetings for individual users, but not Teams channels. The three parts of Teams behave differently, so MP-365 plans each one on its own.

### Teams chats and meetings
Microsoft's Migration Orchestrator can migrate Teams chats and meetings with mailboxes and OneDrive. It copies them, so the original content stays in the source tenant and duplicate threads can appear in both. After the move, users should use only their target identity in Teams.
The standalone mailbox tool does not migrate the Teams chat folder. The source tenant administrator can still search and export that content with a content search.

### Teams channels and their files
Microsoft's Migration Orchestrator documentation states that Teams and channels stay in the source tenant. The cross-tenant SharePoint tool moves the SharePoint site behind a team, but not the Teams content, channels or structure.
That means the files of a team can arrive in the target tenant while the team itself does not.

### Rebuilding teams in the target tenant
MP-365 recreates teams and channels in the target tenant from a list you approve, then connects them to the migrated sites. Microsoft requires the target Microsoft 365 Groups for group-connected sites to be precreated in a specific way, and they cannot be linked to an existing site. The order of work therefore matters.

### Cross tenant SharePoint migration and user data migration
Microsoft's cross-tenant tools split into user data (mailboxes and OneDrive) and shared data (SharePoint sites). The two use different licenses and different prerequisites.

### How cross tenant SharePoint migration works
The cross-tenant SharePoint tool moves group-connected sites, modern sites, classic sites and communication sites, and leaves a redirect at the old location so existing links keep working. It is a one-time move with no incremental passes.
Target sites must not exist before the move, source sites must be in read and write mode, and each site can hold at most 5 TB or 1 million items. Paths cannot exceed 400 characters. Workflows, apps and Power Apps must be recreated.

### How cross tenant user data migration is licensed
User data migration needs the Cross-Tenant User Data Migration add-on, a one-time per-user fee that can be assigned on the source or target user. As of November 2026, Microsoft's SharePoint page says shared data licenses are priced per 100 GB moved and are offered to Enterprise Agreement customers. MP-365 does not resell either license.

### What users see on day one after the move
Users have to rebuild their Outlook profile with their new sign-in name and primary email address, then let Outlook resync their data. Microsoft explains that the old primary address is no longer on the mailbox, so the existing profile cannot find it. Plan the network load, because many profiles download data at once.
Mail sent before the move stays replyable only if the old x500 addresses were copied to the target user. Teams in the source tenant also has limited functionality for the user, and the source mailbox and calendar are no longer reachable there. MP-365 turns these facts into a short user guide for each batch.

### When cross-tenant migration is not the right fit
If you only need people from two companies to share calendars and find each other, see tenant coexistence and domain cutover instead of moving data. If you are consolidating mail inside one tenant, use Exchange to Microsoft 365 migration.
Microsoft also directs customers with more than 50,000 mailboxes to their account team for guidance. For the wider tenant plan, see M&A tenant migration, and for effort and cost, see MP-365 pricing.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you migrate mailboxes between Microsoft 365 tenants?
A: Prepare both tenants with a migration application, endpoint and organization relationship, create matching mail users in the target tenant, then submit migration batches from the target. The source mailbox becomes a mail user that points to the target. Each migrating user needs the Cross-Tenant User Data Migration license.
Q: Can Teams chats move between tenants?
A: Partly. Microsoft's Migration Orchestrator lists Teams chats and meetings as workloads and copies them, so duplicates can exist in both tenants. The standalone mailbox tool does not migrate the Teams chat folder. Teams channels do not move with Microsoft's tools. Confirm current availability with Microsoft before you build the plan around it.
Q: What cannot be migrated between tenants?
A: Microsoft's mailbox tool does not move Teams chat folder content, Outbox items, signatures, Microsoft 365 Groups or mailboxes on hold. Teams channels stay in the source tenant. SharePoint workflows, apps and Power Apps must be recreated, and sensitivity labels are not exported. MP-365 lists each item in your scope.
Q: Can I migrate SharePoint sites between tenants?
A: Yes. Microsoft's cross-tenant SharePoint migration moves site content, leaves a redirect behind and supports sites up to 5 TB or 1 million items. Target sites must not exist beforehand, and Microsoft's page states that licenses are offered to Enterprise Agreement customers as of November 2026. The move cannot run incrementally.
Q: How many mailboxes can go in one batch?
A: Microsoft advises no more than 2,000 mailboxes per batch for the standard mailbox tool, and Migration Orchestrator batches are limited to 100 users. Submitting batches early lets content sync with no impact on users until completion. For over 50,000 mailboxes, Microsoft points customers to their account team.
Q: What happens to a mailbox on legal hold?
A: Microsoft blocks the move for any mailbox on any type of hold. You need to plan for these users before scoping ends, either by removing the hold under your legal team's direction or by choosing another approach. OneDrive accounts with a hold policy are blocked the same way.
Q: Do users need to rebuild their Outlook profile?
A: Yes, for the first sign-in after the move. The old primary email address no longer exists on the target mailbox, so Outlook cannot find it. Users create a profile with the new sign-in name and address, then Outlook resyncs the mailbox. MP-365 provides a step-by-step guide for each batch.
Q: Do shared mailboxes move and keep working?
A: Yes, shared mailboxes move, but only the store permissions are kept. Check full access and send-as rights after the move, and confirm that the people who need them have migrated. MP-365 includes shared mailboxes in the access review so no team loses its inbox on cutover day.
Q: Are Microsoft 365 Groups migrated across tenants?
A: No. Microsoft states that the cross-tenant mailbox feature does not support migrating Microsoft 365 Groups. You recreate them in the target tenant, and group-connected SharePoint sites need their target groups precreated in a specific way. MP-365 builds the group list with you before any site moves.
Q: Can the source admin still access a mailbox after it moves?
A: No. Microsoft deletes the source mailbox after a successful move, so it is not available, discoverable or accessible in the source tenant, and eDiscovery there stops working. If the source needs a copy, copy the content to another mailbox before the move. MP-365 flags this during scoping.

Cross-tenant mailbox migration is predictable when you know its limits before the first batch. MP-365 prepares both tenants, moves the data Microsoft's tools support, and gives your users a plain guide for the parts that change.

## Microsoft 365 Tenant Coexistence and Cutover
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/tenant-to-tenant-migration/coexistence/

Microsoft 365 tenant coexistence keeps two companies working together on separate tenants until the move is done, with shared people search, calendar visibility, mail routing and a planned domain cutover. MP-365 designs the coexistence layer and runs the cutover for IT leads inside a merger, acquisition or divestiture.

bestFor: IT leads in a deal who need two Microsoft 365 tenants to work together until users and the email domain move.
includes: Coexistence design, directory visibility, calendar and MailTips sharing, mail routing review, Teams collaboration settings, a domain cutover plan and run, and post-cutover user support.
notIncluded: Cybersecurity and identity security services, managed IT or help desk, Microsoft license resale and ERP implementation.
howItStarts: A discovery call about both tenants and their domains, then a coexistence design that lists each sharing need and the Microsoft setting that meets it.

### How do two Microsoft 365 tenants coexist during a merger?
Two tenants coexist by connecting them through cross-tenant settings, one need at a time. People need to find each other, calendars need to show availability, mail needs to reach the right mailbox, and teams need a place to work together. Microsoft provides a separate feature for each, and no single switch covers all four.
Coexistence is temporary by design. It covers the period between the deal signing and the day the last user and the domain move. MP-365 builds it to be removed, so nothing is left over once the cutover is done.

### Microsoft 365 tenant coexistence: what each need requires
Need | Microsoft feature | What it does | Limits to know
People search and app access | Microsoft Entra cross-tenant synchronization | Creates and updates B2B collaboration users and security groups in the other tenant, and supports people search | Not a migration tool; needs Entra ID P1 for each synced user in the source tenant; syncs users and security groups, not devices or contacts
Calendar availability and MailTips | Microsoft 365 cross-tenant access policy | Lets each tenant allow the other to see availability, share calendars and read MailTips | Inbound setting, so both tenants must set it; only for organizations hosted in Microsoft 365
Mail between migrated and unmigrated users | Source mail user that points to the target mailbox | Forwards mail from the source tenant to the migrated mailbox, like hybrid mail flow | Anti-spam and transport rules run in the source tenant first, then the target
Shared Teams channels | Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect | Lets people join shared channels in the other tenant with their own identity | Microsoft has no plan to extend it beyond Teams shared channels
File and site access | Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration | Gives guest-style access to SharePoint sites and Teams in the other tenant | Users sign in with the home identity; existing B2B limits apply

### Pre-close and post-close coexistence rules differ
Before a deal closes, the two companies are separate organizations. Microsoft states that cross-tenant synchronization is intended for use within one organization, and that using it across organizations may add compliance duties, including under GDPR. It points to entitlement management for inviting B2B users across organizations.
After close, both tenants belong to one organization and synchronization becomes a fair choice. MP-365 designs the pre-close layer with guest invitations and sharing settings, then switches to synchronization when your legal team confirms the deal.

### How do users share calendars between tenants?
Users share calendars between tenants through Microsoft 365 cross-tenant access policy, which is an inbound setting. Each tenant creates a partner policy that allows availability only, or availability with subject and location. Both tenants must create matching policies for sharing in both directions. As of October 2026, Microsoft says this is the new standard and replaces organization relationships.

### Setting up calendar sharing
You need the other tenant's ID, Global Administrator rights to enable the Microsoft 365 collaboration trust, and Exchange or Global Administrator rights to add the calendar capability. You can limit sharing to a security group of users. MailTips and full calendar sharing use their own capabilities.

### Why Microsoft is replacing organization relationships
Organization relationships and sharing policies depend on Exchange Web Services, which Microsoft is deprecating in Exchange Online. Microsoft says the new policy is rolling out and may not have reached every tenant, so check the Message Center. Keep old sharing policies in place for hybrid or on-premises partners, because the new policy does not cover them.

### What is a domain cutover in Microsoft 365?
A domain cutover moves an email domain from the source tenant to the target tenant, so users keep their email addresses after the move. A domain can belong to only one tenant, so it must be fully removed from the source before the target can verify it.
Microsoft's rules for removing a domain are strict. The domain cannot be the default domain, and no users, shared mailboxes, resource mailboxes, contacts, Microsoft 365 groups, distribution lists or teams can still use it. No admin account can sign in with it either. Missing one object blocks the removal.

### How MP-365 runs a domain cutover
1. List every use of the domain: Find users, aliases, shared and resource mailboxes, contacts, groups, distribution lists, teams, admin sign-ins and apps that use the domain.
2. Move users to a temporary domain: Change user names and primary addresses to another domain, such as the onmicrosoft.com domain, using PowerShell for large user counts so none are missed.
3. Move groups and teams: Change the primary email addresses of Microsoft 365 groups, Teams-connected groups and distribution lists.
4. Change the default domain: Set another domain as the default in the source tenant, and keep at least one Global Administrator on a different domain.
5. Remove the domain from the source tenant: Remove it in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and fix any remaining reference that blocks the removal.
6. Add and verify it in the target tenant: Verify ownership with a DNS TXT record, then add the domain to the target tenant.
7. Switch user addresses and mail routing: Set each user's sign-in name and primary address to the domain, update the MX record and other mail DNS records, and test mail in both directions.
8. Reconnect devices and apps: Walk users through Outlook, phone and Teams sign-in, and update apps that use the email address as the username.
9. Remove temporary coexistence settings: Delete the cross-tenant sync jobs, policies and endpoints you no longer need.

### What can break at domain cutover
- Outlook profiles. The old primary address is not on the migrated mailbox, so profiles need rebuilding and old autocomplete entries need the x500 addresses.
- Blocked removal. One alias, shared mailbox or team that still uses the domain stops the removal.
- Temporary sign-in names. After removal, accounts revert to the onmicrosoft.com address, so users need to know their sign-in during the gap.
- Mail routing. Mail to the domain fails until MX records point to the target tenant.
- Apps that use the address as a username. Business applications and integrations need the new sign-in name.
- Phones. Mobile mail accounts need to be re-added or updated.

### Coexistence decisions to make before the deal closes
- Surviving tenant. Decide which tenant owns identity, licenses and policy.
- Domain order. List which domains move, in what order, and what happens to each one in the interim.
- Calendar scope. Decide which people or departments share calendars before they migrate.
- Guest or member users. Choose how users from the other company appear in your directory.
- Teams collaboration. Decide whether shared channels are needed, which requires B2B direct connect.
- Clean-up owner. Name who removes temporary trust and sync settings after the cutover.

### Mail flow between tenants during coexistence
After a mailbox moves, the source tenant keeps a mail user that points to the target mailbox. Mail sent to the old address is forwarded to the new one, much as in a hybrid Exchange setup.
Microsoft states that inbound mail passes through anti-spam, anti-malware, transport rules and journaling in the source tenant first, then the target tenant. MP-365 reviews both rule sets so mail is not held or rewritten twice.

### When coexistence is not the right fit
If one tenant will dissolve right after close and few users need to share anything, skip most of the coexistence layer and go straight to cross-tenant mailbox migration. The wider tenant to tenant migration page compares Microsoft's tools.
Coexistence also costs design effort, so scope it to the needs you can name. For how MP-365 prices that effort, see pricing.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do two Microsoft 365 tenants coexist during a merger?
A: They coexist through separate cross-tenant settings: Entra cross-tenant synchronization for people and app access, cross-tenant access policy for calendars and MailTips, source mail users for mail routing, and B2B direct connect for shared Teams channels. Each need has its own feature. MP-365 maps them to your needs.
Q: How do users share calendars between tenants?
A: Both tenants create a Microsoft 365 cross-tenant access policy for the other, since it is an inbound setting. Each choice allows availability only, or availability with subject and location. You can limit it to a security group. Hybrid and on-premises partners still use older sharing policies.
Q: What is a domain cutover?
A: A domain cutover moves an email domain from one Microsoft 365 tenant to another. You move all users, groups and teams off the domain in the source tenant, remove the domain, then verify and add it to the target tenant with a DNS TXT record. Then you update MX records and user addresses.
Q: Can two tenants use the same email domain at once?
A: No. A domain can be verified in only one tenant. Microsoft also states that source and target tenant domains must be unique during cross-tenant mailbox migration. Users therefore have target-tenant addresses during the move, and the domain cutover returns their familiar address at the end.
Q: Is Microsoft Entra cross-tenant synchronization enough to merge tenants?
A: No. Microsoft states it is not a migration tool, because the source tenant is still required for users to sign in, and OneDrive and SharePoint data would still need to move. It creates B2B users for access and people search, which helps during coexistence but does not replace migration.
Q: What licenses does cross-tenant synchronization need?
A: Each user synchronized from the source tenant needs a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in that tenant. Synchronizing groups needs Microsoft Entra ID Governance or the Microsoft Entra Suite. Microsoft says the target tenant needs no license for synchronization, though other features there may. MP-365 does not resell licenses.
Q: Can we use cross-tenant synchronization before the deal closes?
A: Microsoft states that the feature is intended for use within an organization, and that using it across organizations may add compliance duties, including under GDPR. Before close, MP-365 usually designs coexistence with guest invitations and sharing settings, then confirms with your legal team before turning on synchronization.
Q: Why is Microsoft replacing organization relationships for calendar sharing?
A: Organization relationships and sharing policies depend on Exchange Web Services, which Microsoft is deprecating in Exchange Online. Its cross-tenant access policy replaces them between Microsoft 365 organizations. Microsoft says the rollout may not have reached every tenant yet, so check the Message Center for yours.
Q: Can people from two tenants use shared Teams channels?
A: Yes. Teams shared channels depend on Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect, which lets people join channels in the other tenant with their own identity. It can run alongside cross-tenant synchronization. Microsoft has no plan to extend B2B direct connect beyond Teams shared channels.
Q: What happens to email addresses at cutover?
A: Users get their familiar address back when the domain moves to the target tenant. Until then, they use target-tenant addresses. After removal from the source, source accounts revert to onmicrosoft.com addresses. Outlook profiles on migrated mailboxes need rebuilding, and MP-365 provides the instructions for every user.

Microsoft 365 tenant coexistence works when each sharing need has a named owner and an end date. MP-365 designs the temporary layer, runs the domain cutover and removes the scaffolding so your target tenant stays clean.

## Microsoft 365 Data Governance Consulting
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/data-governance/

Data governance consulting from MP-365 sets clear rules for who can see, share and keep information in Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365. The work covers permission models, Microsoft Purview and data quality, so people see what their job needs and nothing more. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner, and this is one of eight service areas on the Services page.

### What data governance consulting means in Microsoft 365
Data governance in Microsoft 365 is the set of decisions and settings that control who owns data, who can open it, how it is labeled and when it is cleaned up. Without those decisions, Teams, SharePoint sites and CRM tables grow on their own, and access spreads further than anyone intended.
MP-365 treats governance as a business control, not a security operation. The team designs the permission model, configures the Microsoft tools that enforce it and fixes the records that undermine it. MP-365 does not provide cybersecurity monitoring, compliance certification or audits.

### Data governance consulting services compared
Service | Best for | Typical outcome | Page
Microsoft Purview and permission models | Companies with overshared SharePoint sites, no file labels or no rules for sharing | Clean SharePoint permissions, sensitivity labels and data loss prevention policies tested before they block anyone | Microsoft Purview & Permission Models
Data quality management | Sales and service teams that no longer trust the numbers in Dynamics 365 | Duplicates merged, entries standardized and rules that keep new records clean | Data Quality Management

### Which data governance service to start with
Start with Microsoft Purview and permission models if the worry is who can see what. Start with data quality management if the worry is that reports and forecasts are wrong. Both problems often exist together, and the order depends on which one costs you more today.
Two upcoming projects change the order. If you plan a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout, fix permissions first, because Copilot only surfaces what a user can already open. If you plan a CRM migration or a new integration, clean the data first, because every duplicate moves with it. For Copilot-specific access reviews, see the AI Data Governance Audit.

### Problems that bring teams to data governance consulting
- Oversharing: Files sit in sites that the whole company can open, and nobody knows how that happened.
- No labels: Contracts, HR files and customer lists look the same as meeting notes, so nothing can be protected differently.
- Access sprawl: Former project members, vendors and guests still have access long after the work ended. The CRM version of this problem is covered by the Dynamics 365 Security Roles & Access Audit.
- Duplicate and stale records: The same customer exists three times in Dynamics 365, and each copy has a different owner.
- Copilot hesitation: Leaders want Microsoft 365 Copilot but cannot say what it would find. The Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness service picks up from there.

### How MP-365 approaches data governance
1. Find out where the data lives: MP-365 reviews SharePoint sites, Teams, OneDrive sharing and the Dynamics 365 tables that matter, and lists who owns each one.
2. Measure the exposure: The team uses Microsoft's own reports, such as SharePoint data access governance reports, to see which sites are shared too widely.
3. Agree the rules with business owners: Department heads decide which data is sensitive and who needs it. MP-365 writes those decisions down in plain language before touching a setting.
4. Design the permission model: MP-365 replaces one-off permissions with groups and a small set of site and role patterns that people can understand.
5. Configure Microsoft Purview: Sensitivity labels, data loss prevention policies and retention settings go live in test mode first, then in enforcement once the results look right.
6. Clean and standardize the data: Duplicate detection rules, merges and entry standards fix Dynamics 365 records and keep them fixed.
7. Hand over with owners and a review rhythm: Your team gets documentation, named owners and a short checklist for the periodic reviews that keep the model from drifting.

### Proof from a data governance engagement
In one MP-365 engagement, Dynamics 365 access was granted by email and nobody could say who held which role. MP-365 introduced an approval process, documented the access levels and set up automatic access reports. Access now follows a written process instead of memory.
The company stays anonymous in this example. See the Clients page for named results across other projects.

### Data governance work that connects to other MP-365 services
Permissions drive the design of intranets and portals. The SharePoint Search & Information Architecture service structures content so that access follows the structure. Teams that inherit another company's tenant after a deal often start governance from scratch, which is where M&A tenant migration and this service meet.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is data governance in Microsoft 365?
A: Data governance in Microsoft 365 is the practice of deciding who owns data, who can access it and how long it is kept, then enforcing those decisions with tools such as SharePoint permissions, sensitivity labels and Microsoft Purview policies. It turns informal habits into written, enforceable rules.
Q: Why do companies need data governance before Copilot?
A: Microsoft 365 Copilot answers from content the asking user can already open. If a site is shared with everyone, Copilot can quote it to anyone. Cleaning permissions and labeling sensitive files before the rollout keeps answers useful and prevents unpleasant surprises on the first day.
Q: How much does data governance consulting cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of sites and tables in scope, how much cleanup is needed and how much your team can help. MP-365 sets scope in a discovery call and gives a written estimate. The Pricing page explains the three engagement models and what drives effort.
Q: Is data governance the same as cybersecurity?
A: No. Data governance decides who should have access and how data is handled. Cybersecurity detects and stops attacks. MP-365 provides the first and does not offer security operations or threat monitoring. Your security team or provider can build on a clean governance foundation.
Q: Does MP-365 make us compliant with HIPAA or similar regulations?
A: No. MP-365 does not certify compliance or promise a regulatory outcome. The team builds permission models, labels and policies that support your own compliance program. Your compliance officer or auditor decides whether those controls meet a specific regulation.
Q: What do you need from us to start?
A: MP-365 needs a named business owner, read access to the tenant and the Dynamics 365 environment, and a few short sessions with department heads who know which data is sensitive. Admin changes are made together with your IT team so nothing happens without approval.
Q: Do we need Microsoft Purview licenses?
A: Some Purview features need higher Microsoft 365 license tiers, so the answer depends on what you want to enforce. MP-365 checks your current plan during the first review and tells you what is already included. Microsoft sets license fees, and they are separate from MP-365's fees.
Q: Can you fix permissions without disrupting our users?
A: Yes, with planning. MP-365 changes permissions in stages, starts with the most exposed sites, tells site owners ahead of time and tests data loss prevention policies in simulation mode before enforcing them. Users see fewer surprises because the rules are explained first.
Q: Should we clean our CRM data or fix permissions first?
A: Fix permissions first if Copilot or an external sharing project is coming. Clean data first if a migration, integration or forecasting rollout is coming. If both are on the list, MP-365 usually starts with whichever one blocks the nearest project. The two services can run in parallel.
Q: What happens after the engagement ends?
A: Your team owns the model. MP-365 hands over documentation, the policy settings, named owners and a review checklist. If you want help with periodic reviews or new projects, you can call MP-365 again on the ad hoc, standard or dedicated engagement model.

Good data governance consulting leaves your team with clear owners, a permission model people understand and policies that run quietly in the background. If you are not sure whether to begin with Purview or with data quality, a short call will settle it.

## Microsoft Purview Implementation and Permissions
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/data-governance/microsoft-purview/

Microsoft Purview implementation from MP-365 puts sensitivity labels, data loss prevention (DLP) policies and clean SharePoint permissions in place, so each file is visible only to the people who should see it. It is built for IT leaders and business owners at mid-size and enterprise companies who need a governed Microsoft 365 tenant, not a security operations program.

bestFor: Companies with overshared SharePoint sites, unlabeled sensitive files or a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout coming up.
includes: SharePoint permission cleanup, a sensitivity label scheme, DLP policies tested in simulation mode, label defaults for sites and libraries, and handover documentation.
notIncluded: Cybersecurity operations, threat monitoring, identity management, compliance certification or audits, and Microsoft license resale.
howItStarts: A discovery call, then a read-only review of your SharePoint sharing reports and current Purview settings.

### What Microsoft Purview is and what it does for you
Microsoft Purview is the set of Microsoft 365 tools that classify, protect and govern data. For most mid-size companies, the useful pieces are sensitivity labels, data loss prevention (DLP), retention settings and the reports that show who can open what.
Microsoft renames and regroups Purview features often. As of November 2026, the admin experience lives in the Microsoft Purview portal, and some features, such as DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot, are still in preview in Microsoft's documentation. MP-365 checks the current names and status before each project and writes the handover in your terms.

### Problems Microsoft Purview implementation solves
- Everyone can open it: Sites and libraries are shared with the whole company or with "Everyone except external users" because that was the quickest setting.
- Nothing is labeled: Customer lists, pricing sheets and HR files look like any other document, so no rule can treat them differently.
- Sharing links keep multiplying: Staff send anyone-with-the-link URLs and nobody can find them later.
- Copilot worries: Leaders ask what Microsoft 365 Copilot would reveal, and nobody can answer with confidence.
- Rules exist only on paper: The information policy says "confidential files stay internal," but no setting enforces it.

### How MP-365 delivers a Microsoft Purview implementation
1. Review the current state: Pull SharePoint data access governance reports, sharing link activity and your existing label and DLP settings, read-only.
2. Rank sites by exposure: List the sites that hold sensitive content and are shared too widely, and agree with business owners which to fix first.
3. Design the permission model: Replace one-off grants with Microsoft 365 groups and a short list of site patterns, with named owners for every site.
4. Design the label scheme: Define a small set of sensitivity labels with names, descriptions and protection settings that employees can understand in one read.
5. Publish labels and defaults: Release labels through label policies, set default labels for libraries and containers, and brief site owners and users.
6. Run DLP in simulation mode: Create policies for the data types you named, watch what they would have blocked and tune them with the business owners.
7. Turn on enforcement in stages: Move policies from simulation to policy tips, then to blocking with override, then to hard blocks only where the business agrees.
8. Hand over and set a review rhythm: Document the model, train site owners and give your IT team a short checklist for site access reviews.

### SharePoint sensitivity labels, explained
SharePoint sensitivity labels classify files and the sites that hold them. A label is stored in the file's metadata, so it stays with the content when someone downloads or moves it. A label can add encryption, add a watermark or header, or simply record how sensitive the file is.
Labels also work on containers. Microsoft's Purview documentation (updated October 2026) states that a label applied to a Teams team, Microsoft 365 group or SharePoint site controls privacy, external sharing and access from unmanaged devices. A container label does not label the files inside it.

### How sensitivity labels work in daily use
People pick a label from the ribbon in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, or the label applies automatically when a policy finds a defined data type. MP-365 sets a default label for libraries so unlabeled files get a baseline, and chooses the option that keeps SharePoint permissions attached to files after download.
Label policy changes can take up to 24 hours to reach users, according to Microsoft's documentation. MP-365 plans communications around that delay.

### How many labels to create
Fewer labels work better. Microsoft's Purview documentation (October 2026) notes that effectiveness drops when users face more than five main labels or more than five sublabels under a main label. MP-365 keeps the starting scheme small and adds sublabels only when a department shows it needs them.
