### Microsoft 365 data loss prevention and SharePoint DLP
Microsoft 365 data loss prevention is a policy engine that watches sharing activity and acts when a rule matches. A policy can show a tip to the user, block sharing with an override and a written reason, or block it outright. Microsoft's documentation lists SharePoint sites, OneDrive, Exchange email, Teams chat and channel messages, and Windows and macOS devices among the locations it covers.
SharePoint DLP scans existing items as well as new ones. Exchange DLP scans new email only, not mail already in a mailbox. That difference matters when you plan your cleanup, and MP-365 builds it into the test plan.

### Office 365 DLP is now Microsoft 365 DLP
Office 365 DLP is the older name for the same capability, which Microsoft now documents as data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview. If your team still searches for Office 365 DLP policies, MP-365 migrates old rules into the Purview portal and retires duplicates.

### Why simulation mode comes first
Microsoft advises deploying DLP policies in simulation mode before using restrictive actions, and MP-365 follows that rule on every project. Simulation shows what a policy would have done without stopping anyone from working. Microsoft notes that policies usually take effect about an hour after you turn them on.

### How to clean up SharePoint permissions
Clean up SharePoint permissions by finding the broadest grants first, then replacing them with groups. MP-365 starts with sites shared with large groups or with "Everyone except external users," removes stale sharing links and fixes places where unique permissions override the site's group structure.
SharePoint Advanced Management gives administrators the tools for this. Microsoft's documentation lists data access governance reports, site access reviews that site owners complete, and restricted content discovery that keeps selected sites out of Copilot results. Prerequisites and license requirements are set by Microsoft, and MP-365 confirms them during the first review.

### What you get from the engagement
- Permission model: A written pattern for sites, groups and owners, with exceptions listed.
- Cleaned permissions: The most exposed sites fixed, with before and after reports.
- Label scheme and policies: Sensitivity labels, label policies and default labels, published and explained.
- DLP policies: Tested rules for the data types you chose, moved from simulation to enforcement in agreed stages.
- Owner guide: A short document for site owners on sharing, labels and access reviews.
- Handover session: A working session with your IT team on reports to check and settings to leave alone.

### Microsoft tools involved
Tool | What MP-365 uses it for | Who works with it day to day
Microsoft Purview portal | Sensitivity labels, label policies, DLP policies and activity reports | Your Microsoft 365 administrators
SharePoint admin center | Data access governance reports, site access reviews and sharing settings | SharePoint administrators and site owners
Microsoft 365 groups | The base for site membership instead of individual grants | Site owners
Microsoft 365 Copilot | Respects labels and the permissions you clean up | All licensed users

### Proof from a SharePoint cleanup
MP-365 moved file shares holding hundreds of thousands of files into organized SharePoint libraries with metadata, version control and workflows for one client. Clear structure makes access rules simple to apply, and that structure-first approach is the basis for this service. See the Clients page for other results.

### When Microsoft Purview implementation is not the right fit
Purview is not the right first step if your tenant has no basic structure yet, such as unmanaged Teams creation and no site owners. MP-365 would begin with a smaller cleanup. It is also not a substitute for a security program. If you need threat detection or compliance audits, work with a security provider, and use this service to give them a cleaner tenant.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Microsoft Purview?
A: Microsoft Purview is Microsoft's set of tools for classifying, protecting and governing data across Microsoft 365. It includes sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, retention settings and reports that show how data is shared. Administrators manage it in the Microsoft Purview portal.
Q: How do sensitivity labels work?
A: A sensitivity label is a tag stored in a file's metadata. It can add encryption, a watermark or a header, and it stays with the file when it moves. Users choose a label in Office apps, or a policy applies one automatically when it finds a defined type of data.
Q: How do you clean up SharePoint permissions?
A: Start with the broadest grants, such as sites shared with the whole company, then replace individual permissions with Microsoft 365 groups and name an owner for each site. Use SharePoint data access governance reports to find the worst cases and ask site owners to confirm who still needs access.
Q: What is the difference between a sensitivity label and a DLP policy?
A: A sensitivity label classifies a file and can protect it with encryption or markings. A DLP policy watches activity, such as sharing or copying, and acts when a rule matches. They work together, because a DLP policy can use a label as a condition, for example blocking external sharing of files marked Confidential.
Q: Can DLP stop people from sharing files in SharePoint?
A: Yes. A DLP policy can show a policy tip, block sharing with a written override reason, or block it entirely. MP-365 first runs policies in simulation mode, then enforces them in stages, so legitimate work is not interrupted by a rule nobody tested.
Q: Is Office 365 DLP the same as Microsoft 365 DLP?
A: Yes. Office 365 is the former name of Microsoft 365, and the same data loss prevention capability is now managed in the Microsoft Purview portal. Older rules can be reviewed and rebuilt there. MP-365 checks old policies for overlap before moving or deleting them.
Q: Will sensitivity labels affect Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: Yes. Microsoft states that Copilot and agents recognize sensitivity labels. When a label applies encryption, Copilot returns content only if the user holds the right to copy it. Labels and clean permissions together reduce what Copilot can surface to the wrong person.
Q: How much does a Microsoft Purview implementation cost?
A: Cost depends on how many sites need cleanup, how many data types need policies and how much time your team can give. MP-365 estimates after a discovery call. The Pricing page lists the engagement models. Microsoft license fees are separate and set by Microsoft.
Q: Do we need Microsoft 365 E5 for Purview?
A: Not always. Some capabilities are included in other Microsoft 365 plans and some need higher tiers or add-ons, so it depends on the features you want. MP-365 reviews your current plan first and suggests a scope that fits what you already own.
Q: Does MP-365 provide cybersecurity or compliance certification?
A: No. MP-365 does permission models, labels and DLP policies as data governance work. It does not run security operations, monitor threats, certify compliance or audit against standards. Your security or compliance team can rely on these controls as part of their own program.

A Microsoft Purview implementation succeeds when labels are few, permissions are simple and policies are tested before they block anyone. MP-365 builds that foundation and leaves your team able to run it.

## CRM Data Cleanup and Data Quality Management
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/data-governance/data-quality-management/

CRM cleanup from MP-365 removes duplicate and incomplete records from Dynamics 365 and puts rules in place so the mess does not come back. It is built for sales and service leaders who no longer trust their pipeline, and for IT teams preparing for a migration, an integration or a Copilot rollout.

bestFor: Teams whose Dynamics 365 reports disagree with reality, or who need clean data before a migration, integration or Copilot rollout.
includes: A data quality assessment, duplicate detection rules, bulk duplicate jobs and merges, entry standards, validation rules and an ownership plan for ongoing care.
notIncluded: ERP data cleansing, purchased contact lists, master data management platforms and outsourced data entry.
howItStarts: A discovery call, then a read-only profile of your most important tables, such as accounts, contacts and leads.

### What CRM data cleanup is and why it matters
CRM data cleanup is the work of finding and fixing duplicate, outdated, inconsistent and incomplete records so that reports, forecasts and automation use correct data. A CRM full of duplicates makes every number suspect: one customer shows up as three accounts, and each has a different owner and a different revenue history.
Cleanup alone does not last. Records get messy again within months if nothing changes how they are entered. That is why this service pairs one-time CRM data cleanup with data quality management, which sets the standards and ownership that keep Dynamics 365 trustworthy after the project.

### Signs your Dynamics 365 data needs attention
- Two answers to one question: Sales and finance report different customer counts or revenue for the same period.
- Duplicate accounts and contacts: Reps find two or three versions of the same company and do not know which to update.
- Typed-in chaos: States, countries, job titles and industries are typed a dozen ways, so filters and views miss records.
- Dead records: Leads from years ago and contacts who have left their companies still sit in active views.
- Stalled projects: A migration, integration or Copilot rollout keeps slipping because nobody trusts what would move.

### How MP-365 runs a CRM cleanup
1. Profile the data: Count records, blanks, likely duplicates and inconsistent values on the tables that drive reporting, without changing anything.
2. Agree what clean means: Sales, service and finance leaders choose the match rules, required fields and standard values, and which record survives a merge.
3. Back up before changing records: Export the affected tables and confirm a restore path, so every change can be traced and reversed if needed.
4. Set up duplicate detection rules: Create and publish rules for accounts, contacts, leads and any other tables that need them.
5. Run bulk detection and merge: Run bulk duplicate detection jobs, review the results with record owners and merge confirmed duplicates in batches.
6. Standardize and fill gaps: Correct inconsistent values in bulk, replace typed-in text with choice fields where it helps and archive records nobody needs.
7. Add guardrails at entry: Add required fields, business rules and validation so new records arrive in the agreed format.
8. Hand over data ownership: Name an owner per table, set a review rhythm and give your team a one-page data standard.

### How Dynamics 365 duplicate detection works
Dynamics 365 duplicate detection compares records against rules you define, and warns users or flags records when a match appears. Microsoft's Power Platform documentation (updated 2026) states that model-driven apps include default duplicate detection rules for accounts and contacts only. Every other table, such as leads or custom tables, needs a rule that you create and publish.
A rule has a base record type, a matching record type and one or more criteria. The base and matching types can differ, which lets you compare the email address of a contact against the email address of a lead.

### How to design duplicate detection rules that work
Build rules on fields with values that should be unique, such as email address. Criteria can use exact match, same first characters or same last characters. Options let a rule skip inactive records, ignore case differences and ignore blank values.
Microsoft documents a limit of five published rules for the same base record type at one time. MP-365 designs a small set of rules per table rather than many overlapping ones, because publishing a rule creates a matchcode for every record in the matching type.

### How to clean up duplicate records in Dynamics 365
Clean up duplicates in Dynamics 365 by running a bulk duplicate detection job, reviewing the matches and merging records. Microsoft provides bulk system jobs for detection and a merge function for accounts, contacts and leads. MP-365 checks merge decisions with record owners first, because a merge keeps one record as the survivor and combines the other's data into it.
Rules that match too loosely merge different customers together. MP-365 tests every rule on a sample before running it across the table.

### Common CRM data problems and the fix
Problem | Typical cause | Fix MP-365 applies
Duplicate accounts and contacts | Manual entry, imports and integrations that create records without checking | Duplicate detection rules, bulk jobs and reviewed merges
Inconsistent states, countries and industries | Typed-in text fields | Choice fields, bulk correction and business rules
Missing key fields | Optional fields nobody fills | Required fields at the right stage, with defaults where possible
Outdated contacts and leads | No review rhythm | Agreed archive rules and a scheduled review by record owners
Records created by connected systems | Integrations that skip the checks users see | Matching logic and logging in the integration itself

### How to keep CRM data clean over time
Keep CRM data clean by preventing bad records at entry and by giving each table an owner. Prevention comes from required fields, choice fields, business rules and published duplicate detection rules. Ownership comes from a named person who reviews a short report on a set schedule.
Integrations need the same discipline. When another system writes into Dynamics 365, it creates records outside the screens your users work in. MP-365 builds matching and error handling into the integration, using service accounts and logging, as described on the Dynamics 365 Integration Services page.

### What you get
- Data quality profile: A before and after view of duplicates, blanks and inconsistent values on the tables in scope.
- Published duplicate detection rules: Rules tested on a sample, documented and ready for your admins.
- Merged and standardized records: Duplicates resolved with a record of what was merged and why.
- Entry guardrails: Required fields, choice fields and business rules that match your data standard.
- Data standard: A short document that says what a good account, contact and lead record looks like.
- Ownership plan: Named table owners and a review checklist.

### Proof: one process and clean numbers
In one MP-365 sales tracking project, scattered spreadsheets and inconsistent records gave way to one sales process in Dynamics 365 with live dashboards for leadership. Dashboards only work when the underlying records are consistent. In another project, MP-365 built reliable integrations between the CRM and ERP and marketing systems with logging and alerts, so errors surfaced instead of quietly creating bad records. See the Clients page for named results.

### When CRM cleanup is not the right fit
CRM cleanup is not the right move when the real problem is process, not data. If reps skip fields because the process does not fit their work, new mess will follow any cleanup. MP-365 raises that early and may recommend a Dynamics 365 configuration fix first. Cleanup is also not enough for organizations that need a full master data management platform across many systems, which is a different project.

### Related services
This service belongs to Data Governance. It pairs with Microsoft Purview & Permission Models when you also need to control who can see records. If access to CRM data is part of the concern, see the Dynamics 365 Security Roles & Access Audit. For connected systems that create records, see Dynamics 365 Integration Services.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you clean up duplicate records in Dynamics 365?
A: Create and publish duplicate detection rules, run a bulk duplicate detection job, check the matches with record owners and merge confirmed duplicates. Dynamics 365 supports merging accounts, contacts and leads. Test each rule on a sample first so it does not merge different customers.
Q: What is CRM data cleanup?
A: CRM data cleanup is the process of finding and correcting duplicate, outdated, inconsistent and incomplete records in your CRM. The goal is reliable reporting, forecasting and automation. A good cleanup also changes how data enters the system, so the same problems do not return.
Q: How do you keep CRM data clean over time?
A: Prevent bad records at entry with required fields, choice fields, business rules and published duplicate detection rules. Then give every important table a named owner who reviews a short report on a schedule. Integrations need matching logic too, because they write records outside the user screens.
Q: Does Dynamics 365 have built-in duplicate detection?
A: Yes. Microsoft states that model-driven apps include default duplicate detection rules for accounts and contacts. Other tables, such as leads or custom tables, need rules you create and publish. Microsoft limits you to five published rules per base record type at one time.
Q: Can a cleanup delete records by mistake?
A: It can if nobody plans for it, which is why MP-365 exports affected tables first, tests rules on a sample, checks merges with record owners and keeps a log of what changed. Merges and deletions happen in batches, so a problem is caught early and can be reversed.
Q: How do we know which duplicate record to keep?
A: Agree a survivor rule before merging, such as the record with the most recent activity or the one linked to open opportunities. Business owners decide the rule, and MP-365 applies it consistently. Edge cases, such as parent and child accounts, are handled by hand.
Q: Should we clean data before migrating to Dynamics 365?
A: Yes. Every duplicate and blank field you carry over becomes a Dynamics 365 problem. Cleaning first is usually cheaper than cleaning after go-live, when users already work in the system. MP-365 can profile the source data before the migration plan is final.
Q: Does data quality affect Microsoft 365 Copilot?
A: Yes. Copilot answers questions from the records in your systems, so duplicates, outdated contacts and missing fields lead to weaker answers. Clean, consistent records make summaries and forecasts easier to trust. Cleanup before a Copilot rollout is a sensible step.
Q: How much does CRM cleanup cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of tables, the volume of records, how many rules are needed and how much your team can review. MP-365 scopes after a discovery call and gives a written estimate. The Pricing page explains what drives effort.
Q: Do you clean ERP or other non-CRM data?
A: No. MP-365's data quality work focuses on Dynamics 365. Where an ERP system such as Business Central feeds the CRM, MP-365 looks at how records are matched and passed through the integration, but it does not cleanse the ERP system itself.

CRM cleanup is worth doing once and then protecting. MP-365 fixes the records you have, sets the rules for the records you will create and leaves your team with a data standard to follow.

## Azure Application Modernization Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/application-modernization/

Azure application modernization moves older on-premises business applications to Microsoft Azure and gives their releases a safer, automated path to production. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that does this work for mid-size and enterprise companies whose important systems are tied to Windows servers, SQL Server and the Microsoft stack. Azure is the destination, and your team keeps running it afterward.

### What Azure application modernization includes
Azure application modernization means choosing, for each older application, the lightest change that makes it safe, supportable and ready for the cloud, then moving it to Azure. For some applications that means moving the servers as they are. For others it means moving the database to a managed Azure service, changing code, or replacing the application with a Power Platform app.
MP-365 groups this work into two services. One handles the migration itself. The other builds the release pipelines that stop changes from breaking production. MP-365 does not manage Azure infrastructure after cutover, does not provide managed services and does not build custom software products.

### Application modernization services compared
Service | Best for | Typical outcome | Page
Legacy application migration | Aging on-premises applications on old servers or old SQL Server versions | Applications running on supported Azure services, with a tested cutover and a retirement plan for the old servers | Legacy Application Migration
DevOps and release automation | Teams that break Dynamics 365 or Power Platform with every release | Automated deployments through development, test and production, with testing and release notes | DevOps & Release Automation

### Which application modernization service to start with
Start with legacy application migration if a server, database or operating system is reaching the end of support. Start with DevOps and release automation if your applications are already modern but releases are slow, manual or risky. Many teams need both, and the order follows the nearest deadline.
Deadlines are real. According to Microsoft's lifecycle pages, SQL Server 2016 reached the end of extended support on July 14, 2026, and Windows Server 2016 reaches it on January 12, 2027. Microsoft also ended support for SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 on July 14, 2026. Applications that depend on these products need a plan.

### Migration strategies for legacy applications
Strategy | What changes | Best used when
Rehost | Servers move to Azure with minimal change | The application works well and needs a fast exit from old hardware
Replatform | The application moves to managed Azure services with small code changes | The application is healthy but the database or web server should be managed by Microsoft
Refactor | Code is restructured for maintainability without changing behavior | Technical debt blocks updates, testing or automation
Rearchitect | The design changes to use cloud capabilities | The application cannot scale or integrate in its current form
Replace | A packaged product or a Power Platform app takes over | The application mostly stores records and routes approvals

### How to choose a path for each application
Choose the lightest strategy that solves the real problem. Microsoft's Cloud Adoption Framework notes that a rehost changes where a workload runs but does not improve what it can do. If the application is stable and supported, rehosting is a good first step. If it blocks the business, change it.
MP-365 scores each application on business value, technical health and dependencies, then proposes a path and an order. Simple, low-risk applications go first so your team learns the process before the critical systems move.

### How MP-365 approaches Azure application modernization
1. List the applications and owners: Build an inventory with business owner, users, hosting, database, integrations and support status for each application.
2. Assess technical fit: Use Azure Migrate and the Azure Migrate application and code assessment tools for .NET and Java to find blockers and dependencies.
3. Choose a path and an order: Assign rehost, replatform, refactor, rearchitect or replace to each application, and group them into waves.
4. Build a landing target: Agree the Azure subscription, networking and access setup with your IT team, who own it from then on.
5. Migrate and test in non-production first: Move development and test copies, run the full test cycle and rehearse the cutover and rollback.
6. Cut over and verify: Switch users to the Azure version in an agreed window, check data and integrations, and keep the old system ready for rollback.
7. Automate releases: Set up pipelines so future changes move through test and into production the same way every time.
8. Retire the old servers and hand over: Document the new setup, switch off the old environment and train your team to run it.

### Proof from release automation at OTIS Elevator
At OTIS Elevator, MP-365 provided platform and operations leadership for Dynamics, which made deployments faster and smoother. A deployment that took 13 hours now takes 4, and manual errors fell to near zero. The DevOps & Release Automation page explains the approach. More results are on the Clients page.

### Related work across MP-365 services
SharePoint farms that run on Server 2016 or 2019 are covered by SharePoint Migration, and the full list of service areas is on the Services page.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is Azure application modernization?
A: Azure application modernization is the process of moving an existing business application to Azure and updating it as much as needed to run well there. Depending on the application, that can mean moving servers as they are, switching to managed services, restructuring code or replacing the application.
Q: How long does application modernization take?
A: It depends on the number of applications, their dependencies, the amount of data and how fast your team can test and approve. MP-365 sets a plan after the assessment and groups applications into waves. Simple applications move first, and critical ones follow once the process is proven.
Q: How much does application modernization cost?
A: Cost depends on the strategy for each application, the number of integrations, data volume and your team's available time. MP-365 gives a written estimate after the assessment. Azure usage is billed by Microsoft and is separate from MP-365's fees. The Pricing page explains how projects are priced.
Q: What is the difference between rehost and replatform?
A: Rehost moves servers to Azure with minimal change, like for like. Replatform moves the application onto managed services, such as a managed database or web hosting service, with small code changes. Replatforming removes more maintenance work, while rehosting is usually faster.
Q: Does MP-365 manage our Azure environment after migration?
A: No. MP-365 does not provide managed services or Azure infrastructure management. The team sets up the migration, documents the new environment and trains your IT staff. After handover, your team or your hosting provider runs Azure day to day.
Q: Is MP-365 a custom software development company?
A: No. MP-365 moves and modernizes existing applications and automates their releases. It does not build new software products for sale or act as a development agency. Where an old application fits low-code, MP-365 may replace it with Power Apps or Power Automate.
Q: Which applications are good candidates for modernization?
A: Good candidates run on aging servers or unsupported database versions, depend on one person who knows how they work, or block integration with Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365. Applications that still work and are supported may only need a lighter move or no change.
Q: What risks come with legacy application migration?
A: The main risks are hidden dependencies, data differences, performance changes and cutover problems. MP-365 reduces them by mapping dependencies first, migrating test environments before production and rehearsing rollback. The risks of staying put grow as vendors end support.
Q: How does DevOps fit into application modernization?
A: DevOps makes modernized applications easier to change safely. Pipelines build, test and deploy each change the same way, and release notes record what shipped. MP-365 focuses on Dynamics 365 and Power Platform releases, and sets up pipelines for migrated applications where they apply.
Q: Do you work with Microsoft only?
A: Yes, with a Microsoft focus. MP-365 works on applications that run on or connect to Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, SQL Server, .NET and Azure. Applications on other stacks are outside the service and may be better served by a provider that specializes in them.

Azure application modernization works best when each application gets the lightest change that solves its real problem. MP-365 plans the order, moves the applications and hands your team a running, documented environment.

## Legacy Application Migration Services
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/application-modernization/legacy-migration/

MP-365 is a legacy software modernization company for Microsoft-based applications: it re-engineers older on-premises software so it runs on supported Azure services. The work is for IT and operations leaders who depend on systems that run on aging servers, old SQL Server versions or one person's memory. Your team keeps ownership of the result.

bestFor: Business applications on aging Windows servers, old SQL Server versions or unsupported platforms that need to move to Azure.
includes: Application inventory and assessment, a path for each application, database and data migration, test migrations, a rehearsed cutover and rollback plan, and handover documentation.
notIncluded: Ongoing Azure hosting or management, managed services, building new software products, non-Microsoft technology stacks, and ERP implementation.
howItStarts: A discovery call, then a short inventory of the applications, their owners, servers, databases and connections.

### What a legacy software modernization company actually does
A legacy software modernization company assesses old applications, picks the right change for each one and moves it to a supported platform without losing data or stopping the business. MP-365 does this for Microsoft-based applications and moves them to Azure.
The key skill is restraint. Not every application needs a rewrite. Some need a move, some need a new database, and some should be replaced by a Power Apps app that costs less to maintain. This page is part of Application Modernization & DevOps.

### Problems that lead to legacy system migration
- End of support: The operating system, database or web server no longer gets updates from Microsoft. SQL Server 2016, for example, left extended support on July 14, 2026, according to Microsoft's lifecycle page.
- Hardware risk: The application runs on a server nobody wants to restart.
- Key-person risk: One employee or contractor knows how it works, and that person is leaving.
- Integration blockers: The application cannot connect to Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365 or Power BI without fragile workarounds.
- Slow, risky changes: Every update is a manual copy that someone hopes works.

### Legacy items and where they usually go in Azure
What you have | Common Azure destination | Typical approach
Windows servers running a stable internal app | Azure virtual machines | Rehost, then plan later improvements
.NET web application on IIS | Azure App Service | Replatform after a code assessment
SQL Server database | Azure SQL or SQL Server on Azure virtual machines | Move with a tested data migration and a rollback plan
Access databases, spreadsheets and old forms | Power Apps with Dataverse or SharePoint | Replace with a low-code app
Old SharePoint farm | SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Staged migration, covered under the SharePoint services

### How MP-365 migrates a legacy application to Azure
1. Take inventory: Record the owner, users, servers, database, scheduled jobs and every connection to other systems.
2. Assess the code and configuration: Run Azure Migrate for servers and its application and code assessment tools for .NET and Java to find blockers before any move.
3. Pick a path per application: Choose rehost, replatform, refactor or replace, and say in writing why, so the decision can be challenged.
4. Map dependencies and group them: Group applications that share databases, services or sign-in so they move together.
5. Build the target and migrate a test copy: Set up the Azure target with your IT team, move a development copy and run the full test cycle with business users.
6. Migrate the data and rehearse: Choose a data transfer path, rehearse the cutover and write the rollback steps before the real date.
7. Cut over and verify: Switch users in the agreed window, check data counts and integrations, and keep the old system on hold.
8. Retire the old system and hand over: Switch off the old servers once the business confirms, update documents and train your team.

### How do you migrate a legacy application to Azure?
Migrate a legacy application by assessing it, choosing a strategy, moving a test copy, rehearsing cutover and only then moving production. Microsoft's Cloud Adoption Framework recommends migrating non-production environments before production and defining rollback criteria before the move. MP-365 follows that order.
Data moves by the path that fits its size and sensitivity. The Cloud Adoption Framework lists ExpressRoute, VPN, Azure Data Box for large volumes and the public internet, and MP-365 helps your IT team choose.

### Rebuild, rehost or replace a legacy app
Option | Choose it when | Watch out for
Rehost | The app works, the deadline is close and the code is stable | Problems move with the app, because nothing is improved
Replatform or refactor | The app is valuable but its database, web server or code needs updating | Hidden dependencies and old libraries
Rebuild | The design is the problem and the business needs new behavior | Cost and scope growth, and MP-365 does not run large product builds
Replace | The app handles forms, records or approvals that Power Apps or a packaged product can cover | Staff habits and data mapping

### What are the risks of legacy system migration?
The main risks of legacy system migration are hidden dependencies, data loss or corruption, performance surprises and a failed cutover. Dependencies hide in scheduled jobs, shared folders, service accounts and reports that nobody remembers. MP-365 maps them before choosing a path.
Data risk is handled with counts, sample checks and a rollback plan. Cutover risk is handled by rehearsal. Microsoft's guidance separates migrations with downtime from near-zero downtime migrations, and a critical application may need continuous replication for the second kind. MP-365 asks the business what outage it can accept before choosing.

### What you get
- Application inventory: A single list of applications, owners, servers, databases and connections.
- Assessment report: Blockers, dependencies and a recommended path for each application.
- Migration plan: Waves, cutover windows, data transfer path and rollback criteria.
- Migrated applications: Running on Azure services your IT team has approved.
- Release pipeline: A repeatable deployment path where it applies, built with the DevOps & Release Automation service.
- Handover pack: Architecture notes, runbooks and a training session.

### Microsoft products involved
Product | Role in the project
Azure Migrate | Server discovery, assessment and migration
Azure Migrate application and code assessment | Code and configuration analysis for .NET and Java applications
Azure App Service | Hosting for replatformed web applications
Azure SQL and SQL Server | Database targets and sources
Power Apps and Dataverse | Replacement for form and workflow applications
Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions | Automated deployment for migrated applications

MP-365 has moved SharePoint from 2007, 2010, 2013 and 2016 to Microsoft 365 in stages for financial and manufacturing clients, and has moved Dynamics 365 from on-premises to the cloud with zero data loss as the goal. The staged method, where each stage is tested before the next begins, is the same one used for applications. See the Clients page for named results.

### When legacy migration is not the right fit
Legacy migration is not the right fit when the application should be retired, when it runs on a non-Microsoft stack, or when the real need is a new product. MP-365 will say so in the assessment. Retiring an unused application is cheaper than moving it. For ongoing hosting and support, work with a managed services provider, since MP-365 does not offer those services.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you migrate a legacy application to Azure?
A: Take inventory, assess code and dependencies, choose a path per application, migrate a test copy, rehearse the cutover and migrate production with a rollback plan ready. Azure Migrate and its application and code assessment tools help with the assessment. Non-production environments always move before production.
Q: Should we rebuild, rehost or replace a legacy app?
A: Rehost if the app works and the deadline is close. Replatform or refactor if the app is valuable but its database or code needs updating. Rebuild only if the design itself is the problem. Replace with Power Apps or a packaged product when the app mainly handles forms, records and approvals.
Q: What are the risks of legacy system migration?
A: The main risks are hidden dependencies, data loss, performance changes and a failed cutover. MP-365 reduces them by mapping dependencies first, checking data with counts and samples, testing in non-production and rehearsing rollback. Waiting also carries risk when vendors end support.
Q: What is cloud modernization?
A: Cloud modernization is the practice of updating applications so they run well on cloud platforms such as Azure. It ranges from moving servers unchanged to redesigning an application. Microsoft treats replatforming, refactoring and rearchitecting as steps along a range of complexity and value.
Q: How long does a legacy migration take?
A: It depends on the number of applications, dependencies, data volume and how quickly your team can test and approve. MP-365 gives a plan after the assessment and groups applications into waves. We do not quote a duration before knowing what is in scope.
Q: How much does legacy application migration cost?
A: Cost depends on the path chosen for each application, the amount of data, the number of integrations and how much your team can test. MP-365 provides a written estimate after the assessment. Azure usage is billed separately by Microsoft. See the Pricing page for the engagement models.
Q: Will we have downtime during the move?
A: Possibly, and you decide how much. Microsoft separates migrations with a planned outage from near-zero downtime migrations that use continuous replication. A noncritical app may accept a maintenance window, while a customer-facing app may need the second method. MP-365 agrees the window with the business.
Q: Does MP-365 rewrite applications from scratch?
A: Rarely, and only as a considered choice. MP-365 prefers the lightest change that solves the problem, such as a move, a database upgrade or a low-code replacement. Large custom product builds are outside the service, and MP-365 will say so in the assessment.
Q: Do you manage the application on Azure afterward?
A: No. MP-365 hands over documentation, runbooks and training, and your team or provider runs the environment. MP-365 does not offer managed services or Azure infrastructure management. You can call MP-365 again for changes or the next wave of applications.
Q: Can you move our old Access databases and forms?
A: Often yes, and usually by replacing them rather than moving them. Access databases, spreadsheets and old forms that track records and approvals fit Power Apps with Dataverse or SharePoint. MP-365 reviews each one first, because some are better retired than rebuilt.

A good legacy software modernization company does not push one answer. MP-365 assesses each application, chooses the lightest change that works and moves it to Azure with a tested rollback, then hands the result to your team.

## Dynamics 365 DevOps and Release Automation
URL: https://mp-365.com/services/application-modernization/devops-release-automation/

Power Platform pipelines move your Dynamics 365 and Power Platform changes from development through test to production in a controlled, repeatable way. MP-365 sets them up, adds testing and release notes around them, and connects Azure DevOps or GitHub where the work needs more than Microsoft's built-in tool. The goal is simple: releases that no longer break the CRM.

bestFor: Dynamics 365 and Power Platform teams that deploy by hand, break production with releases or cannot say what changed.
includes: Environment strategy, solution structure, Power Platform pipelines or Azure DevOps and GitHub pipelines, a QA cycle, release notes and a trackable backlog.
notIncluded: Azure infrastructure management, managed services, help desk, custom software development and ERP implementation.
howItStarts: A discovery call, then a review of your environments, solutions and how changes reach production today.

### What are Power Platform pipelines?
Power Platform pipelines are Microsoft's built-in way to deploy solutions between environments. Microsoft's documentation (updated September 2026) describes them as application lifecycle management (ALM) automation with continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) capabilities built into the service. Makers start a deployment from their development environment in a few clicks, and admins control the stages and approvals.
A pipeline deploys solutions, plus target settings such as connections, connection references and environment variables. It does not deploy the data in Dataverse tables. The same pipeline handles Power Apps, Power Automate flows and Dynamics 365 customizations that sit inside a solution.

### Problems release automation solves
- Hand-built releases: Someone exports a solution, imports it elsewhere and fixes connections by hand, and each release goes slightly differently.
- Fixes that break something else: A change that worked in development fails in production because the environments differ.
- Nobody knows what changed: Users report new behavior, and there are no release notes to check.
- Weekend deployments: Releases need a long, careful window because errors are common.
- Skipped testing: Nobody has time to retest, so users find the bugs.

### How MP-365 sets up Dynamics 365 DevOps
1. Map how changes reach production today: List environments, solutions, who changes what, and where releases fail or slow down.
2. Design the environments: Agree on development, test and production environments, plus a pipelines host, and name an owner for each.
3. Structure the solutions: Split customizations into solutions with clear ownership, environment variables and connection references instead of hardcoded values.
4. Build the deployment pipeline: Configure Power Platform pipelines, or Azure DevOps or GitHub pipelines where you need source control and gated builds.
5. Add automated checks: Run solution checks on every build and add regression tests for the processes that matter most.
6. Set the QA cycle: Define who tests in the test environment, what passes a release and who approves production.
7. Produce release notes and a backlog: Generate a short note for every release and keep a single backlog that links work to releases.
8. Train your team and hand over: Walk makers and admins through a live release and give them a one-page runbook.

### How to move Dynamics 365 changes from development to production
Move Dynamics 365 changes by packaging them in a solution, exporting a managed version and importing it into test, then into production, in that order. Microsoft recommends deploying managed solutions to every non-development environment. Pipelines do this for you: the same exported file passes through each stage in sequence, so nobody can skip QA by pushing a different version.
Environment settings differ between stages. Connection references and environment variables hold those differences, so the solution itself does not change between test and production.

### Power Platform pipelines requirements and limits
Topic | What Microsoft's documentation says | What it means for you
Environments | The pipelines host should be a production environment. Development and QA can be developer environments | Plan at least a host, a development, a test and a production environment
Managed Environments | All other environments used in pipelines, including the target, must be managed environments | Target environments need premium-use licenses. Microsoft sets license fees
Enforcement from October 2026 | Admins are notified when pipelines deploy to unmanaged targets and have 30 days to approve enabling managed environments before deployments are blocked | Convert targets early and avoid a blocked release
Scope | One solution per deployment, one development environment per solution | Large teams may need Azure DevOps or GitHub for parallel work
Tenants | Pipelines cannot deploy to a different tenant | Cross-tenant moves need Azure DevOps or GitHub
Rollback | Past solution versions can be redeployed if the setting is enabled | MP-365 turns it on and tests it

### Power Platform pipelines or Azure DevOps and GitHub
Need | Use Power Platform pipelines | Add Azure DevOps or GitHub
Simple promotion from development to production | Yes, with approvals | Not required
Source control and code review for solution files | Only through pipeline extensions | Yes
Several developers on one solution | Not supported with one development environment | Yes, with branches and merges
Deployment to another tenant | Not supported | Yes
Custom steps such as notifications or extra tests | Through pipeline extensions and Power Automate | Yes, in build and release stages

### What Dynamics 365 release management involves
Dynamics 365 release management is the discipline of deciding what ships, testing it and telling users what changed. It sits on top of the pipeline. The pipeline moves files, and release management makes sure the right files move at the right time.

### Testing before every release
Testing happens in the test environment with a copy of real processes, not only in development. MP-365 uses solution checks for quality rules and builds regression tests for the paths that would hurt most if they broke, such as lead conversion, quote approval and case routing.

### Release notes and the backlog
Release notes tell users what changed and what to try. Each note lists the items shipped, who requested them and how to reach support. A single backlog links requests to releases, so "when did that change?" has an answer.

### What you get
- Environment plan: A diagram and owner list for every environment and the pipelines host.
- Solution structure: Solutions, environment variables and connection references organized for clean deployment.
- Working pipelines: Power Platform pipelines, plus Azure DevOps or GitHub pipelines where needed.
- QA cycle: A written test and approval routine with named testers.
- Release notes template: A short format your team can fill in each time.
- Runbook and training: A one-page guide and a live walkthrough for makers and admins.

### Proof from OTIS Elevator and CRM deployments
At OTIS Elevator, MP-365 gave platform and operations leadership for Dynamics, and deployments fell from 13 hours to 4, with manual errors reduced to near zero. In another engagement, MP-365 set up automatic deployment, a reliable QA cycle, release notes and a trackable backlog for a CRM. Both follow the pattern on this page. The Clients page has more results.

### When this service is not the right fit
A full DevOps setup is not worth it for a small tenant with one maker and a handful of simple apps. A manual process with a checklist may be enough, and MP-365 will say so. Teams that want software engineering for non-Microsoft products should look elsewhere, since MP-365 focuses on Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

### Related services
This service belongs to Application Modernization & DevOps. Moving older applications to Azure is covered by Legacy Application Migration, and pipelines can then carry the migrated apps. Pipeline extensions can use Power Automate. For roles that control who can deploy, see the Dynamics 365 Security Roles & Access Audit.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What are Power Platform pipelines?
A: Power Platform pipelines are a Microsoft feature that deploys solutions from a development environment through test to production with admin-defined stages and approvals. They add ALM and CI/CD capabilities inside the platform, so makers deploy in a few clicks instead of exporting and importing files by hand.
Q: How do you move Dynamics 365 changes from development to production?
A: Put the changes in a solution, export it as managed and import it to test, then production, in sequence. Pipelines automate those steps and ensure the same file passes every stage. Environment variables and connection references handle the differences between environments.
Q: What does Dynamics 365 release management involve?
A: It covers deciding what ships, testing it in a non-production environment, getting approval, deploying and telling users what changed. The pipeline moves the solution. Release management adds the QA cycle, release notes and a backlog that shows when each change was released.
Q: What is ALM in Dynamics 365?
A: ALM, or application lifecycle management, is the set of practices that govern how a system is built, tested, released and maintained. In Dynamics 365 it means solutions, separate environments, version control, testing and controlled deployments, instead of editing production directly.
Q: Do Power Platform pipelines deploy data?
A: No. Pipelines deploy solutions and target settings such as connections, connection references and environment variables. Microsoft states that solutions do not contain data stored in Dataverse tables. Data moves through separate import, integration or migration tools.
Q: Do we need Managed Environments for pipelines?
A: Yes for most environments. Microsoft states that environments used in pipelines, other than the host and developer environments, must be managed environments with premium-use licenses. Starting October 2026, deployments to unmanaged targets are blocked after a notice period. Microsoft sets those license fees.
Q: Should we use pipelines or Azure DevOps?
A: Use Power Platform pipelines for straightforward promotion with approvals. Add Azure DevOps or GitHub when you need source control, several developers on one solution, cross-tenant deployment or custom build steps. Microsoft itself suggests extending pipelines with other CI/CD tools when needed.
Q: Can we roll back a bad release?
A: Yes, if the setting that redeploys past solution versions is enabled in the pipelines host. Microsoft's documentation describes redeploying earlier versions from the run history. MP-365 enables it, tests a rollback during setup and writes the steps into the runbook.
Q: How much does release automation cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of environments and solutions, whether you need Azure DevOps or GitHub, and how much testing you want automated. MP-365 estimates after a discovery call. The Pricing page explains the engagement models. Microsoft licenses are separate.
Q: Does this replace our developers or admins?
A: No. Your makers and admins keep making changes, and the pipeline gives them a safe way to ship. MP-365 builds the process, trains your team and steps back. The pipeline is easier to maintain than a collection of manual steps.

Power Platform pipelines will not fix a team's habits on their own, but they give you a release path that is the same every time, with tests and notes around it. MP-365 builds that path and teaches your team to use it.

## SharePoint Intranet: Build on Microsoft 365 or Buy
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/sharepoint-intranet/

A SharePoint intranet gives every employee one trusted place for news, policies, people and tools, built on the Microsoft 365 licenses you may already own. This guide explains how it works, how it compares with buying intranet software, and what MP-365 builds when you want help.

### What a SharePoint intranet is and how it works
A SharePoint intranet is a company portal made from SharePoint Online sites. A communication site holds the home page, news and policies. Team sites hold the working files of departments and projects. Hub sites tie related sites together with shared navigation, a common look and combined search.
Staff sign in with their work account and open the intranet in a browser or inside Microsoft Teams. Page owners edit pages in the browser, with no code. Because SharePoint ships with ready-made site and page templates, most of the work is deciding structure, ownership and content, not programming.

### Microsoft 365 intranet, SharePoint intranet and Teams intranet
Term | What it means in practice
SharePoint intranet | The sites, pages, news and document libraries in SharePoint Online. This is where company content is published and found.
Microsoft 365 intranet | The SharePoint intranet plus the services around it: Microsoft Entra sign-in, Microsoft Search, Teams, Power Automate and Power Apps.
Microsoft Teams intranet | The intranet opened as a tab or app inside Teams, so staff reach news and policies where they already chat and meet.

### The day-to-day problem: nobody trusts where things live
Most companies do not lack content. They lack one agreed place for it. The handbook sits in email, on a shared drive and on an old site, each with a different date. Announcements go out by email and vanish. Staff in plants, branches and job sites cannot reach documents without a VPN or a call to a colleague.
Search makes it worse. Old versions, duplicates and files with no titles bury the page someone needs, so people ask a coworker instead. Every question answered that way is time taken from someone else.

### Who feels the problem
- HR and internal communications: you send the same policy reminder again because nobody can find the last one.
- Operations and plant managers: your teams work from printed or outdated procedures.
- IT leaders: you maintain an old SharePoint Server site or a portal that nobody owns.
- New hires: you spend the first days asking where things are.
- Executives: your announcements reach only the people who read email.

### What a weak intranet costs the business
Symptom | Business impact
Several copies of the same policy | Staff follow an outdated rule, and managers spend time correcting it.
News sent only by email | Frontline and field teams miss changes that affect their work.
Pages with no named owner | Content goes stale and updates queue up behind IT.
Search returns noise | People interrupt colleagues instead of finding answers themselves.
VPN needed for basic documents | Remote and field staff lose time, or work around the system.

### What features a modern intranet should have
- A clear home page: news, quick links to the top tasks and a search box, with the most used items one click away.
- Structure by audience and function: hubs for areas such as HR, IT and operations, with consistent navigation.
- Search that works: titles, metadata and scoped results so the right page rises to the top.
- Named owners and review dates: every page has a person responsible for it.
- Mobile and Teams access: staff reach content from a phone or from inside Teams.
- Targeted news: the right announcement reaches the right audience, such as one site or one region.
- Simple permissions: broad read access for company content, tighter access for sensitive sites.

### Build a SharePoint intranet or buy intranet software
Question | Build on Microsoft 365 | Buy intranet software
License cost | SharePoint is part of most Microsoft 365 business and enterprise plans, so there is no second platform license. | A separate subscription on top of Microsoft 365, usually priced by user.
Time to a working site | Depends on design and content work. Templates speed up the page layouts. | Faster to a polished start, because many features come packaged.
Built-in extras | Basics are included. Analytics, surveys or recognition may need extra setup or add-ons. | Often bundled, with vendor support.
Control and fit | High. You shape structure, permissions and automation to your company. | Limited to what the vendor offers and how it connects to Microsoft 365.
Ownership after launch | Your page owners and administrators run it with Microsoft's own tools. | Your team plus the vendor's admin console and support.
Data and security | Content stays in your Microsoft 365 tenant under your existing permissions. | Content or identities may sync to another vendor's platform.

### Our verdict on building versus buying
Build on Microsoft 365 if you already license it, you have people who can own content, and you want the intranet to share permissions and search with the rest of your tenant. This is the better fit for most mid-size companies that run on Microsoft.
Buy software if nobody will own the site, you want analytics and engagement tools out of the box, and you accept paying for a second platform. A packaged product can be the right call. It is worth choosing on purpose rather than by default.

### How MP-365 builds your SharePoint intranet
1. Interview each audience: Talk with office staff, field teams and managers, and write down the ten tasks they most need to finish on the intranet.
2. Audit what exists today: List the old site pages, shared drives and Teams content, and mark each item to keep, rewrite, move or retire.
3. Design the site map and hubs: Lay out communication sites, team sites and hubs, with one owner named for each. Plan navigation around tasks, not the org chart.
4. Set permissions and sign-in rules: Create a small set of permission groups and decide which sites stay open to everyone and which are restricted.
5. Build the home page and one department site: Deliver a working first slice you can click, so your team reacts to something real before the rest is built.
6. Test with real staff: Ask a mixed group to complete their top tasks, then adjust labels, navigation and layout where they struggle.
7. Migrate content and launch in waves: Move approved content, retire old pages and open departments one group at a time.
8. Train owners and document the rules: Teach page owners to publish and review, and hand your administrators a short governance guide.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
Site map with hubs and named owners | Staff and owners know where content lives and who keeps it current.
Home page, navigation and news setup | Employees land on one page that shows what matters today.
Page and news templates | Owners publish consistent pages without waiting for IT.
Permission model and documentation | Access is simple to explain and easy to audit.
Search tuning with titles and metadata | People find policies and forms without asking a colleague.
Approvals and review reminders in Power Automate | Policies get reviewed on schedule, with no manual chasing.
Owner training and governance guide | Your team runs the intranet after launch.

### What it takes: scope, effort and cost
Effort depends on the number of audiences and sites, the amount of content to move, the systems you want linked and how quickly owners review pages. MP-365 scopes this on a discovery call and does not guess from a page of questions.
SharePoint license fees are set by Microsoft and are separate from consulting. The pricing page explains how MP-365 engagements work.

### Proof: a modern intranet for a manufacturer
A manufacturing company needed a modern intranet to replace an older setup. MP-365 delivered an information architecture that fits how the company works, a simpler security model and faster content updates. The client name is withheld.
Read more project summaries on the clients page, or see how we serve manufacturing companies.

### When this is not the right fit
A custom SharePoint intranet is not for companies that want a packaged product with analytics, a vendor help desk and little setup. It is also not for teams that need a public marketing website or heavy custom software, which MP-365 does not build. If nobody can own content after launch, fix that first or choose software with managed support.

### Related services and next steps
If you want a team to design and deliver the build, see SharePoint intranet development. If search is the weak spot, SharePoint search and information architecture fixes the base. For other business outcomes, browse all Microsoft solutions for mid-size companies.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is a SharePoint intranet?
A: A SharePoint intranet is a private company portal built on SharePoint Online. It brings news, policies, department pages and tools together on sites that share navigation and search. Employees sign in with their work account and use it in a browser or in Teams. Page owners update content without writing code.
Q: Should you build an intranet on Microsoft 365 or buy software?
A: Build on Microsoft 365 if you already license it and have people to own content. You avoid a second platform and keep content under your existing permissions. Buy software if you want built-in analytics and vendor support with little setup. Compare the cost of the extra subscription against the extra control.
Q: What features should a modern intranet have?
A: A modern intranet needs a clear home page, news that reaches the right audience, search that returns the right page, simple navigation by task, and a named owner for every page. It should also work on phones and inside Teams. Fancy extras matter less than these basics.
Q: What is the difference between a SharePoint intranet and a Microsoft 365 intranet?
A: The SharePoint intranet is the set of sites and pages. A Microsoft 365 intranet is that plus the services around it: Entra sign-in, Microsoft Search, Teams and Power Automate. Most companies mean the same thing by both terms, but the second includes how people reach and use the content.
Q: Can Microsoft Teams act as an intranet?
A: Not on its own. Teams is built for chat, meetings and team collaboration, while an intranet publishes content to the whole company. The usual setup is a SharePoint intranet shown inside Teams as an app, so staff read news and policies where they already work and chat there too.
Q: Are there SharePoint intranet templates we can start from?
A: Yes. SharePoint includes site and page templates you can adapt, and MP-365 builds reusable page and news templates for your owners. Templates save layout work, but they do not decide your structure, permissions or content. Plan those first, then apply the template that fits.
Q: Do employees need a VPN to reach a SharePoint intranet?
A: No. SharePoint Online runs in Microsoft 365, so staff reach it from any device by signing in with their work account. Your organization can still add rules, such as requiring a managed device or a second sign-in step, but the intranet itself does not need a VPN.
Q: Who should own a company intranet?
A: Give the intranet a business owner, usually from communications or HR, and name a content owner for each site. IT runs the platform and permissions, but it should not write every page. Intranets go stale when ownership sits only with IT. MP-365 sets these roles during design.
Q: Can you move content from an old intranet or shared drive?
A: Yes, after review. MP-365 sorts content into keep, rewrite, move and retire, then moves the approved items into the new sites. Old classic pages and custom code usually need rebuilding as modern pages. Moving everything unchanged only carries the old clutter into the new site.
Q: How does MP-365 keep an intranet from going stale?
A: MP-365 puts a named owner and a review reminder on each section, using Power Automate where it helps. Owners are trained to publish and update, and a short governance guide records the rules. Stale pages usually come from missing ownership, so the design fixes that first.

A SharePoint intranet works when it has clear structure, named owners and search that finds the right page. Build it on Microsoft 365 or buy software, but decide on purpose. If you want help, MP-365 designs and builds it with your team.

## Power BI Executive Dashboards for Leaders
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/executive-dashboards/

A Power BI executive dashboard puts live sales, service and operations numbers in front of leaders, so decisions stop waiting on a monthly spreadsheet. MP-365 builds these dashboards on Dynamics 365 and your other business systems, with one agreed definition for every number.

### The problem: leaders get the numbers after the moment has passed
In many companies the monthly report is a person with a stack of exports and a spreadsheet. By the time it reaches the leadership meeting, the data is stale, and two managers show two different revenue figures for the same period.
Leaders then argue about whose number is right instead of what to do. The fix is not a prettier chart. It is a single, trusted source that refreshes on its own and shows the same figure to everyone.

### Who feels it
- CEOs and general managers: you steer by gut feel because the numbers arrive late.
- Sales leaders: you cannot see pipeline, forecast and rep activity in one view.
- Service and operations leaders: you learn about backlogs and missed commitments after customers complain.
- Finance and analysts: you spend days each month compiling reports by hand.
- IT: you field report requests that never end, each one a custom export.

### What slow, manual reporting costs the business
Symptom | Business impact
Reports built by hand each month | Skilled people spend days compiling numbers instead of analyzing them.
Numbers differ between teams | Meetings go to reconciling figures, and trust in the data drops.
Data is out of date at review time | Leaders react to last month's problems, not today's.
Pipeline and forecast live in separate files | Forecast misses surface late, when there is little time to respond.
No view of service backlog | Customers wait, and leaders find out through escalations.

### What a Power BI executive dashboard should show
- Sales: pipeline by stage, forecast against target, win rate and the deals at risk.
- Service: open cases by age and urgency, response and resolution trends, and repeat issues.
- Operations: the handful of volume and throughput measures that tell you if work is flowing.
- Customers: growth, renewals and churn signals drawn from the CRM.
- Targets and trends: each number beside its goal and its direction, not just a total.
- One drill path: from a headline number to the records behind it, so questions get answered in the meeting.

### How MP-365 builds your Power BI executive dashboard
1. Ask leaders what decisions they make: Start from the questions each leader needs answered every week, not from the data that happens to exist.
2. Agree on a definition for each number: Write down what counts as a qualified lead, a closed deal or an open case, and who owns each definition.
3. Map the data sources: List where each number comes from, such as Dynamics 365, SharePoint lists and your other systems, and note gaps in quality.
4. Clean and connect the data: Fix duplicates and missing fields at the source where possible, then connect the sources to one Power BI data model.
5. Build a first dashboard on real data: Create a working page with a few headline measures so leaders react to something real, then refine it.
6. Set refresh and access rules: Schedule data refresh, and control who sees what, so each leader sees the right slice of the business.
7. Validate against the old reports: Compare the dashboard with the spreadsheet figures, resolve every difference and sign off the numbers with their owners.
8. Train users and hand off: Show leaders how to filter and drill down, and give your team a short guide for changes and new measures.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
A measure dictionary with named owners | Everyone uses the same definition for every number.
A Power BI data model on your sources | Sales, service and operations data sits in one place that updates on schedule.
Executive and team dashboards | Leaders see headline numbers and can drill into the detail.
Sales dashboard views in Power BI | Pipeline, forecast and activity are visible without exporting to a spreadsheet.
Access rules by role | Each person sees the data they should, and no more.
Data quality checks | Bad records get flagged before they distort a chart.
User guide and training | Your team can adjust and extend the dashboards.

### How to keep dashboard data accurate
Accurate dashboards start at the source. If sales reps enter deals inconsistently, no chart can fix it. MP-365 sets required fields and clear stages in Dynamics 365 first, then builds the dashboard on top, so the report reflects how the business actually works.
Each measure then gets an owner, a written definition and a reconciliation against the old report before launch. Quality checks flag duplicates and missing values after launch, so problems surface early and do not sit hidden in a total.

### Proof: from spreadsheets to live sales dashboards
One client tracked sales across scattered spreadsheets and compiled reports by hand every month. MP-365 set up one sales process and live dashboards for leadership, so the team stopped assembling reports and started using them. The client name is withheld.
Read more project summaries on the clients page.

### Scope, effort and cost
A dashboard project grows with the number of data sources, the state of the data and how many audiences need their own view. A single sales dashboard on clean CRM data is a smaller job than a company-wide view that joins several systems.
MP-365 scopes this after a short discovery call. The pricing page explains how engagements work, and Power BI license fees are set by Microsoft and are separate.

### When this is not the right fit
An executive dashboard is not the right fit if your underlying process is undefined, for example no agreed sales stages or case statuses. Fix the process and data entry first, or build them together. It is also not for teams that need real-time machine monitoring or a data warehouse project, which are outside what MP-365 delivers.

### Related services for manufacturers and others
The hands-on build sits under Power BI consulting and dashboards. When data comes from several systems, Dynamics 365 integration services connect them first. Operations leaders can see how this fits manufacturing companies. For other outcomes, browse all Microsoft solutions for mid-size companies.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What should an executive dashboard show?
A: An executive dashboard should show the few measures leaders use to decide, each beside its target and trend. Typical sets cover pipeline and forecast for sales, open cases and response times for service, and a few throughput measures for operations. Keep it to one screen and let people drill down for detail.
Q: How do you build a sales dashboard in Power BI?
A: Connect Power BI to your CRM, define each measure, and build a model for deals, stages and owners. Then add pages for pipeline, forecast and activity. The hard part is consistent data entry, so MP-365 sets required fields and stages in Dynamics 365 before building the report.
Q: How do you keep dashboard data accurate?
A: Fix data at the source, write one definition for each measure, and name an owner for it. Before launch, reconcile the dashboard against the old report and resolve every gap. After launch, run checks for duplicates and missing values so errors surface early instead of hiding inside totals.
Q: Can Power BI use Dynamics 365 data?
A: Yes. Power BI connects to Dynamics 365 and to many other sources, so one dashboard can combine CRM data with other systems. MP-365 builds the data model, sets refresh, and controls who sees which records. Quality of the dashboard still depends on how consistently the CRM is used.
Q: Do executives need Power BI licenses to view the dashboards?
A: It depends on how you share them. Microsoft sets licensing rules for Power BI, and they differ between viewing, creating and sharing in a workspace. MP-365 checks your current Microsoft 365 plan during discovery and tells you what viewers need, so there are no surprises later.
Q: How often does the dashboard refresh?
A: You choose the refresh schedule, and it depends on the data source and the need. Many leadership views refresh daily, while service views may refresh more often. MP-365 sets the schedule for each dataset during the build and documents it, so users know how current each number is.
Q: Can different leaders see different data?
A: Yes. Power BI supports row-level security, so a regional manager sees only their region while the CEO sees everything. MP-365 sets access by role and tests it with real accounts before launch. Clear rules matter because executives often share screenshots outside the meeting.
Q: Is this a replacement for our finance reporting?
A: No. An executive dashboard covers operational and commercial measures that leaders watch day to day. It does not replace your official financial statements or close process. It can show finance-related measures from approved sources, but the accounting records stay in the systems that own them.
Q: Can we change the dashboard ourselves after launch?
A: Yes. MP-365 documents the data model and measures and trains your team to adjust pages and add measures. Keep changes tied to the measure dictionary, so new numbers get a definition and an owner. MP-365 can return when you need larger changes or new data sources.

A Power BI executive dashboard earns its place when leaders open it before the weekly meeting and trust what they see. MP-365 gets you there by fixing definitions and data first, then building views your team can keep improving.

## CRM Implementation Services: Go Live in Weeks
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/crm-implementation/

CRM implementation services from MP-365 put Dynamics 365 Sales or Customer Service into daily use quickly, so your team stops living in spreadsheets and inboxes. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that starts with a working first version instead of a long design phase.

### What CRM implementation services include
CRM implementation is the work of turning a CRM license into a system your team uses every day. It covers setting up your process in the software, loading your existing customer data, connecting the tools around it, testing, training people and switching them over.
The software itself is rarely the hard part. Most of the effort goes into deciding how leads, accounts, cases and approvals should move, then building exactly that and nothing extra. A Dynamics 365 implementation follows the same path whether you start with sales, service or both.

### Three ways to run a Dynamics 365 implementation
Approach | Best for | Trade-off
Big-bang build from a full requirements document | Organizations with unusual processes and a long runway before users need the system. | Users see nothing until late, so misunderstandings surface after most of the work is done.
Template-based build with a working first version | Mid-size sales and service teams whose process looks like most other teams in their field. | Starts from proven patterns, so very unusual rules are added in later releases rather than on day one.
Do it yourself with the in-house IT team | Teams with a Dynamics 365 administrator who has time to spare. | Day-to-day work competes with the project, and the first release often slips.

### Why CRM projects take longer than planned
CRM projects slow down when the team tries to design everything before anyone touches the system. Requirements grow, each department adds a wish list, and the go-live date keeps moving.
The other common cause is the release process. When changes move to production by hand with no test cycle, each release is risky, so teams release rarely and in large batches.

### Who feels a slow CRM rollout
- Sales leaders: pipeline numbers come from spreadsheets assembled by hand, and forecasts lag the real deals.
- Service managers: cases live in shared inboxes with no clear owner, status or urgency.
- Sales and service reps: they enter the same details twice and stop trusting the system.
- IT leaders: they carry a half-finished project, a backlog with no order and releases nobody wants to run.
- Executives: they approve the budget and still ask for reports in a spreadsheet.

### What a delayed CRM costs the business
Symptom | Business impact
Go-live date keeps moving | Reps keep working in spreadsheets, so customer history stays scattered while you pay for licenses nobody uses.
Releases are manual and untested | Each change risks breaking sales or service screens, so improvements wait and bugs reach users.
No single lead or case process | Leads go unanswered and customer requests fall through, which costs revenue and goodwill.
Reports built by hand | Leaders wait on monthly numbers and make decisions on stale data.
Low user adoption | The CRM fills with partial records, so the data cannot support forecasts or service decisions.
