## Dynamics CRM Migration and Classic CRM Upgrade
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/dynamics-365-migration/

Dynamics 365 migration services move a classic Dynamics CRM from your own servers to Dynamics 365 online, and replace old workflows and plugins with modern automation along the way. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that treats zero data loss as the goal of every move.

### What a classic Dynamics CRM is and why it ages
A classic Dynamics CRM is an older, on-premises installation of Microsoft Dynamics CRM, running on servers your own team patches and backs up. Over the years it collects custom workflows, plugins written in code, old-style forms and reports that only one person understands.
The system still works, which is why it stays. The cost shows up elsewhere: upgrades are painful, outside tools are hard to connect, and every change depends on the few people who remember how it was built.

### Who feels the weight of an old CRM
- IT leaders: they keep servers and customizations alive, and each upgrade feels like a risk.
- Sales and service managers: screens are dated, mobile access is limited and small changes take a long time.
- Operations leaders: reports need manual exports, and data does not flow between the CRM and other systems.
- The one CRM expert: the person who built the customizations carries knowledge nobody else has.

### What staying on a classic CRM costs
Symptom | Business impact
Servers and databases managed in house | IT time goes to maintenance instead of improving how sales and service work.
Classic workflows nobody fully understands | A small change can break a process, so people avoid changing anything.
Plugins written in code | Fixes need a developer, and every upgrade needs the plugins re-tested.
Old forms and screens | Users work around the system, and new hires take longer to learn it.
Few ways to connect modern tools | Teams copy data by hand between the CRM and the tools they actually use.

### Your options for an on-premises Dynamics CRM
Option | What happens | Best for
Stay as it is | You keep the current system and manage servers yourself. | Systems close to retirement with few users and no plans for change.
Move to the cloud as it is | The database moves to Dynamics 365 online, and customizations are carried over without redesign. | Teams that want the cloud first and have simple customizations.
Migrate and modernize | Data moves to Dynamics 365 online while classic workflows, plugins and forms are replaced with current tools. | Teams that want the move to remove old technical debt, not carry it along.
Start fresh in a new tenant | You configure a new Dynamics 365 setup and import only the data you still need. | Teams whose process has changed so much that the old design no longer fits.

### How MP-365 migrates Dynamics CRM to Dynamics 365 online
1. Inventory what you run today: List entities, custom fields, classic workflows, plugins, reports, integrations and users. Mark each one to keep, replace or retire.
2. Choose the target and the order: Decide with you whether to move as is, modernize or rebuild, and which parts move first.
3. Prepare and clean the data: Remove duplicates and dead records worth leaving behind, and map every field from the old system to the new one.
4. Rebuild workflows in Power Automate: Replace classic workflows with Power Automate flows that your team can read, test and change without a developer.
5. Replace plugins with low-code automation: Move logic that lived in custom code into configuration and flows where possible, and keep code only where nothing else fits.
6. Upgrade old forms to modern custom pages: Redesign dated forms so users get cleaner screens, with fields arranged around the work they actually do.
7. Rehearse the move and compare the data: Run a trial migration into a test environment and compare record counts and sample records against the source until they match.
8. Cut over and support the first days: Switch users to Dynamics 365 online on an agreed date, keep the old system available for checks and fix issues as they appear.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
A written inventory of customizations and a migration plan | You see exactly what moves, what changes and what is retired before work starts.
Your data in Dynamics 365 online, checked against the source | Records arrive complete, and the old system stays a safe fallback during cutover.
Power Automate flows replacing classic workflows | Business rules become visible and editable by your own administrators.
Low-code replacements for plugins | Fewer fixes depend on a developer, and upgrades carry less risk.
Modern custom pages in place of old forms | Users get cleaner screens that match how they work.
Tested releases with release notes | Changes after the move reach production in a predictable way.

### Why Dynamics 365 migration services start with an inventory
The riskiest part of a Dynamics 365 upgrade is what nobody remembers. A workflow that fires on a hidden field, a plugin that updates a related record: these are the things that break quietly after cutover. MP-365 reads what is actually in the system before it plans the move.
That is why the plan is written from the inventory, not from a sales estimate. Effort follows what you find, and the Pricing page explains how MP-365 engagements work. When the move is done, DevOps & Release Automation keeps later changes tested and documented.

A migration is not the right fit if your CRM is close to retirement and few people use it, or if you plan to replace it with a different product entirely. It also does not suit teams that expect every old customization to be copied exactly. MP-365 will tell you which parts of a classic design are better left behind.

## Contract Management Automation on Microsoft 365
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/contract-management-automation/

Contract management automation moves contracts out of inboxes and shared folders into one process with defined stages, named owners and renewal reminders. MP-365 builds it on SharePoint and Power Automate, so legal and finance see every contract and what is due next.

### What contract management automation is
Contract management automation is a way of running contracts through a defined process, with software handling the routine steps. A request comes in, the contract moves through drafting, review, approval and signature, and then sits in a central place with its key dates and owner.
The software does the chasing: it routes approvals, sends reminders before a renewal date and updates a status that anyone can read. People still negotiate and decide. They just stop managing the process by email.

### The problem: contracts live everywhere and expire quietly
In many companies, contracts sit in email attachments, personal folders and shared drives. Nobody has a full list. Renewal dates live in one person's calendar, and approvals run on forwarded messages that nobody can trace afterward.
The result is predictable. A contract auto-renews on terms nobody reviewed, or lapses before anyone noticed. Finance cannot tell what is committed, and legal answers the same status questions again and again.

### Who feels it
- Legal and contract managers: you answer status questions all day and chase approvers by email.
- Finance: you cannot see upcoming commitments or confirm what was approved.
- Sales and account teams: you wait on approvals with no view of where the contract is stuck.
- Procurement and operations: you miss renewal windows with suppliers and partners.
- Executives: you sign off without a clear picture of obligations across the company.

### What unmanaged contracts cost the business
Symptom | Business impact
Missed renewal or notice dates | Contracts auto-renew on old terms, or lapse and interrupt service.
Approvals by email | Deals stall, and nobody can show who approved what.
Several versions of one contract | Teams work from the wrong draft, which creates disputes.
No central list of contracts | Finance and legal cannot report on obligations or spend.
Status questions answered by hand | Skilled staff spend time on updates instead of review.

### Options for contract management automation
Option | Where it fits | Watch for
Spreadsheet and shared folder | A small number of contracts and one person who manages them. | No reminders, no audit trail, and it breaks as volume grows.
Built on Microsoft 365 | You use Microsoft 365 and want contracts with your existing permissions and tools. | It needs a defined process and an owner, since it is built to your rules.
Dedicated contract software | Complex clause libraries, heavy e-signature use and a large legal team. | A separate license and system, and a second place for your content.

### Can SharePoint manage contracts?
Yes, for many companies. A SharePoint library can hold each contract with fields such as counterparty, type, owner, start date, end date and status. Version history keeps earlier drafts, and permissions limit who can see sensitive agreements.
On its own, SharePoint stores and organizes. Add Power Automate, and it also routes approvals, sends renewal reminders and updates status. That combination is what turns a folder into a contract management automation process.

### How MP-365 builds contract management automation
1. Map how contracts move today: Walk through a request, review, approval and signature with legal, finance and the business owners, and note where it stalls.
2. Define stages, owners and contract types: Agree on the stages every contract passes through, who owns each stage and which contract types need different handling.
3. Design the contract record: Choose the fields you need, such as counterparty, value, end date and notice period, and keep them to what people will actually fill in.
4. Build the library and permissions in SharePoint: Create the contract library with views by stage and owner, and set access so sensitive agreements stay restricted.
5. Automate requests and approvals: Build the request form and approval routing in Power Automate, so each contract moves forward without email chasing.
6. Set up renewal and notice reminders: Send alerts to the contract owner and backup before key dates, and escalate if nobody acts.
7. Load existing contracts: Bring current agreements into the library with their key dates, starting with those closest to renewal.
8. Add dashboards and train the team: Build a view for legal and finance of what is due and where contracts are stuck, then train owners and administrators.

### How renewal reminders work in Power Automate
A Power Automate flow reads the end date and notice period from each contract record. It runs on a schedule, finds contracts reaching a set number of days before the notice date, and sends a message to the owner. If nobody marks the contract as reviewed, it can alert a manager.
You choose the lead times, the recipients and the escalation rules. MP-365 tests the flows against real contracts before launch, so the first reminder is not the first time anyone sees it work.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
A defined contract process with stages and owners | Everyone knows who acts next and where each contract stands.
A SharePoint contract library with key fields | Contracts live in one searchable place with version history.
Request and approval flows in Power Automate | Approvals move on their own and leave a record.
Renewal and notice reminders | Owners hear about key dates before they pass.
Dashboards for legal and finance | Both teams see what is due, what is stuck and what is committed.
Role-based access | Sensitive agreements stay with the people who need them.
Owner training and a short guide | Your team runs the process and adjusts it as rules change.

### Proof: contracts with stages, owners and reminders
One MP-365 client managed contracts without a clear process. MP-365 set up defined stages, named owners, reminders and dashboards for legal and finance, so both teams could see the state of every contract. The client name is withheld.
Read more project summaries on the clients page.

### Scope, effort and cost
Effort depends on how many contract types you have, how many existing contracts to load, how many approval paths exist and whether other systems need links. A single contract type with one approval path is a smaller build than several types across regions.
MP-365 scopes this on a discovery call. The pricing page explains how engagements work, and Microsoft license fees are set by Microsoft and are separate.

### When this is not the right fit
This is not the right fit if you need a large clause library, redlining inside a dedicated legal tool or a full legal department platform. It is also not the right fit if you have no agreed contract process yet and nobody to own it. MP-365 does not provide legal advice or review contract wording.

### Related services for your industry
The automation behind this solution is covered in Power Automate workflow automation. The storage side sits under SharePoint and intranets. Teams in construction and engineering often manage subcontract and supplier agreements, and medical device companies manage supplier and distributor agreements. For other outcomes, browse all Microsoft solutions for mid-size companies.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is contract management automation?
A: Contract management automation runs contracts through a defined process using software for the routine steps. Requests, approvals, reminders and status updates happen automatically, and every contract sits in one place with an owner and key dates. People still negotiate and decide, but they stop managing the process by email.
Q: Can SharePoint manage contracts?
A: Yes. A SharePoint library can store contracts with fields for counterparty, owner, dates and status, keep version history and restrict access. Alone it stores and organizes. With Power Automate added, it also routes approvals and sends reminders. For clause libraries and redlining, dedicated software may suit better.
Q: How do renewal reminders work in Power Automate?
A: A flow reads each contract's end date and notice period on a schedule. When a contract reaches the lead time you set, it messages the owner. If nobody marks it reviewed, the flow can alert a manager. You choose the lead times, recipients and escalation steps.
Q: What is a contract governance process?
A: A contract governance process is the set of rules for how contracts are requested, reviewed, approved, stored and renewed. It defines stages, owners and who may sign what. Automation enforces those rules so they hold under pressure. Write the rules down first, because software cannot fix a process nobody agreed on.
Q: Do we need dedicated contract software or can Microsoft 365 do it?
A: Microsoft 365 handles many contract needs: storage, approvals, reminders and dashboards, using licenses you may already own. Dedicated software fits better when you need a large clause library, heavy redlining or a big legal team. Start by listing your real requirements, then compare them honestly.
Q: Can we automate approvals for sales contracts?
A: Yes. A request form can route a sales contract to the right approvers based on its type or value, and record each decision. Sales sees where the contract is stuck without asking legal. The rules for who approves what come from your business, and MP-365 helps you write them down first.
Q: Can you load our existing contracts into the new system?
A: Yes. MP-365 loads current agreements into the SharePoint library with their key dates and owners, starting with those closest to renewal. Documents without clear dates need a person to read them and fill in the fields. Plan time for that review, because it decides how reliable your reminders are.
Q: Who can see sensitive contracts?
A: Only the people you grant access to. MP-365 sets permissions by contract type and role, so a sales agreement and an executive employment contract can sit in the same system with different audiences. Access is reviewed with legal and finance during the build and can be adjusted later.
Q: Does this include e-signatures?
A: That depends on the signature tool you already use. MP-365 builds the process around signing, such as approvals before sending and storing the signed copy with its dates. It can connect to a signature service where one is available. Discuss your current tool on the discovery call.

Contract management automation works when the process is simple, every contract has an owner and nobody learns about a renewal after the date has passed. MP-365 builds it on SharePoint and Power Automate, using the Microsoft 365 tools your team already knows.

## M&A IT Integration and Separation on Microsoft 365
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/m-and-a-it-integration/

M&A IT integration brings two companies onto one Microsoft 365 environment after a merger or acquisition (M&A, mergers and acquisitions), and splits one apart when a business unit is sold. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that plans the email, files and Teams moves so people keep working on Day 1.

### What M&A IT integration means on Microsoft 365
M&A IT integration is the technical work of joining or separating two companies' systems when ownership changes. On Microsoft 365, that work centers on the tenant, which is each company's own Microsoft 365 environment holding its users, mailboxes, Teams and files.
When you buy a company, you usually combine tenants. When you sell a unit, you split one tenant in two, which people call a carve out. Either way, the same people who close the deal depend on email, calendars and documents working on the first morning.

### What Day 1 IT readiness means
Day 1 IT readiness means the people affected can sign in, send email and reach the files they need on the first day the deal takes effect. It is a short list of must-work items, agreed before closing, not a full integration.
Everything else, such as moving every mailbox and merging every site, happens afterward in planned waves. Separating Day 1 from the longer program keeps the deal from stalling while IT finishes the full job.

### Combine tenants or separate them
Deal type | What IT does | What can go wrong
Acquisition: bring a company in | Move users, mailboxes, Teams and files into the buyer's tenant, or run both side by side first. | Duplicate addresses, broken sharing links and staff who cannot find shared documents.
Merger: two equals | Choose which tenant becomes the main one, or plan a new one, then move both sides in waves. | Arguments over naming and permissions that delay the work.
Divestiture: sell a unit | Copy the unit's data out of the parent tenant into a new tenant and remove access it should no longer have. | Data that belongs to the buyer stays behind, or data that should stay is copied out.
Coexistence period | Keep both tenants live while users see each other in address books and calendars. | Calendar availability gaps and mail loops if the setup is not tested.

### Who feels it when integration goes wrong
- Deal and finance leaders: they need the new organization to work on schedule, or promised savings slip.
- IT leaders: they have a fixed date, two sets of administrators and little time to learn the other side's setup.
- Employees on both sides: they lose email, cannot find documents or see strange address books.
- Legal and compliance teams: they need to know who can see which data after the deal.

### What a rough integration costs the deal
Symptom | Business impact
Email or calendars break on Day 1 | Customers and employees miss messages, and the deal starts with a visible failure.
Two sets of files and Teams | Staff keep duplicates, and nobody trusts which version is current.
Permissions copied without review | People see data they should not, or lose access to data they need.
Separation left half done | Seller and buyer both hold data that belongs to the other, which creates legal risk.
IT team stretched across the deal | Regular work stalls while a few people handle the move.

### How MP-365 runs M&A IT integration and separation
1. Map both sides' Microsoft 365 setups: List users, domains, mailboxes, Teams, SharePoint sites, shared files and licenses on each side, and note who owns what.
2. Define Day 1 and the later waves: Agree on the must-work list for the first morning, then group everything else into planned moves with owners.
3. Design the target tenant: Decide naming, domains, groups and permissions in the surviving or new tenant before any user is moved.
4. Set up coexistence: Connect the tenants so users see each other in the address book and calendar while the moves run.
5. Pilot with a small group: Move a few mailboxes, a Team and a file library first. Check that mail flows, sharing links hold and users can sign in.
6. Move mailboxes, Teams and files in waves: Migrate groups on a schedule that avoids busy business periods, and compare results with the source after each wave.
7. Cut over domains and clean up access: Switch mail domains on the agreed date, then review permissions so each side keeps only the data it should.
8. Hand off with documentation: Give your administrators the final structure, the permission model and a list of what was moved or retired.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
An inventory of both tenants | Both sides see the same picture before a single user moves.
A Day 1 readiness checklist | Everyone knows what must work on the first day and who is responsible.
A coexistence setup between tenants | Staff see colleagues in both organizations while the moves continue.
Cross-tenant mailbox, Teams and file moves in waves | Work continues during the move, with checks after each wave.
A permission model for the final tenant | Each group sees the data it should, and sensitive areas stay limited.
Handoff notes for your administrators | Your team can run the result without MP-365.

Carlisle Construction asked MP-365 to steady its Dynamics and SharePoint operations. MP-365 stabilized them within a week, with no long discovery phase. That same fast, hands-on start suits a deal, where the calendar matters more than a thick planning document.

This service is not the right fit if your deal needs network, data center or phone system work, or if you only need advice on deal strategy. ### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What is M&A IT integration?
A: M&A IT integration is the technical work of joining two companies' systems after a merger or acquisition, or splitting them after a divestiture. On Microsoft 365, it covers tenants, mailboxes, Teams, files, domains and permissions, so employees keep working while ownership changes.
Q: How do you separate IT after a divestiture?
A: You build a new tenant for the unit being sold, copy its mailboxes, Teams and files out of the parent tenant, switch its domains, then remove access each side should no longer have. MP-365 plans the split in waves and checks the data after each one.
Q: What does Day 1 IT readiness mean?
A: Day 1 IT readiness means employees can sign in, send email and reach the documents they need on the first day the deal takes effect. MP-365 agrees a short must-work list with you before closing, and handles the larger moves in later waves.
Q: What is an IT carve out?
A: An IT carve out is the separation of one business unit's systems from its parent company so the unit can be sold or run alone. On Microsoft 365, that means moving the unit's users and data into their own tenant and cutting shared access.
Q: Can we integrate Office 365 and Microsoft 365 tenants after an acquisition?
A: Yes. Office 365 is now called Microsoft 365, and tenants on either name are combined the same way. MP-365 inventories both sides, sets up coexistence so staff see each other, then moves mailboxes, Teams and files into the surviving tenant in planned waves.
Q: Do both companies need to keep working during the move?
A: Yes. The plan is built so people keep using email, Teams and files while moves run. Coexistence keeps address books and calendars connected, and waves are scheduled around busy periods. Some users may see a short change at their own cutover, which is announced beforehand.
Q: When should IT planning start in a deal?
A: Start as soon as the deal is likely, and before closing if you can. Day 1 decisions, such as domains, sign-in and who needs access, take time to agree. Starting early lets MP-365 test the setup before real users depend on it.
Q: How much does M&A IT integration cost?
A: Cost depends on how many users, mailboxes, Teams and files move, and whether you are combining or separating. License fees go to Microsoft and are separate from MP-365 fees. The Pricing page describes how engagements are structured.

M&A IT integration works best when Day 1 is planned before closing and the rest is moved in tested waves. MP-365 maps both tenants, sets up coexistence and hands your administrators a clean result, whether you are combining companies or splitting one apart.

## CRM and Marketing Systems Integration
URL: https://mp-365.com/solutions/crm-systems-integration/

CRM and marketing automation integration connects Dynamics 365 to your marketing, service and third-party tools through secure APIs, so leads, orders and customer updates arrive without retyping or dropped records. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that builds integrations with logging and alerts, so problems show up before customers notice.

### When your systems do not talk to each other
A lead fills in a form on your website, lands in the marketing tool, and then waits for someone to copy it into the CRM. A customer emails support, and the service tool has no idea what sales promised last week. Each tool holds part of the story, and people fill the gaps by hand.
Integration removes the hand work. Data moves between systems automatically, in the right direction, with a record of what moved and what failed.

### Who feels disconnected systems
- Marketing managers: campaign leads reach sales late, with missing fields, and nobody can tell which campaign produced a won deal.
- Sales reps: they re-enter details or work from stale contact records.
- Service agents: they answer a customer without seeing open deals, past orders or earlier cases.
- Operations leaders: order and status updates reach the CRM late, so customer promises rest on guesses.
- IT leaders: they inherit scripts and personal logins that break without warning.

### What disconnected systems cost the business
Symptom | Business impact
Leads copied by hand into the CRM | Follow-up is slow, and leads get lost between tools.
Two records for the same customer | Marketing and sales contact the same person with different messages.
Failed syncs nobody notices | Records go missing for days, and trust in the data erodes.
Integrations running on a personal login | The connection stops when that person changes roles or changes a password.
No view of which campaign won the deal | Marketing budget is spent without evidence of what works.

### How CRM and marketing automation integration works
CRM and marketing automation integration moves data between Dynamics 365 and a marketing platform on rules you define. Forms, campaign responses and email activity flow into the CRM as leads and contacts, and lead status and ownership flow back out to marketing.
The same pattern applies to other tools. A service platform can read account and order details from the CRM. A SharePoint library can hold a customer's documents beside the CRM record. A third-party application can read or update CRM data through its API (application programming interface), the secure doorway the software offers for exactly this purpose.

### Ways to connect a CRM to other systems
Method | Best for | Watch out for
Built-in connectors | Common tools with a ready connector and simple one-way or two-way sync. | Limited control over rules, field mapping and error handling.
Power Automate flows | Event-based steps, such as sending a new lead to a team or updating a record after an approval. | Very large volumes or complex logic can need a more robust design.
Custom API integration | Tools without a connector, or rules that need exact control and monitoring. | Needs careful design, testing and someone to own it later.
Manual export and import | One-off loads and rare updates. | Slow and error-prone when done repeatedly.

### How MP-365 builds reliable integrations
1. List every system and the data that moves: Write down which tools hold customers, leads, orders and cases, and which direction each field should travel.
2. Pick one source of truth for each record: Decide which system owns each type of data, so two tools never fight over the same field.
3. Choose the connection method: Use a built-in connector or Power Automate flow where it fits, and a custom API integration where it does not.
4. Map fields and matching rules: Match records by agreed keys such as email or account number, and set rules for duplicates and missing values.
5. Use service accounts and secure storage: Run each connection on a dedicated service account, not a personal login, and store passwords and keys in secure storage.
6. Add logging and alerts: Record every run, and alert the right person when a record fails, so nothing is dropped silently.
7. Test with real records: Send sample leads, orders and cases through the connection and compare the results in both systems before going live.
8. Hand off with documentation: Document what connects to what, who owns it and how to restart a failed run.

### What you get from MP-365
What MP-365 builds | The result
Connections between Dynamics 365 and your marketing tools | Leads reach sales with their campaign details, and sales status flows back to marketing.
Links to customer service tools and SharePoint | Agents see customer context, and documents sit beside the CRM record.
Integrations with third-party applications through secure APIs | Data moves in the right direction without retyping.
Service accounts and secure credential storage | Connections keep running when people change roles.
Logging and alerts on every run | Failures are visible within the system, not discovered by customers.
Documentation and an owner for each connection | Your team knows how the flow works and who maintains it.

In client work, MP-365 has built integrations between the CRM and marketing systems that use logging and alerts, service accounts instead of personal accounts, and secure password storage. The result is connections that report their own failures instead of dropping records quietly.
Hunter Panels, a manufacturer, uses MP-365 for Dynamics CRM support that cuts manual work and aligns the platform with the business.

### Who this is not the right fit for
This service is not the right fit if you want to replace every tool you own, or if the systems involved have no way to connect, such as software with no export or API. MP-365 connects Dynamics 365 to other tools. It does not build new software products from scratch.

### Related services and industries
Start with Dynamics 365 Integration Services for the service view of this work. Marketing activity runs in Dynamics 365 Customer Insights, the product formerly called Dynamics 365 Marketing. Event-based steps come from Power Automate Workflow Automation.
Teams in Logistics & Supply Chain often connect order and shipment updates to the CRM, and Retail teams connect customer and campaign data. For the full list of outcomes, see Solutions. Effort depends on how many systems are involved, as the Pricing page explains.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: How do you connect a CRM to marketing automation?
A: You map which data moves in each direction, then connect the two systems through a built-in connector, a Power Automate flow or a custom API integration. Forms and campaign responses flow into Dynamics 365 as leads, and lead status flows back to marketing, with logging on every run.
Q: How do you sync a CRM with other business systems?
A: Name one system as the owner of each type of record, match records by an agreed key such as email or account number, and run the sync on a dedicated service account. MP-365 tests with real records and adds alerts so failures are visible.
Q: How do you avoid dropped records in an integration?
A: Log every run, alert a named person when a record fails, and make sure failed records can be retried. MP-365 also tests with real sample data and uses matching rules for duplicates, so records are not lost or doubled when two systems disagree.
Q: What is the difference between a connector and an API integration?
A: A connector is a prebuilt link to a known product, set up with configuration. An API integration is custom logic written against a product's programming interface. Connectors are quicker for common cases, while API work gives exact control when no connector exists or rules are complex.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 connect to our existing marketing platform?
A: Usually yes. If the platform offers a connector or an API, MP-365 can link it to Dynamics 365. During discovery, MP-365 checks what the platform exposes, which fields need to move and whether the sync should run one way or both ways.
Q: Why use a service account instead of a personal login?
A: A personal login stops working when that person leaves, changes roles or resets a password, and it ties data changes to one name. A service account belongs to the integration itself. MP-365 uses service accounts and secure password storage for every connection.
Q: Can we integrate SharePoint with our CRM?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 can link customer records to SharePoint document libraries, so contracts, proposals and files sit beside the account or case. MP-365 sets up the structure and permissions so people see only the documents that belong to their records.
Q: How much does a CRM integration cost?
A: Cost depends on how many systems connect, how much data moves, how often, and whether a connector exists. License fees for the tools involved are separate from MP-365 fees. The Pricing page explains how MP-365 engagements work.

CRM and marketing automation integration pays off when records arrive complete and failures are visible. MP-365 connects Dynamics 365 to your marketing, service and third-party tools through secure APIs, with logging and alerts that show you what moved and what did not.

## CRM for Manufacturing on Dynamics 365
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/manufacturing/

A CRM for manufacturing should track RFQs, quotes and distributor accounts in one place, connect to your other systems, and be simple enough for sales to use every day. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that sets up Dynamics 365 for mid-size manufacturers that have outgrown spreadsheets and inbox-based quoting.

### What to look for in a CRM for manufacturing
- Quote and RFQ tracking: every request for quote should become a record with an owner, a due date, line items and revisions, so nothing sits unanswered.
- Account structure that matches how you sell: direct customers, distributors, dealers and the end users behind them need separate but linked records.
- Long, multi-step deals: a custom job or a spec-driven order moves through engineering, pricing and approval, and the CRM stages should reflect that.
- Connections to your other systems: quotes, orders and shipping status should flow in without retyping, so sales sees one version of the facts.
- Reporting leaders trust: pipeline, win rate by product line and quote turnaround should come from live data, not a monthly spreadsheet.
- Low effort for the sales team: if logging a call takes more than a minute, people stop doing it and the data decays.

### Common challenges in manufacturing sales and service
- RFQs get lost or answered late: requests come in through email, portals and phone calls, and a slow quote often loses the order.
- Distributor and dealer data is thin: you know what the distributor ordered, but not who the end customer is or what the pipeline looks like.
- Systems do not talk to each other: sales checks one tool for quotes, another for order status, and a spreadsheet for everything else.
- Reporting takes days: leaders wait on analysts to compile the pipeline instead of opening a dashboard.

MP-365 configures the stages to match your own process. A made-to-order manufacturer might add an engineering review. A distributor-led manufacturer might add a channel approval. Reminders and approvals can run through Power Automate, so late quotes surface before the customer asks.

## CRM for Logistics and Supply Chain Companies
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/logistics-supply-chain/

A CRM for logistics should keep shipper accounts, lanes, rate quotes and service issues in one record, so sales and operations work from the same facts. MP-365 sets up Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 for freight brokers, carriers and supply chain companies that run on email, spreadsheets and memory.

### What to look for in a CRM for logistics companies
A logistics CRM must match how freight is sold, not how software is usually sold. A shipper rarely buys once. They send quote requests for specific lanes, compare you with other carriers or brokers, and expect fast answers when something goes wrong. A good CRM records that whole relationship.
Before you pick a tool, check that it handles the points below. Most generic CRMs cover the first and last. Few handle the middle well without setup.

### Features that matter in a logistics CRM
- Shipper and carrier accounts: one place for the customer, their locations, contacts and the carriers or partners you use for them.
- Lane and rate history: the routes, volumes and quoted rates for each shipper, so a rep sees what was offered last time.
- Quote tracking: every request has an owner, a status and an outcome, including why a quote was lost.
- Service cases: a missed delivery or claim becomes a case with an owner, a cause and a due date.
- Connections to your other systems: load, tracking and billing data should reach the account record without retyping.
- Mobile access: reps and operations staff are often away from a desk, so the CRM must work on a phone.

### How freight brokers use a CRM
A freight broker uses a CRM to manage two sides of the business: the shippers who need freight moved and the carriers who move it. For the shipper side, the CRM tracks prospects, quote requests, lanes and win or loss reasons. For the carrier side, it tracks capacity, contacts and past performance.
A broker CRM is not a transportation management system. It does not dispatch loads or settle payments. It supplies the relationship and sales view that those systems lack, which is why connecting the two matters.

### Common challenges in logistics and supply chain
- Quotes are answered from memory: a rep quotes a lane without seeing what the same shipper paid last month.
- Service issues have no owner: problems pass between sales, dispatch and billing with no single record.
- Teams are scattered: dispatchers, account managers and drivers work across offices and vehicles, so information stays in individual inboxes.
- Data lives in separate tools: load status, billing and customer history sit in different places.

### How MP-365 supports logistics teams
Challenge | What MP-365 sets up | Where to read more
Quotes are answered from memory | Quote and opportunity tracking by shipper and lane, with history and loss reasons. | Dynamics 365 Sales
Service issues have no owner | Alerts, routing and approvals that notify the right person when a case opens or a quote waits too long. | Power Automate Workflow Automation
Teams are scattered | Shared Teams channels and SharePoint libraries for each major account, with permissions that match each role. | Modern Company Intranet
Data lives in separate tools | Connections that bring load, billing and marketing data into the CRM record, with logging and alerts. | CRM & Systems Integration

### How Microsoft 365 helps logistics teams collaborate
Microsoft 365 gives logistics teams shared spaces around each account. Teams carries the conversation, SharePoint stores rate sheets, contracts and proof of delivery, and the CRM record links to both. A dispatcher in one office sees what the account manager in another office promised.
Permissions matter here. MP-365 sets access so a carrier contact list or a customer's rate sheet is visible only to the people who need it. Power Automate can then post alerts into a Teams channel when a high-value quote is waiting.

### Proof: case tracking from a similar project
MP-365 replaced email-based support at another organization with one case system that shows each issue's owner, status and urgency. The client and industry are withheld, and the project was not in logistics. The same pattern applies to a missed pickup or a damaged load.

Q: What should a logistics company look for in a CRM?
A: A logistics company should look for shipper and carrier accounts, lane and rate history, quote tracking with loss reasons, service cases, and connections to load and billing data. Phone access also matters, because reps and dispatchers often work away from a desk. Ease of use decides whether staff keep records current.
Q: How do freight brokers use a CRM?
A: Freight brokers use a CRM to track shippers, quote requests, lanes and win or loss reasons, and to keep carrier contacts and capacity notes. It supplies the relationship view that a transportation system lacks. It does not dispatch loads or settle payments, so it works alongside those tools.
Q: How can Microsoft 365 help logistics teams collaborate?
A: Microsoft 365 gives each account a Teams channel for conversation and a SharePoint library for rate sheets, contracts and delivery documents. Linked to the CRM record, they let dispatch and account managers see the same facts. MP-365 sets permissions so each role sees only what it needs.
Q: Can a CRM track lanes and rates for each shipper?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 can store lanes, volumes and quoted rates as records linked to the shipper's account. A rep preparing a new quote then sees what was offered before. MP-365 sets up the fields and views to match the way your team names lanes.
Q: Does a logistics CRM replace a transportation management system?
A: No. A CRM manages customer relationships, quotes and service cases. A transportation management system plans and dispatches freight. Most logistics firms need both, connected so load status appears on the account. MP-365 builds the CRM side and the connection, not the dispatch system.
Q: Can we manage service claims and missed deliveries in Dynamics 365?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 Customer Service turns each claim or missed delivery into a case with an owner, status, priority and due date. Power Automate can alert the account manager when a case ages. This replaces the shared inbox where issues are easy to lose.
Q: Is a CRM worth it for a small freight brokerage?
A: It depends on volume. A broker with a few shippers can run on a shared mailbox and a spreadsheet. A CRM pays off when several reps share accounts, when staff turnover would cost relationships, or when leaders need quote and win-rate reporting.
Q: How does MP-365 approach a logistics CRM project?

A CRM for logistics works when quote requests, lanes and service issues are recorded once and visible to everyone who needs them. MP-365 builds that on Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365, connected to the systems you already run.

## CRM for Utilities and Energy Companies
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/energy-utilities/

A CRM for utilities keeps each customer account, service request and contact conversation in one record, so staff stop searching several systems for the full story. It does not replace your billing system. MP-365 builds it on Dynamics 365, with SharePoint for the documents that sit behind each account.

### What a CRM does for a utility
A CRM gives a utility one record for each customer relationship. That record shows the account, the service address, past requests, planned work, key contacts and the conversations around them. Staff stop asking customers to repeat themselves and managers can see where requests stall.
The goal is a better view of the customer, not a new place to enter every number. Rates, meter reads and invoices stay where they are. The CRM connects to them so staff can see the customer's whole situation from one screen.

### What to look for in a CRM for utilities and energy
- Account and site structure: a customer may have several service locations, contacts and contracts, and the record should show how they relate.
- Service request tracking: every call, email or crew report becomes a case with an owner, a status and a target date.
- Large and commercial accounts: key accounts need account managers, planned work and contract dates, not just a case queue.
- Links to documents: contracts, permits and inspection notes should open from the account instead of a separate folder search.
- Role-based access: field crews, call center staff and executives should each see only what their role requires.
- Reporting: request volume, age and resolution patterns should come from live data.

### How energy companies manage customer accounts in a CRM
Energy companies manage accounts in a CRM by treating the customer as a parent record with linked sites, contacts, contracts and cases. A commercial customer with five locations has one account and five linked sites. A residential service request attaches to one address and one contact.
In Dynamics 365, MP-365 sets up these relationships, adds the fields your team uses, and builds views for account managers, service staff and supervisors. The account record also links to its SharePoint folder, so a contract or permit opens in one click.

### How a CRM differs from a billing system
Question | CRM | Billing system

Typical records | Accounts, contacts, cases, notes and planned work | Meter data, tariffs, bills and payments
Typical users | Service staff, account managers and supervisors | Billing, finance and collections staff
Who changes it | Business teams, with admin help | Specialist staff, under strict controls
How they relate | Shows billing information on the customer record through a connection | Remains the source for charges and balances

### Common challenges for utility and energy teams
- No single customer view: service, account management and billing each hold a different piece of the story.
- Service requests have no clear owner: requests pass between the call center, dispatch and field crews without a shared record.
- Documents are hard to find: contracts, easement records and inspection notes live in nested folders.
- Reports take too long to build: leaders want a trend, and the data sits in several exports.

MP-365 also does not promise compliance with any regulation or provide security operations. It does set up permission models, access audits and document control, so the right people see the right records. For wider context, see Microsoft solutions by industry.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What does a CRM do for a utility?
A: A CRM gives a utility one record per customer, showing accounts, service locations, contacts, requests and conversations. Staff answer questions faster and supervisors see where requests stall. Rates and invoices stay in the billing system, which the CRM connects to for reference.
Q: How do energy companies manage customer accounts in a CRM?
A: Energy companies treat the customer as a parent account with linked sites, contacts, contracts and cases. A commercial customer with several locations keeps one account and many sites. MP-365 builds these relationships in Dynamics 365 and links each account to its SharePoint folder.
Q: How is a utility CRM different from a billing system?
A: A CRM manages relationships, requests and conversations, while a billing system calculates usage, applies rates and issues invoices. The two serve different users and follow different change controls. MP-365 connects them so service staff can see billing facts without editing them.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 track service requests from phone, email and crews?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 Customer Service can turn requests from several channels into cases with an owner, priority and due date. Field crew reports can enter through a form or a Power Automate flow. Supervisors then see one queue instead of separate inboxes.
Q: Does a utility need a CRM if it already has a billing system?
A: Usually yes, if staff cannot see customer history in one place. A billing system records charges, not conversations or service work. A CRM adds that missing view. Smaller utilities with simple needs may manage with the billing tools they have.
Q: How can SharePoint help with contracts and field documents?
A: SharePoint can hold contracts, permits and inspection notes in libraries with metadata, version control and permissions. Linked to the account record, a document opens in one click. MP-365 can also move existing shared-drive folders into SharePoint Online in an organized structure.
Q: Does MP-365 promise regulatory compliance for utilities?
A: No. MP-365 does not provide compliance certification or security operations. It builds permission models, audits who has access to Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 content, and sets up document control. Your own compliance team decides whether those controls meet the rules you must follow.
Q: Can executives see request trends without waiting for an analyst?
A: Yes. Power BI can read case data from Dynamics 365 and show volume, age and resolution on a live dashboard. Executives open it themselves instead of requesting a spreadsheet. MP-365 builds the dashboard around the measures your leaders already use.

A CRM for utilities pays off when staff can see one clear record for every customer, request and document, while billing stays in its own system. MP-365 builds that on Dynamics 365 and SharePoint, with permissions that match each role.

## CRM for Construction and Engineering Firms
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/construction-engineering/

A CRM for construction industry firms should track bids, clients, subcontractors and active projects in one place, and connect to the project documents your team already works from. MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that builds this on Dynamics 365 and SharePoint for construction and engineering companies.

### What to look for in a CRM for construction industry firms
- Bid and opportunity tracking: each bid has a due date, an estimator, a status and a result, and you can see every open bid in one view.
- Relationships beyond the client: owners, general contractors, architects, engineers and subcontractors all appear as linked contacts on the same job.
- A path from won bid to project: the record carries over to the project instead of being retyped.
- Project documents you can reach: drawings, contracts and RFIs open from the CRM record, with version control and permissions that match the project team.
- Connection to your other systems: estimating tools, scheduling and accounting data can feed the CRM so staff do not enter it twice.
- Easy use from the field: project managers and superintendents can read and update records from a phone or tablet.
- Reports leadership trusts: backlog, bid volume and win rate come from live data, not a monthly spreadsheet.

### Common challenges in construction and engineering firms
- Bid pipeline hidden in personal files: estimators keep their own lists, so leadership cannot forecast work or see which bids need attention.
- Subcontractor and client history is lost: who bid, who performed and who to invite next time lives in people's heads.
- Project documents sprawl: drawings and specs exist in several places, and teams build from an old revision.
- Closeout hand-offs break: sales, preconstruction and project teams each keep a separate record of the same job.
- Reporting costs days: backlog and win-rate numbers need manual assembly every month.

## Dynamics 365 for Credit Unions and Finance
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/financial-services/

MP-365 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner that builds this on Dynamics 365 and SharePoint for credit unions and other financial services teams.

### What to look for in a credit union CRM
A credit union CRM is measured by how well it supports member relationships, not how many sales features it has. The right system helps staff answer a member once, with full context, instead of asking the member to repeat their story.
Compare any option on a short list: a single member record, service and sales in one place, controlled access to sensitive notes, and a way to connect to your core banking system.

### Features a credit union should check before choosing a CRM
- One member record: accounts, household relationships, recent contacts and open cases appear on a single screen.
- Role-based access: tellers, lenders, advisors and managers each see only what their job requires, and changes to access are recorded.
- Service and sales together: a member service request can lead to a loan or product conversation without switching tools.
- Workflow for loans and requests: applications, document requests and approvals move through defined steps with owners.
- Connection to core banking: data from your core banking systems appears in the CRM through a controlled integration, not manual copy.
- Reporting for leadership: member service volume, referral sources and product interest come from live data.
- Document control: forms, disclosures and member files are stored with version history and the right permissions.

## CRM for Medical Device Companies
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/medical-devices/

A medical device CRM should track hospital accounts, distributors, contracts and rep activity in one place, with permissions that match who may see what. MP-365 builds this on Dynamics 365 Sales and SharePoint for medical device companies that have outgrown spreadsheets and shared inboxes.

### What to look for in a medical device CRM
- Account hierarchies: a hospital system, its facilities and its departments should sit in one structure, so a rep sees the whole buying group.
- Contacts by role: clinicians, materials management, procurement and value analysis committees each need to be recorded with their part in the decision.
- Distributor and direct channels: the CRM should show which accounts you serve directly and which a distributor covers.
- Contract tracking: every agreement needs a stage, an owner, key dates and a link to the signed document.
- Territory-based access: a rep should see their own accounts, a manager their region, and finance only what it needs.
- Quick updates for reps: if a visit note takes longer than a minute, it will not get written.
- Clean, shared account data: duplicates and inconsistent names undo every report built on top.

### How a CRM supports medical device sales
A CRM supports medical device sales by giving each rep one view of their hospital accounts, open opportunities and next steps. Managers forecast from live pipeline data instead of a spreadsheet that someone rebuilds every reporting period.
Device sales cycles often involve several buyers and long evaluation stages, so the record of who said what matters. When a rep changes territory, the history stays with the account instead of leaving with the person.

### Common challenges for medical device companies
- Contracts live in email and folders: renewal dates are tracked by memory, and legal asks sales for documents that finance also needs.
- Pipeline visibility depends on reps: updates arrive in meetings, not in the system, so forecasts lag behind the real situation.
- Duplicate hospital and distributor records: one health system appears under several spellings, which breaks territory reports and mailing lists.
- Access is too broad or too narrow: either everyone sees every price list, or reps cannot see the accounts they need.
- Reports built by hand: leadership packs come from exports and manual copying.

## CRM for Retail on Dynamics 365
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/retail/

A retail CRM should give you one view of each shopper across stores and online, connect to your point of sale and ecommerce platform, and report across every location. MP-365 builds retail customer service, reporting and system connections on Dynamics 365 and Power BI.

### What a retailer should look for in a retail CRM
A retail CRM earns its place when store staff, the service team and marketing all work from the same shopper record. Search results for this topic are mostly software lists, so start with your own needs before you compare products.
Retail also has a rhythm that other industries lack: seasonal peaks, high transaction counts and staff who rotate often. A CRM that needs long training or slows down a till queue will not be used.

### Checks before you choose retail CRM software
- One shopper record: purchases from stores, ecommerce and phone orders should resolve to the same person.
- Point of sale and ecommerce connections: transactions should reach the customer record without retyping.
- Returns and complaint handling: each case needs an owner, a status and a link to the order.
- Loyalty and segments: the CRM should hold member status and let marketing build groups, such as lapsed shoppers.
- Multi-store reporting: leaders should compare stores, regions and product groups from one source.
- Store-level access: a store manager should see their location, while head office sees all of them.
- Simple for store staff: the screens a floor employee uses should take seconds, not minutes.

### Common challenges for retailers
- Shoppers contact you in many places: store, email, phone, chat and social channels create separate threads.
- Reporting is manual: weekly sales and returns packs are built from exports from the point of sale.
- Systems do not talk: the point of sale, ecommerce platform and marketing tools each hold a different version of the shopper.
- Seasonal peaks overload service: returns and questions spike, and staff track them on shared inboxes.
- Duplicate customer records: the same shopper appears several times with different spellings and addresses.

Reporting is manual | Builds live dashboards across stores, regions and product groups to replace weekly spreadsheets. | Power BI Consulting & Dashboards
Systems do not talk | Connects the CRM to your point of sale, ecommerce platform and marketing tools, with logging and alerts when a connection fails. | CRM & Systems Integration
Seasonal peaks overload service | Adds routing, queues and templates so cases reach the right person during busy periods. | Power Automate

### When this is not the right fit
MP-365 is not the right fit if you want a packaged point of sale, a store design or a new ecommerce site, because it does none of these. It connects the CRM to the systems you already run.
MP-365 also does not resell Microsoft licenses or run help desk support for your stores. If you need a ready-made loyalty engine, buy one and let MP-365 connect it to the shopper record.

### Related services for retail teams
Retail teams that run campaigns often start with Customer Insights and shopper segments. For the wider picture, see all industries MP-365 serves.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What should a retailer look for in a CRM?
A: Look for one shopper record across stores and online, a way to log returns and complaints, and reporting that covers every location. The CRM should connect to your point of sale and ecommerce platform so data is not retyped. Check that store staff can use it quickly.
Q: How can Power BI help retail reporting?
A: Power BI combines sales, returns and customer data from several sources into live dashboards, so you compare stores, product groups and periods without spreadsheets. Managers open one report instead of requesting exports. MP-365 builds these through its Power BI consulting.
Q: How do retailers use Dynamics 365?
A: Retailers use Dynamics 365 Customer Service to handle shopper questions, returns and complaints, and Customer Insights to manage campaigns and segments. Dynamics 365 Sales supports wholesale and business accounts. The apps share the customer record, so every team sees the same history.
Q: Does a retail CRM replace our point of sale system?
A: No. The point of sale records transactions at the till, while the CRM records the relationship around them, such as service cases, preferences and campaigns. MP-365 connects the two so purchase data reaches the shopper record without double entry.
Q: Can Dynamics 365 support a loyalty program?
A: Partly. Dynamics 365 can hold member records, segments and campaign journeys, and Customer Insights - Journeys can send targeted messages. If your points engine lives in another platform, MP-365 connects it to the shopper record rather than replacing it.
Q: How should a CRM handle returns and complaints?
A: Log each return or complaint as a case with an owner, status and urgency, linked to the shopper and the order. Store staff and the service team then see the same history. Dynamics 365 Customer Service supports queues, routing and status tracking for this work.
Q: Can store managers see only their own store's data?
A: Yes. Dynamics 365 security roles and business units can limit each manager to one store or region, while head office sees all locations. MP-365 documents these access levels so later changes are easy to review.
Q: Should we buy retail CRM software or build on Dynamics 365?
A: Buy a packaged product if your needs are standard and you want little configuration. Build on Dynamics 365 if you already use Microsoft 365, need to connect several systems, or want multi-store reports in Power BI. MP-365 builds on Dynamics 365 and does not resell licenses.

A retail CRM should make life easier for store staff and give head office a trusted view of every shopper and every location. MP-365 builds that on Dynamics 365 and Power BI, connected to the point of sale and online systems you already use.

## Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 for Healthcare
URL: https://mp-365.com/industries/healthcare/

In Dynamics 365 healthcare work, organizations use the CRM for the administrative side of the business, such as service requests, referral sources and provider relations. MP-365 pairs it with Microsoft 365 for document control and permission models, and does not touch clinical records.

### Dynamics 365 healthcare use cases for administrative teams
Healthcare organizations use Dynamics 365 to manage the relationships and requests around care, not the care record itself. Typical uses include service request tracking, referral management, provider relations, community partner outreach and constituent inquiries.
MP-365 scopes work to this administrative side. It does not build electronic health record, clinical or validated systems, and your clinical record stays in the system built for it.

### What a healthcare provider should look for in a CRM
- Request tracking: every inquiry needs an owner, a category, a status and a due date.
- Referral and provider records: the CRM should show referral sources, provider contacts and the history of each relationship.
- Clear permission controls: access should follow job role, and someone should be able to report who can see what.
- Defined data scope: decide in advance what the CRM will hold, and keep clinical details out of it.
- Reporting leaders trust: queue size, overdue items and referral trends should come from the same data.
- Connection to documents: policies, forms and agreements should link to the record from SharePoint.
- Healthcare CRM software that staff use: busy teams will not tolerate a tool that adds steps.

### Common challenges for healthcare organizations
- Requests lack owners: email threads hide who is handling what and what is overdue.
- Provider and referral data is scattered: liaison teams keep their own lists, and reports disagree.
- Document control is weak: policies and forms live on shared drives with unclear versions and wide access.
- Permissions drift: access granted for one project is never removed.
- Teams work in separate tools: scheduling, requests and files do not connect.

### How MP-365 helps with each challenge
Challenge | What MP-365 does | Where to read more
Requests lack owners | Sets up cases, queues, categories and status tracking in one system. | Dynamics 365 Customer Service
Provider and referral data is scattered | Builds one set of provider and referral records with a documented process for updating them. | Dynamics 365 Sales
Document control is weak | Designs SharePoint libraries, metadata, version control and search so staff find the current version. | SharePoint Search & Information Architecture
Permissions drift | Documents access levels, reviews who has what and sets up reports for later checks. | Microsoft Purview & Permission Models
Teams work in separate tools | Uses Power Automate to move approvals and notifications between systems. | Power Automate

### Microsoft 365 for healthcare organizations and SharePoint document control
SharePoint for healthcare gives teams a controlled home for policies, procedures, forms and agreements. Libraries keep version history, metadata and approval steps, and owners decide who may read or edit.
Microsoft 365 for healthcare organizations also includes Teams for communication and Power Automate for routing approvals. MP-365 designs the structure and permissions. Your compliance staff decide whether the result meets your own rules.
